# Getting started

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/getting-started.html
Source file: README.md

## Features

**Editing**
- Blocks: text, headings, lists, checklists, toggles, callouts, code, tables, images, files,
  link cards, sandboxed embeds and columns, from a categorised insert menu.
- Spreadsheet block and linked charts, as above.
- Databases: typed fields with table, board, calendar, gallery, Timeline and Workload views;
  filter, sort, CSV import and export; formulas, relations and rollups.
- Whiteboards and diagrams: shapes, sticky notes, pen, attached arrows, shape libraries,
  connector routing, layout, and draw.io and Excalidraw import ([diagram guide](docs/29-DIAGRAMMING.md)).
- 40 templates in 9 categories. Autosave only, on desktop and phone.

**Collaboration**
- Edits merge in real time with a CRDT (Yjs), with cursors, presence, follow mode and comments.
- View, comment and edit roles enforced on the server; role changes apply live
  ([collaboration](docs/06-COLLABORATION-AND-PRESENCE.md)).

**Platform**
- Headless API (`/api/v1`) with TypeScript (`@opencanvas/client`) and Rust (`opencanvas-client`)
  clients, and signed webhooks ([integration guide §7](docs/05-INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md)).
- [Block SDK](docs/33-BLOCK-SDK.md): write your own sandboxed blocks.
- Editor profiles: each host picks notebook, meeting, project, diagramming, document or the
  full workspace.
- Live blocks shown and edited in several canvases; find and replace, and search across canvases
  through the host's search; automation rules; offline editing. All four are off until the host
  turns them on ([release notes 0.3.0](docs/35-RELEASE-v0.3.0.md)).
- [Version history](docs/30-VERSION-HISTORY.md): named versions, comparison and restore;
  availability depends on the host and permissions.
- Assistant and MCP endpoint: **experimental, off by default**, run only in the server with a
  model the operator configures on the Claude Platform or an OpenAI-compatible server (OpenAI,
  vLLM, Ollama, llama.cpp) ([AI and MCP](docs/24-AI-AND-MCP.md)).

**Integrations**
- [Jitsi Meet](integrations/jitsi/README.md), [Nextcloud](integrations/nextcloud/README.md),
  [Mattermost](integrations/mattermost/README.md) and [Element / Matrix](integrations/matrix/README.md).
  Host integrations for WOPI files, channel canvases and room widgets.
- Any WOPI host, or the `<open-canvas>` web component and signed launch tokens for your own app.

**Storage and scale**
- One container with SQLite to start; MySQL, MariaDB and Redis when you need a cluster.
- SQLite by default. MySQL 8.4 and MariaDB 11.4 work when `DATABASE_URL=mysql://…` is set;
  `REDIS_URL` turns on cluster mode. Docker image and Helm chart ([operations](docs/13-OPERATIONS-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md),
  [capacity and sizing](docs/22-CAPACITY-AND-SIZING.md)).

## Benchmarks

Every number comes from a result file with its hardware and load mix
([benchmarks page](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/benchmarks.html),
[capacity and sizing](docs/22-CAPACITY-AND-SIZING.md)). The runs below are short runs on one
developer laptop (Apple M4, 10 cores, 16 GB, SQLite), not the 4 vCPU / 8 GB reference machine, so
rerun them on your hardware (`scripts/bench/run`) before you size production.

| Run | Load mix | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 10,000 connections on one node ([result](bench/results/2026-11-26-x10k-short-local-perf11.json)) | 500 rooms; 75% idle viewers, 15% moving cursors at 2/s, 10% typing at 1 edit/s; `kill -9` and restart at 2 min | p99 edit latency at most 64.2 ms in every bucket outside the 60 s after the restart; 3,210 MB RSS; all 10,000 clients back within 37.1 s |
| 1,000 people in one room ([result](bench/results/2026-11-26-r1k-short-local-cap1000.json)) | cap raised to 1,000; 90% moving cursors at 5/s, 10% typing at 2 edits/s | p99 at most 80.6 ms, no drops; **memory still grew during the run, so the default cap stays 550** |
| 100,000-row database in the browser ([result](e2e/perf/results/db100k-local-m4-incremental.json)) | one tab, 100,000 rows × 30 fields, scrolling with a cell edit every 500 ms | frame time p95 16.7 ms (60 fps) in table and board views, no long tasks |

## Run it

With Docker, using a hosts file written from the [integration guide](docs/05-INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md):

```sh
docker run -p 8080:8080 -v oc-data:/data \
  -v "$PWD/hosts.toml:/etc/opencanvas/hosts.toml:ro" \
  -e OC_PUBLIC_URL=https://canvas.example.com \
  -e OC_KEK=$(openssl rand -base64 32) \
  ghcr.io/casualoffice/opencanvas:0.4.3
```

From source, with the sample host (Rust stable, Node 24 and pnpm 9):

```sh
cd web && pnpm install && pnpm --filter @opencanvas/editor build && cd ..
OC_DEV=1 cargo run --release -p oc-server     # http://localhost:8080
node examples/sample-host/server.mjs          # http://localhost:4000
```

Open http://localhost:4000 and open a file; in a second tab pick another user under "Signed in
as" to see live collaboration. `docker compose up --build` runs both services. `OC_DEV=1` allows
starting without `OC_KEK`; in production set `OC_KEK` (32 bytes, base64) and the variables in
[operations](docs/13-OPERATIONS-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md). For the UI alone, run
`pnpm --filter @opencanvas/editor dev` and open `http://localhost:5173/app/#demo`.

## Embed it

```html
<script type="module" src="https://canvas.example.com/sdk/embed.js"></script>
<open-canvas server="https://canvas.example.com" token="{{ launch_jwt }}" style="height:100vh"></open-canvas>
```

The token claims, callbacks, postMessage events and REST API are in the
[integration guide](docs/05-INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md); the wire formats are in the
[build contract](docs/15-BUILD-CONTRACT.md).

## How it works

```
Your app  ── signs launch token (who, which file, which role) ──▶ OpenCanvas iframe
          ◀── load / save / assets / members / copies callbacks ──  OpenCanvas server
```

- **Your app owns** authentication, users, permissions, files, versions and retention.
- **OpenCanvas owns** the editor, real-time merge, presence, export and autosave back to your storage.
- **OpenCanvas never becomes the system of record:** it keeps only a transient room log and a save outbox.
- HS256, RS256, EdDSA and JWKS launch tokens are single use, and callbacks are signed
  ([security](docs/07-SECURITY-AND-LIMITS.md)).

## Releases and roadmap

The latest release is 0.4.1 (2026-11-28), which closed the spreadsheet, chart and Timeline gaps
in the [0.4.0 release notes](docs/37-RELEASE-v0.4.0.md); every version is in the
[CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md). Next: v0.4.2 finishes partial sync (spreadsheets as parts, the first
screen under 2 s); v0.5 brings plugins with a marketplace, backlinks, a knowledge graph and SDK
extension points; OpenCanvas Workspace, a first-party host, is a parallel track; v0.6 is advanced
automation and app building ([roadmap](docs/09-ROADMAP.md)). Support is best-effort, with no
production SLA.


# Release notes 0.4.0

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/release-040.html
Source file: docs/37-RELEASE-v0.4.0.md

**Status:** released 2026-11-28, tag `v0.4.0`.
**Licence:** Apache-2.0 (ADR-037).
**Plan:** [docs/36](36-ROADMAP-v0.4.md). **Approved prototypes:** [docs/prototypes/v04-approved/](prototypes/v04-approved/).
**Benchmarks:** [site benchmarks page](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/benchmarks.html); results are in `bench/results/` and `e2e/perf/results/`.

OpenCanvas 0.4.0 adds spreadsheets, advanced databases and charts, and is a performance and
reliability release. The host still owns users, permissions and files; the server never stores
documents (ADR-001). Support is best effort, with no SLA.

## 1. What 0.4.0 contains

| Area | What it does | Decisions |
|---|---|---|
| Spreadsheet block (SHEET-00..08) | Excel-style grid on opencalc's engine with our own grid: name box, formula bar, Excel keyboard, about 120 functions per cell, sheets, fill and Ctrl-drag, paste from Excel and Sheets with options, formats, freeze, filters, merge, borders, wrap, find and replace, move/hide rows and columns, tab colours; full screen; live editing with peers' selections; phone layout and view only; offline. `.xlsx`/`.ods` import (with formats, styles and widths) and `.xlsx` export; values in exports, `search.json`, the API and MCP | ADR-080 |
| Linked charts | Column, line, area, pie, donut and scatter charts from a sheet range or a database grouped field; live updates; exports write the values as a table | SHEET-06 |
| Database ⇄ spreadsheet | "Open as spreadsheet" as a live view or a copy; a sheet range converted to a database | SHEET-06 |
| Advanced databases | Formulas in spreadsheet syntax, relations and rollups; virtualized tables at 100,000 rows; Timeline (Gantt) with dependencies, milestones and critical path; Workload by person and week | DB4, DB5-01 |
| Partial sync | Databases and boards load as subdocuments, on by default | ADR-076..079 |
| Performance | 10,000 connections on one node; up to 1,000 editors in a room (cap 550 by default); progressive first screen; memory fixes | docs/36 |
| Reliability | Overload answers 503 with `Retry-After`, never 500; recovery admission after a restart; crash and restore drills; downgrade-tolerant migrations; saves after a restart with a slow host | RLB-01..04 |
| Nextcloud Talk | A canvas beside a chat or call, meeting canvases, the canvas card, Follow me | TALK-01 |
| Board toolbar | One row with priority overflow; optional left rail | UX4-01 |
| Security | Dependency upgrades (jsonwebtoken 12, p256 0.14, resvg 0.50); import limits for spreadsheets; a time budget for formula computation on the server; SEC-54..64 | docs/18 §7 |

## 2. Upgrade notes (from 0.3.x)

1. **Partial sync is on by default.** Editors before 0.4 are closed with 4426 on split rooms.
   Deploy the 0.4 editor with the 0.4 server, or set `[host.flags] partial_sync = false`.
2. **Migrations** `0012` (WAL per document id) and `0013` (restore epoch) run at start-up.
3. **HS256 hosts need a non-empty secret** (jsonwebtoken 12 refuses an empty one).
4. **Busy servers answer 503 with `Retry-After`.** Clients should retry after the given delay; the editor and SDKs already do.
5. **New block types** `core.spreadsheet` and `core.chart`; `xlsx` and `ods` in `import_formats` and `export_formats` when the host allows them.
6. **Container:** `ghcr.io/casualoffice/opencanvas:0.4.0`. Helm chart `0.4.0`.

## 3. Known limitations

In 0.4.0, and whether 0.4.1 (2026-11-28, [CHANGELOG](../CHANGELOG.md)) closed them:

- Partial sync does not split spreadsheets yet, and the 50 MB first screen is above the 2 s target. Still open after 0.4.1: the partial-sync items PSYNC-BUG-2..4 are v0.4.2.
- Spreadsheet: no cell comments, no "changed since" undo message, no merge and wrap in the phone layout, and merges across frozen panes were two cells. Fixed in 0.4.1.
- Charts: no browser test for database charts and the live database ⇄ spreadsheet view; the chart was placed after the sheet, not floating over it. Fixed in 0.4.1.
- Timeline: Workload reassigned through a select, not by dragging; no Months grouping on phones; Timeline was not in the insert menu. Fixed in 0.4.1, except that on a phone reassigning still uses the select.
- The slow-host save drill ran on SQLite only, and DEP-01 lacked the SBOM and update policy. Since 0.4.1 the drill passes on SQLite and MySQL 8.4, and SBOMs and the update policy are in place.
- Benchmarks marked `local` ran on a developer laptop, not the reference machine.

## 4. Release checklist

1. Pre-push gates, `cargo test` for oc-server, oc-model and oc-sheet, and the full Playwright suite on the release commit (157 of 159 passed in one run; the import-dialog wording test was updated and passes, and the access-expiry test passed alone).
2. CI green on `main`.
3. Version 0.4.0 everywhere, CHANGELOG dated.
4. `gh release create v0.4.0 --target <sha>`.
5. Check the binaries and the container on the release.


# Release notes 0.3.0

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/release-030.html
Source file: docs/35-RELEASE-v0.3.0.md

**Status:** released 2026-11-26, tag `v0.3.0` (tracker REL-05).
**Licence:** Apache-2.0 (ADR-037).
**Plan:** [docs/34](34-ROADMAP-v0.3.md). **Acceptance:** [docs/23 §v0.3](23-ACCEPTANCE.md#v03-acceptance-acc-v3).
**Approved prototypes:** [docs/prototypes/v03-approved/](prototypes/v03-approved/).

OpenCanvas 0.3.0 adds portable live blocks, search, automation and offline editing. Every new
feature is off until the host turns it on. The host still owns users, permissions and files;
the server never stores documents (ADR-001). Support is best effort, with no SLA.

## 1. What 0.3.0 contains

| Area | What it does | Decisions |
|---|---|---|
| Live blocks (LIVE-01..11) | One block shown live in several canvases and edited in place; "Make live", the host's picker, references that refresh, convert to a copy, `<open-canvas view="block">`, the folder path in the header, the "/" menu inside a live block | ADR-039, ADR-069..073 |
| Search (SRCH-01..06) | Find and replace in a canvas (also inside live blocks, with its own confirmation); search all canvases through the host's own search; `search.json` in every save, `POST /api/v1/extract`; Nextcloud unified search | ADR-065, ADR-066 |
| Automation (AUTO-01..07) | Rules stored in the canvas: triggers (row added, field changed, checklist checked, comment, date, schedule), actions (set a field, move a row, checklist, comment, notify, call a URL), limits, auto-pause, run history, Undo | ADR-067, ADR-068 |
| Offline (OFF-01..07) | A copy kept on the person's device, opted in by the host and then per canvas; editing without a network; reconnect and merge with a summary; revocation; sign-out clears the device | ADR-063, ADR-064, ADR-074 |

Also: the categorised insert menu (0.2.1), the trademark notices (LEGAL-01), and the site's
structured data and facts page (SITE-03).

## 2. Upgrade notes (from 0.2.x)

1. **Migrations.** `0010_automation` and `0011_offline_generation` run at start-up on SQLite and
   MySQL/MariaDB. They hold metadata only (schedules, run log, a generation number per person).
2. **New host sections, all off by default** (docs/05):
   - `[host.flags] live_blocks` and `[host.live]` (§2c); live blocks need `/access`, `POST /files` and `perms.live`.
   - `[host.search]` with the optional `GET /search` callback (§2).
   - `[host.automation]` and `perms.automate` (§2e). Scheduled runs call the load, save and
     `POST /mentions` callbacks with no bearer token; the v2 signature is the proof.
   - `[host.offline]`, `perms.offline` and `offlineReason` (§2d); JWT hosts only. Reconnect asks
     the host for a fresh token; a person who lost access is answered with `Action_RefreshToken { access: "none" }`.
3. **Editors older than 0.3 on documents with live blocks** are closed with 4426, as 0.2 did for SDK blocks.
4. **Every save now carries `search.json`** (plain text, capped at 2 MB, no comments by default).
5. **Container:** `ghcr.io/casualoffice/opencanvas:0.3.0`. Helm chart `0.3.0`.

## 3. Known limitations

- Offline is tested in Chromium; the phone layout is built but has no WebKit/Firefox run, and
  there is no end-to-end test for the expiry lock or queued uploads (OFF-08 deferred).
- Automation with Redis-only storage is refused at start-up; a cluster with Redis as its shared store was not tested.
- Nextcloud unified search is unit-tested; its Nextcloud glue is checked manually (no Nextcloud CI).
- The live block "from which canvas" cursor label was dropped (owner decision, ADR-069 note).
- SDK blocks cannot be made live yet.

## 4. Release checklist

1. Full local run on the release commit: `cargo test --workspace`, `pnpm -r test`, the full Playwright suite.
2. CI green on `main`.
3. Version 0.3.0 everywhere, CHANGELOG dated.
4. `gh release create v0.3.0 --target <sha>` (the release must exist before `release.yml` publishes).
5. Check the binaries and the container on the release.


# Release notes 0.2.0

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/release-020.html
Source file: docs/32-RELEASE-v0.2.0.md

**Status:** released 2026-11-25, tag `v0.2.0` (tracker REL-04). Includes the block SDK runtime
(BSDK-03/04), host editor profiles (EDP-01) and block discovery metadata.
**Licence:** Apache-2.0 (ADR-037).
**Plan:** [docs/27](27-ROADMAP-v0.2.md).
**Acceptance:** [docs/23 §v0.2](23-ACCEPTANCE.md#v02-acceptance-acc-v2).
**Security audit:** [docs/18 §6](18-SECURITY-AUDIT.md#6-release-audit-v020-2026-11-25-rel-04).

OpenCanvas 0.2.0 makes the headless API the supported way for programs to read and write
canvases. It also adds webhooks, version history and a block SDK. The host still owns users,
permissions and files; OpenCanvas never stores documents (ADR-001). Support is best effort, with
no SLA.

## 1. What 0.2.0 contains (frozen)

v0.2 = the stable headless API (docs/27 §4), the block SDK (§3), version history and webhooks
(§0). The owner moved portable live blocks (§2, LIVE-01..06) to v0.3 on 2026-11-24. On
2026-11-25 the owner added host editor profiles and block discovery metadata.

Version 0.1.2 already shipped part of this work: HAPI-01..05 (the `/api/v1` router, tokens,
idempotency, cursors and rate limits, and the events stream) and version history. 0.2.0 makes
them the stable contract and adds the rest.

| Part | Content | Rows | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Headless API | `/api/v1` with OpenAPI 3.1 at `/api/v1/openapi.json` and RFC 9457 errors. User-scoped bearer tokens share one auth check with MCP (`canvas:read/comment/write/admin`). `Idempotency-Key` works on every file write. Cursors are signed. Rate limits use `RateLimit` headers and are shared with MCP. There is an events stream (SSE and WebSocket) and a headless CRDT sync token. The 0.1 routes stay as deprecated aliases | HAPI-01..05 | Built (in 0.1.2), stable in 0.2.0 |
| Clients | TypeScript `@opencanvas/client` and Rust `opencanvas-client`, both generated from the OpenAPI document. They retry, send idempotency keys, page through cursors, resume events and verify webhooks, and they share one conformance suite | HAPI-06, HAPI-07 | Built |
| MCP over the API | Every MCP canvas tool is an adapter over an API operation, with the same scope, limiter and idempotency store. `POST /api/v1/files/{id}/boards` is new | HAPI-08 | Built |
| API reference | `/api/` on the website: guides, plus one page per OpenAPI tag | API-DOCS-01 | Built |
| Webhooks | Signed deliveries of the events-stream events from a durable outbox (`webhook_outbox`). Retries with backoff, sent once per cluster, same-origin only | WH-01 | Built |
| Version history | Named versions, list, preview, diff, and restore with a 30 s undo. History comes from host callbacks or from bounded in-file history | VH-00..03 | Built (in 0.1.2) |
| Block SDK, data side | Block manifests with a JSON Schema registry in MOD-01, checked on every write path (including the room WebSocket, SEC-46). One generic `extBlock` node and the `ext` root. Declarative export templates and fallbacks. Versions and declarative migrations. 0.1.x forward compatibility | BSDK-01, -02, -05 | Built |
| Block SDK, runtime | A sandboxed iframe per block on a separate origin, a CSP and a bridge RPC. The `@opencanvas/block-sdk` package, the `oc.progress` and `acme.okr` samples, and an author guide | BSDK-03, -04 | **In progress: gates the tag** |
| Block discovery metadata | The manifest gains `discovery`: label, category, keywords, profiles and complexity | (SDK agent) | **In progress: gates the tag** |
| Host editor profiles | `[host.editor]` profiles (notebook, meeting, project, diagramming, document, full). Each sets the enabled blocks, the quick-insert blocks and the feature switches. Hidden blocks are never deleted | EDP-01 | **In progress: gates the tag** |

## 2. Change control until the tag

- **Allowed:** finishing BSDK-03/04, EDP-01 and block discovery metadata as designed, and P0/P1
  fixes and security fixes. Each change has a tracker row, a test seen failing first and a
  CHANGELOG line.
- **Not allowed:** new endpoints, new config or format changes outside those rows. They go to
  0.2.1 or v0.3.
- `.ocanvas` stays format version 1 and `schemaVersion` 1 (ADR-042). Additions are additive:
  `extBlock`, the `ext` root, `history/` and `requires.blocks`.

## 3. Upgrade notes

The steps differ by the version you start from. **Back up the database and the host files
first.** Let pending saves finish before you replace the server. Migrations run at start-up.

1. **Database migrations 0008 and 0009.**
   - `0008_api_idempotency` (new in 0.1.2) creates the `api_idempotency` table.
   - `0009_webhook_outbox` (new in 0.2.0) creates the `webhook_outbox` table.
   - Both hold ids, counts, revisions and event JSON only, never document content.
   - Both run on SQLite, MySQL 8 and MariaDB 10.11. Redis-only storage uses keys instead.
   - Nodes that start together on an empty database now wait for each other's migrations
     (SEC-47). From 0.1.0 or 0.1.1 both migrations run; from 0.1.2 only 0009.
2. **New per-host config sections.** All are optional. A host without them behaves as in 0.1.x.
   - `[host.api]`: user tokens (`issuer`, `audience`, `all_files`, `token_admin`), rate limits
     (`rate_per_sec`, `burst`, per-file writes) and `default_mode`. User tokens need
     `OC_PUBLIC_URL` or `[host.api] audience`.
   - `[host.webhooks]`: `url` (same origin as `callback_base`, checked at start-up), `events`,
     `secret` and `max_attempts`. Receivers verify `X-OpenCanvas-Signature` v2 and deduplicate
     by `Idempotency-Key`.
   - `[host.versions]`: history sources and the bounds of in-file history (docs/30).
   - `[host.blocks]`: `enabled = ["type@range"]` picks which installed SDK packages the host's
     editors see; the default is none. Packages are installed by the operator in
     `OC_BLOCKS_DIR`. `OC_BLOCKS_ORIGIN` must be a different site from `OC_PUBLIC_URL`.
   - `[host.editor]` (EDP-01): the editor profile. The default, `full`, behaves exactly like
     0.1.x. A narrower profile hides blocks and features in the editor and never deletes
     content.

   Start-up checks every section and refuses a bad value with a message that names it.
3. **The headless API is on by default** (owner decision, 2026-11-25). `/api/v1` answers for
   every host unless it sets `[host.flags] api_v1 = false`. It grants nothing new: every call
   needs the host key, which the 0.1 routes already accept, or a token of at most 15 minutes that
   the host signs itself, and user tokens stay off until the host sets a public base URL. The 0.1
   routes (`/v1/files/{id}/patch|commit|role|import|session`, `/v1/convert`) keep working. They
   now carry a `Deprecation` header and a `Link: rel="successor-version"`, and v0.3 retires them
   (docs/27 §9 decision 8), so on by default gives hosts the 0.2 line to move over.
4. **Editors older than 0.2 on documents with SDK blocks are closed with 4426.** A 0.1.x
   editor deletes every `extBlock` it receives, because its schema has no such node. The room
   refuses that update and closes the session with code 4426 ("editor out of date: reopen the
   canvas"). Reloading the page loads the current editor. Hosts that cache the editor bundle or
   pin an old embed should reload it after the upgrade. Documents without SDK blocks are not
   affected.
5. **Room updates are checked against SDK block schemas** (SEC-46). A client that writes attrs
   or data that break an installed package's schema gets a denial, as API and MCP writes
   already did.
6. Container: `ghcr.io/casualoffice/opencanvas:0.2.0`. Helm: chart `0.2.0`. WOPI hosts still
   need proof keys. For older deployments, read the
   [v0.1.0 upgrade notes](28-RELEASE-v0.1.0.md#upgrade-notes) first.

## 4. Known limitations

- **No portable live blocks.** They moved to v0.3 (docs/27 §2, docs/23 LIVE-A1..A7 deferred).
- **The categorised insert menu is a v0.2.1 follow-up.** It uses `[host.editor]` profiles and
  block discovery metadata, and it is built after its prototype is approved (ADR-011). In 0.2.0
  the existing slash menu shows what the profile enables.
- **Block SDK.** No marketplace, and no install from the browser (v0.5). No third-party code
  runs on the server. Script migrations run only in the sandbox.
- **Headless API.** No `OpenCanvas-Version` date header (decision 6). The MCP tool
  `inputSchema`s are still written by hand, not generated from the OpenAPI components. The Rust
  client has no `yrs` CRDT-sync feature; `create_sync_token` returns a ticket for any
  y-websocket client. Neither client is published to a registry (`private` / `publish = false`).
- **Open Low security findings** (docs/18 §6), each with a recorded decision:
  - token grants allow exports of what the token can read;
  - the sync-ticket connect window counts from first use;
  - history caches are per room;
  - huge diagram coordinates become `null`;
  - SEC-36 and SEC-37 from v0.1.0.
- **Not demonstrated:** scale-out across machines. Single node first; the room cap is 550
  (docs/22).
- AI and MCP are experimental and off by default.

## 5. Release checklist

Run on **the release commit**, after BSDK-03/04, EDP-01 and the discovery metadata are merged.
A check that ran only on an earlier commit does not count. Results from this preparation run
(branch `worktree-agent-a1106dbc1b8b0f9f0`) are recorded for reference.

# Release notes 0.1.2

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/release-012.html
Source file: docs/31-RELEASE-v0.1.2.md

OpenCanvas 0.1.2 adds host integrations, structured diagramming, version history, and a
versioned headless API. See the [changelog](../CHANGELOG.md) for changes since v0.1.1
and the [execution tracker](10-EXECUTION-TRACKER.md) for implementation and test evidence.

## What's included

- The [Nextcloud app](../integrations/nextcloud/README.md) uses WOPI and keeps canvas files,
  versions, and shares in Nextcloud. The [Mattermost plugin](../integrations/mattermost/README.md)
  adds canvases to channels. The [Element / Matrix widget](../integrations/matrix/README.md)
  provides shared room canvases. [Jitsi Meet](../integrations/jitsi/README.md) continues to
  support temporary meeting canvases.
- [Diagram mode](29-DIAGRAMMING.md) adds libraries, ports, routing, and auto-layout.
  Import draw.io and Excalidraw with a dry-run report, and export draw.io and Mermaid alongside
  PNG and SVG. See the diagram guide for format coverage and mixed-version behavior.
- [Version history](30-VERSION-HISTORY.md) supports named saves, comparison, restore, and a
  30-second undo after restore. The history menu depends on host capabilities and user permissions.
- The [host integration guide](05-INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md) describes the headless API, scoped access,
  and host launch options. Read the [operations guide](13-OPERATIONS-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md) for deployment
  and monitoring.

## Upgrade notes

- Back up host files and follow the [recovery guidance](25-RELEASE-v0.1.0-alpha.1.md#durability-modes)
  before upgrading. Allow active saves to complete before replacing the server.
- Use `ghcr.io/casualoffice/opencanvas:0.1.2` for the container. For Helm, use chart `0.1.2`
  from the checkout with `image.repository=ghcr.io/casualoffice/opencanvas`. WOPI hosts still
  need proof keys. Consult the [v0.1.0 upgrade notes](28-RELEASE-v0.1.0.md#upgrade-notes) for older deployments.
- Configure each integration with its own guide, including the allowed iframe origins. Hosts adopting
  version history should check their callback support and the permissions granted to each user.

## Known limitations

Support is best-effort, with no production SLA. Start with a single node and review the
[capacity guidance](22-CAPACITY-AND-SIZING.md) before scaling. AI and MCP are experimental and
off by default. For diagram interchange and mixed-version sessions, see the
[diagram guide](29-DIAGRAMMING.md).


# Release notes 0.1.0

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/release.html
Source file: docs/28-RELEASE-v0.1.0.md

**Embeddable collaborative workspace canvas.**

**Status:** released 2026-11-23, tag `v0.1.0`. Scope: [docs/26](26-RELEASE-v0.1.0-SCOPE.md)
(tracker REL-02, REL-03). Licence: Apache-2.0 (ADR-037).

v0.1.0 is the first final release of OpenCanvas. It is open source under the
[Apache License 2.0](../LICENSE); keep [NOTICE](../NOTICE) when you redistribute it. Your
application keeps the users, the permissions and the files; OpenCanvas does the editing,
real-time merge (Yjs CRDT), presence, export and autosave back to your storage (ADR-001).

Support is **best effort, with no SLA** (see [Known limitations](#known-limitations) and
[SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md)).

> **Upgrading from v0.1.0-alpha.1? Read [Upgrade notes](#upgrade-notes) first.** WOPI hosts now
> need proof keys or the server refuses to start; MCP needs `OC_PUBLIC_URL` (or `mcp_audience`);
> MCP tokens must name their files unless the host has `/access` or `mcp_all_files`; WOPI
> sessions are capped at 10 h; invalid `.ocanvas` files and invalid writes are refused.

## What's included

v0.1.0 is **v0.1.0-alpha.1 + the alpha.2 security fixes + the three release blockers**, and
nothing else (docs/26 §1). Everything that alpha.1 shipped is unchanged and its evidence is in
[docs/25 §What's included](25-RELEASE-v0.1.0-alpha.1.md#whats-included): rich text, databases,
whiteboards, 40 templates, collaboration and roles, autosave through the outbox, the standalone
SQLite deployment (MySQL/MariaDB and Redis optional), the host SDK and REST API, JWT and WOPI
launch, the tested import and export formats, and the experimental AI assistant and MCP endpoint
(off by default). The durability modes and backup and recovery are also as described in
[docs/25](25-RELEASE-v0.1.0-alpha.1.md#durability-modes).

## What changed since v0.1.0-alpha.1

Rust tests are in `crates/oc-server/tests/` and `crates/oc-model/tests/`; acceptance IDs are
in [docs/23](23-ACCEPTANCE.md); security IDs in [docs/18](18-SECURITY-AUDIT.md).

### Security: the three Medium findings of the alpha.1 audit (SEC-33, SEC-34, SEC-35)

- **SEC-33, MCP audience.** The MCP token audience comes from `[host.ai] mcp_audience` or
  `OC_PUBLIC_URL`, never from the request's `Host` header. With neither, `/mcp/{hostId}` answers
  404 and start-up logs one warning. Test: `mcp::without_a_public_url_a_token_matching_the_host_header_is_refused`
  (seen failing: 200 instead of 404).
- **SEC-34, MCP file scope.** Without the host `/access` callback, an MCP token without a
  `files` claim is refused (`FILES_REQUIRED`) unless the host sets
  `[host.ai] mcp_all_files = true`. Tests: `mcp::without_the_access_callback_a_token_without_files_is_refused`
  (seen failing), `mcp::mcp_all_files_lets_a_token_without_files_cover_every_file`,
  `mcp::the_host_access_callback_decides_the_role_over_the_token_claim`.
- **SEC-35, WOPI session cap.** A WOPI session ends at `access_token_ttl` or 10 h after the
  launch, whichever is first. Test: `wopi::a_far_future_access_token_ttl_is_clamped_to_the_session_cap`
  (seen failing: expiry 10 years out).

### WOPI proof keys (WOPI-13 PASS, SEC-44)

Every WOPI call to the host carries `X-WOPI-TimeStamp`, `X-WOPI-Proof` and `X-WOPI-ProofOld`
(SHA256withRSA over the spec bytes), and `/hosting/discovery` publishes the current and old
`<proof-key>`. Keys come from `OC_WOPI_PROOF_KEY` and `OC_WOPI_PROOF_KEY_OLD` (PEM, or sealed
with `OC_KEK` by `opencanvas seal-proof-key`); `OC_DEV=1` generates one. The Helm chart mounts
them from a Secret, `wopi.proofKeySecret` (keys `current` and, during rotation, `old` with
`wopi.oldKey: true`). The reference WOPI host verifies every call and refuses missing, tampered
and stale (> 20 min) proofs.

- docs/23 **WOPI-13** PASS (was FAIL in alpha.1): `proof::tests::*`,
  `wopi::every_wopi_call_carries_a_valid_proof`, `wopi::discovery_route_serves_xml`,
  `scripts/e2e-wopi.sh` (seen failing with `WOPI_PROOF=off`).
- docs/18 **SEC-44** (Medium) fixed. Rotation: [docs/05 §6](05-INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md); variables:
  [docs/13](13-OPERATIONS-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md).

### Block schema validation (MOD-01) and the template load test (FC-07)

- **MOD-01.** `oc-model` validates the block schema (docs/15 §4.1): `oc_model::validate`,
  `validate_json` and `validate_blocks` return errors and warnings with a JSON-pointer path.
  Errors refuse the input: `read_ocanvas` fails with `Error::Invalid` naming the bad node
  (`POST /v1/convert` answers 400 `INPUT_INVALID`; a host file that breaks the schema does not
  open), and REST patch, server-side import and MCP writes answer 400 `PATCH_INVALID`. Unknown
  blocks, marks and attributes are warnings only, kept verbatim and counted in
  `oc_schema_warnings_total`. Tests (seen failing first): `tests/validate.rs`,
  `acceptance::mod01_rich_document_validates`,
  `host_api::patch_applies_to_the_live_room_and_reaches_clients` (REST 400),
  `metrics::tests::schema_warnings_are_exported`. docs/23 **FC-01**, **FC-02**, **FC-04** still
  PASS (unknowns kept).
- **FC-07** PASS (was Not run): all 40 built-in templates are built as the gallery builds them,
  checked against `crates/oc-model/tests/fixtures/templates.json`, validated with no errors or
  warnings and round-tripped through `.ocanvas`
  (`web/packages/editor/src/templates.fixture.test.ts`,
  `templates::fc07_every_builtin_template_validates_and_round_trips`; seen failing with a
  corrupted heading level).
- The web editor still relies on ProseMirror's own schema; MOD-01 is the server's view.

### Memory returned after eviction

The jemalloc purge had never run (`arena.4096.purge` was called with a non-null input and the
error was ignored). It now uses null pointers, logs failures, and its sweeper starts in
`AppState::new`. In the 1,000 rooms × 5 nonstop-typing run, RSS 60 s after typing stopped, with
0 rooms open, fell from **856 MB to 174 MB** ([docs/22 §9.7](22-CAPACITY-AND-SIZING.md)). Tests:
`alloc::tests::jemalloc_purge_is_accepted`, `tests/alloc_release.rs`. (This fix is also recorded
in the alpha.1 notes and CHANGELOG.)

### Release artefacts

`.github/workflows/release.yml` builds from the tag:

- a multi-architecture container image, `ghcr.io/casualoffice/opencanvas` (linux/amd64 and
  linux/arm64, native builds), pinned to the tag;
- standalone Linux binaries (x86_64, aarch64) with the editor bundle;
- SHA-256 checksums and build provenance for both.

Running them: [docs/13](13-OPERATIONS-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md).

### Licence and planning

- Relicensed to the **Apache License 2.0** (ADR-037), with NOTICE and an SPDX header in every
  source file.
- The v0.2 plan is [docs/27](27-ROADMAP-v0.2.md) (portable live blocks, block SDK, stable
  headless API under `/api/v1`; ADR-039 to ADR-042).

## Upgrade notes

From v0.1.0-alpha.1 (or a build of `main` before it). **Each item can stop a working
deployment; check them before you upgrade.**

1. **WOPI hosts now require proof keys.** If the hosts file has any WOPI host, the server
   **refuses to start** without a proof key. Generate a 2048-bit (or larger) RSA key
   (`openssl genrsa -out proof.pem 2048`), set `OC_WOPI_PROOF_KEY` to its path (or a file sealed
   with `opencanvas seal-proof-key < proof.pem`), and give every node the same key. On Helm, set
   `wopi.proofKeySecret` to a Secret with the key `current`. To rotate later, set
   `OC_WOPI_PROOF_KEY_OLD` (Helm: key `old` and `wopi.oldKey: true`). Hosts that do not check
   proofs keep working. See [docs/05 §6](05-INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md) and
   [docs/13](13-OPERATIONS-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md).
2. **MCP needs a public URL.** Set `OC_PUBLIC_URL`, or `[host.ai] mcp_audience`, on any host that
   uses MCP. Without either, MCP is off (404) and start-up logs a warning. Tokens whose `aud` was
   built from a `Host` header no longer work.
3. **MCP tokens must name their files** (`files` claim) unless the host implements the `/access`
   callback or sets `[host.ai] mcp_all_files = true` (broad: one token's role on every file).
   Otherwise the call is refused with `FILES_REQUIRED`.
4. **WOPI sessions are capped at 10 h.** An `access_token_ttl` further out is clamped; past the cap
   the host launches again.
5. **Invalid documents and writes are refused.** An `.ocanvas` that breaks the block schema is
   refused when read (`/v1/convert` answers 400 `INPUT_INVALID`; a host file of that kind does
   not open), and a REST patch, import or MCP write that breaks it answers 400 `PATCH_INVALID`
   with the path of the bad node. Unknown blocks and attributes are still accepted and kept.
   Check any tool that writes `.ocanvas` or calls `/v1/files/{id}/patch`.

Unchanged from alpha.1: the database migrations run at start-up (back up first); `.ocanvas`
stays format version 1 and `schemaVersion` 1 for all of 0.1.x (docs/26 §3); the defaults listed
in [docs/25 §Upgrade notes](25-RELEASE-v0.1.0-alpha.1.md#upgrade-notes) still apply. The host
REST API (`/v1/…`) is usable but not yet versioned as stable; v0.2 adds `/api/v1` and keeps the
0.1 routes as aliases until v0.3 (docs/27).

## Known limitations

- **No SLA.** Support is best effort, as stated in [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md): 0.1.x gets
  security fixes and P0/P1 bug fixes only (docs/26 §3); there is no maintained release branch
  beyond that and no uptime, response-time or data-retention commitment.
- **Memory grows with document size under nonstop typing.** yrs keeps dead items, so a room's
  live document is about 15–20× its encoded size while people type
  ([docs/22 §9.4, §9.5](22-CAPACITY-AND-SIZING.md)). Memory is now returned after rooms close
  (above), but size for the documents you keep open. Sizing: docs/22 §4 and docs/13.
- **Single node first.** Cluster mode passes the crash and chaos runs, but scale-out across
  machines is not demonstrated (docs/22 §12); the room cap is 550.
- **Durability depends on the mode** (`memory`, `wal`, Redis WAL):
  [docs/25](25-RELEASE-v0.1.0-alpha.1.md#durability-modes).
- **AI and MCP are experimental and off by default**; canvas content goes to the model server
  you configure. AI-01, AI-02 and AI-UI are in Review.
- **WOPI:** no `LOCK`/`UNLOCK` by design; conflicts use timestamps (WOPI-05).
- **Not built:** SSRF-safe link unfurl (UNF-01), server-rendered preview for viewers (RND-01),
  host team templates (TPL-01), an editor import menu (docs/23 FC-10: server import only).
- **Helm** is linted and rendered in CI but has not been installed in a real cluster, and there
  are no dashboards (OPS-01).
- **No portable live blocks, block SDK or stable headless API**: these are v0.2
  ([docs/27](27-ROADMAP-v0.2.md)). Third-party block types are kept as unknown blocks, not
  rendered. Only `.ocanvas` version 1 exists.
- **MOD-01 is server-side only**; the web editor uses ProseMirror's schema, and link and embed
  URLs are sanitised on export rather than checked.
- **Open Low security findings**, each with a recorded decision (docs/18 §5): SEC-36 (redirects
  in operator-configured clients), SEC-37 (`canvas:write:direct` not checked), SEC-38 to SEC-42
  accepted; SEC-43 (MCP `comment_add` always refused, fails closed) is an open functional bug.
- **Owner review.** Most design documents (docs/02 to docs/08) and several built features are
  still `Review` in the tracker, awaiting the owner's approval; the owner's approval of the
  docs/26 scope lock is pending.

# FAQ

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/faq.html

## FAQ

Short, direct answers, each followed by the page that says more. Numbers link to where they were measured.

## What is OpenCanvas?

OpenCanvas is an open-source, real-time collaborative canvas that other applications embed, the way they embed Collabora Online for office files. One document holds rich text, databases and whiteboards, with live cursors and comments. Your application keeps the users, the permissions and the file; OpenCanvas does the editing and saves the file back to it. See the facts for the release, the stack and the measured capacity.

## Can I use it in production today?

OpenCanvas 0.4.3 is an early release with best-effort support and no production SLA. You can run it, but read the known limitations before you rely on it: durability depends on the persistence mode you choose, and scale-out across several machines has not been demonstrated yet. Source: CHANGELOG.md, “## [0.4.3] - 2026-11-28” The limits are in the release notes and on the home page .

## Is OpenCanvas free?

Yes. OpenCanvas is open source under the Apache-2.0 licence, so you may use, modify, self-host, embed and redistribute it, including in commercial and closed-source products, at no cost. The one duty when you redistribute it is to keep the NOTICE file and the licence with it.

## What does the licence allow?

OpenCanvas is under the Apache License, copyright CasualOffice. You may use, modify, self-host, embed and redistribute it, in open or closed, commercial or non-commercial products and services. When you redistribute OpenCanvas or a work derived from it, keep the NOTICE file and the licence. The bundled fonts are under the SIL Open Font License. The LICENSE file states the exact terms and is the authority; this summary is not legal advice.

## Does OpenCanvas keep my documents?

Only while a session is live. The server keeps a snapshot and the recent updates of an open canvas so it survives a restart and late joiners can catch up, and deletes them after the session is saved and idle. The file itself lives in your application, and OpenCanvas writes every change back there. See Architecture .

## How do users sign in?

They sign in to your application, not to OpenCanvas. Your backend checks access and signs a short-lived launch token naming the file, the user and the role: view, comment or edit. OpenCanvas trusts that decision for the life of the token, enforces it on every edit, and switches a role live when your app calls the role API. See the integration guide .

## Is there a Save button?

No. Every change saves to your application on a short timer, when the canvas goes idle, when the last person leaves and when the server shuts down. Each save goes through a durable outbox, so a restart resends it. If your copy of the file changed elsewhere, the policy you chose runs: save a copy, or reload.

## We already use Collabora through WOPI. Can we reuse that?

Yes. OpenCanvas is a WOPI client: it uses discovery, CheckFileInfo, GetFile, PutFile and PUT_RELATIVE, calls only the WOPISrc URLs on its allow-list, and signs every call to your WOPI host with the WOPI proof headers. Nextcloud's integration works this way. See WOPI mode and Nextcloud .

## How is OpenCanvas different from Collabora Online?

They share an integration model and edit different things. Collabora Online edits office documents: text, spreadsheets and presentations. OpenCanvas edits a canvas: blocks, databases and whiteboards in one document. In both, the host application keeps the file and the permissions, and the editor runs the live session and saves back to the host. The project's research note studies Collabora's integration in detail.

## How does it compare with Slack Canvas, Zoom Canvas and Microsoft Loop?

Those canvases live inside their vendor's product and the vendor stores the file: Slack, Zoom, or OneDrive and SharePoint for Loop. OpenCanvas is built to be embedded in your own application, stores the file in your application through callbacks, and runs on your own servers. Loop's portable live components have no OpenCanvas equivalent yet; they are planned. The comparison table on the home page has the details, from the vendors' public documentation.

## Which apps does it integrate with?

There are ready integrations for Jitsi Meet (a temporary canvas in every meeting), Nextcloud (.ocanvas files through WOPI), Mattermost (canvases in channels) and Element / Matrix (a room widget). Any other web application can embed OpenCanvas with a launch token signed by its backend, or open it as a WOPI client. See Jitsi Meet , Nextcloud , Mattermost , Element / Matrix and the integration guide .

## What can it import and export?

It exports Markdown, HTML, JSON, its native .ocanvas file and Word, and PDF when the operator runs the optional Gotenberg sidecar; otherwise the editor prints to PDF. Whiteboards export as SVG and PNG. It imports Markdown, HTML and CSV into a canvas, when the host turns import on: it is off by default. See Operations .

## How many users can one server handle?

The project's sizing guide gives up to 1,000 concurrent users on 1 vCPU and 512 MB, and up to 5,000 on 2 vCPU and 2 GB; beyond 5,000, run cluster mode. These figures come from load tests on one laptop, with most people watching and some typing, so measure on your own hardware. Source: docs/22, “In short: up to 1,000 concurrent users on 1 vCPU and 512 MB; up to 5,000 on 2 vCPU and 2 GB; beyond 5,000, cluster mode.” See Capacity and sizing , which also has the nonstop-typing, crash and cluster runs.

## How does it scale?

One node runs on SQLite with no database to set up. For more users, run several nodes against MySQL or MariaDB with Redis: each room has one owner node, the other nodes relay to it, and if the owner dies another node takes the room over from its log. See Operations and Architecture .

## What is it built with?

The server is written in Rust, on tokio and axum, and ships as one binary or a Docker image. The editor runs in the browser and is built on Tiptap (ProseMirror) with Yjs, the CRDT that merges everyone's edits. Storage is SQLite by default, or MySQL or MariaDB, with Redis for a cluster. See Architecture .

## Does the demo send anything anywhere?

No. The demo is the real editor running against a document in your browser, with simulated collaborators. There is no server behind it, and exports that need a server say so. Its assistant plays a scripted run: no model is called and nothing leaves your browser.

## Where does the assistant send my content?

Only to the model server the operator configures: the Claude Platform, or a self-hosted model through vLLM, Ollama or llama.cpp. The OpenCanvas server makes that call, never the browser. AI is off unless the operator turns it on for your app. A self-hosted model needs tool calling for the assistant to edit; without it, it can only answer. See AI and MCP . Last changed 2026-11-28 .


# Facts

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/facts.html

## Facts

OpenCanvas in short, for people and for tools that quote it. Each row links to the repository file, test or tracker entry it comes from; the release and its date are read from Cargo.toml and CHANGELOG.md when the site is built.

## What is OpenCanvas?

OpenCanvas, by CasualOffice, is the open-source collaborative workspace engine for your application: a real-time collaborative canvas that other applications embed. One document holds documents, spreadsheets, databases, whiteboards and diagrams, with live cursors and comments. The host application keeps the users, the permissions and the file; OpenCanvas does the editing, merges every change live and saves the file back to the host. Source: README.md, “The open-source collaborative workspace engine for your application.”

# Integration guide

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/integration.html
Source file: docs/05-INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md

**Status:** draft v0.1, 2026-11-21. This is the contract an integrating
application implements. Modelled on Collabora Online's WOPI integration
([01 §4](01-RESEARCH-COMPETITIVE-ANALYSIS.md)).

> **Golden rule:** your application decides *who* may open *which* file with
> *what* role. OpenCanvas trusts that decision for the life of the token and
> enforces it on every edit. Your application stores the file.

## 1. Choose a handshake

| | **JWT launch** (recommended for new apps) | **WOPI-compatible** (for existing WOPI hosts) |
|---|---|---|
| Who verifies the user | You sign a JWT | OpenCanvas calls your CheckFileInfo |
| Callbacks you implement | `GET file`, `PUT file`, assets (people search and resolve optional) | WOPI: CheckFileInfo, GetFile, PutFile |
| Extra round-trip on open | none | CheckFileInfo |
| Good for | Any custom app | Nextcloud, ownCloud, Seafile-style hosts |

## 2. Register your host

`opencanvas.hosts.toml` (or `hosts` table):
```toml
[[host]]
id              = "acme"
name            = "Acme"
mode            = "jwt"                    # jwt | wopi | both
jwt_alg         = "HS256"                  # or RS256 / EdDSA: jwt_public_key (PEM) or jwt_jwks_url
jwt_secret      = "env:ACME_OC_SECRET"
api_key         = "env:ACME_OC_API_KEY"    # for server→server REST calls to us
callback_base   = "https://api.acme.example/opencanvas"
allowed_origins = ["https://app.acme.example"]
# frame_ancestors = ["https://chat.example"] # optional: extra origins that may frame THIS host's editor (§4)
asset_origins   = ["https://cdn.acme.example"] # extra image origins for exports (unsigned GET);
                                           # your callback_base origin is always allowed
[host.flags]
embeds          = ["youtube", "vimeo", "loom", "figma", "maps"]
export_formats  = ["md", "html", "pdf", "ocanvas"]   # formats this host allows: md, html, json, docx, pdf, ocanvas, svg/png (board images), xlsx (spreadsheet blocks); omit for all
import_formats  = ["md", "html", "csv", "drawio", "excalidraw", "xlsx", "ods"]  # formats editors may import (POST /v1/import); absent or empty = import OFF;
                                           # any other value is refused at start-up
autosave_secs   = 60
on_conflict     = "copy"                   # copy | reload
team_templates  = true                     # gallery "From your team" from GET /templates (§5, TPL-01); default off
temporary_wording = "meeting"              # storage = "ephemeral" only (§8a, ADR-049): "meeting" (default) or "room"
history         = true                     # you implement the version callbacks (§5); default off
# history_url   = "https://app.acme.example/files/{fileId}/versions"  # else: link to your own version page

[host.versions]                            # version history sources (§5a, docs/30, ADR-051, ADR-055)
file              = true                   # bounded history inside the .ocanvas: default true for JWT
                                           # hosts, false for WOPI hosts; never for temporary canvases
file_max_kb       = 1024                   # its byte budget (compressed)
file_max_versions = 50                     # and its count
prefer_host       = true                   # with your versions too: your list first, in-file = "recent changes";
                                           # on restore or conflict your version wins

[host.blocks]                              # SDK blocks your editors may load (§2a, BSDK-01); default none
enabled           = ["acme.okr@^1", "acme.ticket"]   # "type@SemVer requirement" (requirement optional);
                                           # a bad entry is refused at start-up, one not installed is logged;
                                           # the / menu lists them in this order
[host.blocks.permissions."acme.okr"]       # optional: narrow what a block may do on this host (decision 9)
network           = ["https://okr.acme.example"]     # a subset of the manifest's origins
members           = "none"                 # "read" (the manifest's ask) or "none"
```

### 2a. SDK block packages (BSDK-01, docs/27 §3, ADR-040, ADR-058)

Third-party blocks are **installed by the server operator** and **enabled per host**. There is no
upload API and nothing is installed from the browser.

- `OC_BLOCKS_DIR`: a directory with one sub-directory per package, each holding `block.json` (the
  manifest, docs/15 §4.2) and the bundle it names in `entry`. At start-up the server parses every
  manifest, checks it (type name, SemVer, JSON Schemas, templates, permissions, migrations) and
  verifies the bundle against `integrity` (`sha384-<base64>`, Subresource Integrity). A package that
  fails any check is **refused**: logged, listed on `/healthz` as `blocks.refused[{package,
  reason}]`, and not installed. The server still starts; documents using its type keep the blocks
  as they are and show their fallback.
- Type names are lowercase reverse-DNS labels (`acme.okr`, `com.example.ticket-card`); `oc.` is
  reserved for OpenCanvas's own blocks. One package per type.
- `OC_BLOCKS_ORIGIN`: the separate origin block code runs on (`https://blocks.canvas.example`;
  `http://` only for local development). Point a second host name at the same server; it answers
  `/blocks/frame/{host}/{type}` (the sandboxed frame document) and `/blocks/{type}/{version}/{file}`
  (bundle, migrations script, `preview.png`) **only** for requests to that host name, and 404 on
  the editor's. It must differ from `OC_PUBLIC_URL`'s origin, or the server refuses to start.
  Without it no block code runs: editors show every SDK block as its read-only saved copy. Set
  `OC_PUBLIC_URL` too, so frames may be embedded only by the editor (`frame-ancestors`).
- `[host.blocks] enabled` picks which installed packages a host's editors see, in that order.
  `[host.blocks.permissions."<type>"]` narrows what a block may do on this host: `network` keeps
  only the listed origins of the manifest's, `members = "none"` withholds the member list. A host
  can take permissions away, never add. The session (`GET /v1/sessions/:ticket`) lists the
  packages as `blocks: [{type, version, v, title, icon, description, publisher, keywords, discovery, content,
  attrs, data, export, migrations, entry, frame, preview, integrity, permissions}]` (`frame` is
  `{OC_BLOCKS_ORIGIN}/blocks/frame/{host}/{type}`, `entry` and `preview` live under
  `{OC_BLOCKS_ORIGIN}/blocks/{type}/{version}/`, all null without a block origin; `permissions` is
  the effective set). A host with no `[host.blocks]` gets an empty list.
- The frame's CSP is `default-src 'none'; script-src '<runtime sha384>' <package path>/;
  style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data: blob:; font-src data:; connect-src <effective network
  or 'none'>; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors <OC_PUBLIC_URL origin>`; the
  bundle loads with its SRI hash. The editor frames it with `sandbox="allow-scripts"` only.
- Validation of block attributes and data (docs/15 §4.2) uses every **installed** package, whatever
  a host enables, on `.ocanvas` load, the REST patch, imports, the headless API and MCP writes.

People (docs/21 revision 2): the @mention list is the people with access to the canvas, the same
for every viewer. Everyone with access sees real names and the `detail` second line. OpenCanvas
never shows or stores e-mail.

### 2b. Editor profiles (EDP-01, ADR-061; `[host.editor]`)

One engine, many experiences. A profile decides which blocks the editor **offers to insert**;
`features` turn whole surfaces off. Omit the table for today's behaviour (`full`).

```toml
[host.editor]
profile = "meeting"          # notebook | meeting | project | diagramming | document | full (default)
allow_profile_switch = false # reserved: stored and sent, no UI yet
intents = true               # INS-01: goal chips in the insert menu (default true)
chips   = ["Track tasks", "Plan a sprint", "Draw architecture"]  # replaces the built-in chips

[host.editor.blocks]         # optional
enabled      = ["core.text", "core.heading", "core.checklist", "acme.okr"]  # replaces the profile's set
quick_insert = ["core.checklist"]  # the insert menu's Quick insert tiles, in order; default []

[host.editor.features]       # every key optional
comments        = true
version_history = true
ai              = true
diagramming     = true
templates       = true
import          = true
```

**Block ids.** `core.text`, `core.heading`, `core.checklist`, `core.bulleted_list`,
`core.numbered_list`, `core.toggle`, `core.quote`, `core.callout`, `core.divider`, `core.code`,
`core.database`, `core.kanban`, `core.calendar`, `core.table`, `core.spreadsheet`, `core.chart`, `core.image`, `core.file`,
`core.date`, `core.link_preview`, `core.embed`, `core.whiteboard`, `core.diagram`,
`core.shapes`, `core.columns`, `core.import`, `core.assistant`. `kanban` and `calendar` are views
of a database and insert through the Database entry; `diagram` and `shapes` are modes of a
whiteboard and insert through the Whiteboard entry. A block list may also name an SDK block type
that `[host.blocks]` enables for this host.

**Profiles** (the owner's proposal; additions so each profile is usable are marked +):

| Profile | Blocks |
|---|---|
| `notebook` | text, lists (bulleted, numbered, checklist), image, link preview, callout; + heading |
| `meeting` | text, heading, checklist, bulleted and numbered lists, callout, divider, simple table; + date |
| `project` | database, kanban, calendar, checklist; + text, heading, date |
| `diagramming` | whiteboard, diagram, shapes; + text, heading |
| `document` | text, heading, simple table, image; + bulleted and numbered lists, divider |
| `full` | every block (default) |

`core.text` is always offered, even when `enabled` leaves it out. Every profile keeps the
`core.import` and `core.assistant` actions; the `import` and `ai` features decide whether they
show. SDK blocks follow their manifest's `discovery.profiles` (absent: `full` only, the SDK default);
with an explicit `enabled` list only the SDK types it names are offered.

**Hide, never delete.** A profile only hides blocks from the insertion surfaces: the / menu (and
the gutter and phone "+", which open it), the phone bar's quick buttons, "Turn into", the empty
canvas starters and the markdown shortcuts that would create a hidden block (`> ` stays text in
`meeting`). Paste is not filtered. A document holding any block type opens, renders, stays
editable and round-trips unchanged in every profile; nothing on the server reads the profile
when it loads, saves or exports a document.

**Features and the older switches.** An explicit `[host.editor.features]` value wins; an unset
one leaves the older switch in charge:

| Feature | Off means | Older switch (alias) |
|---|---|---|
| `comments` | no new threads, no Comments button; `perms.comment` false; the API and MCP refuse comment writes | none (on) |
| `version_history` | no history menu (`history: "none"`, `perms.history` false); `/v1/history*` answer `404 HISTORY_OFF`. In-file history already in the file is kept as is | `[host.flags] history`, `[host.versions]` |
| `ai` | no assistant, no MCP for this host, whatever `[host.ai]` says. `true` cannot turn AI on without a `[host.ai]` agent | `[host.ai] enabled`, `mcp` |
| `diagramming` | no Diagram button, menu entry or Shift+D on whiteboards (existing boards still open) | none (on) |
| `templates` | no template gallery or Templates starter; no "From your team" | `[host.flags] team_templates` (that section only) |
| `import` | no Import entry; `POST /v1/import` answers `403 IMPORT_OFF`. `true` without `import_formats` allows every import format | `[host.flags] import_formats` |

**The insert menu (INS-01, ADR-062).** "/" (and the gutter and phone "+") opens one menu:
*Quick insert* (`quick_insert`, else Text, Heading, List, Image, Table; at most five; an id like
`core.checklist` or `core.kanban` inserts that variant), *Recent* (this browser only), *Start from
a goal* (the goal chips) and *Explore* (Content, Data & planning, Visual & diagrams, Layout,
Extensions). A profile with 8 or fewer blocks (counting List, Heading, Callout, Columns, Database
and Diagram once each) gets one flat list in `quick_insert` order instead, with no bands and no
"Browse all blocks"; `meeting` lists Text, Heading, List (Checklist), Callout (Decision), Simple
table, Date and Divider. `intents = false` removes the goal chips; `chips` (at most 6 phrases of
1-40 characters) replaces the built-in "Track tasks", "Draw architecture", "Write notes". A chip
only fills the search; matching is local keyword matching, nothing is sent anywhere. Recent is
kept in the browser's `localStorage` per host and person (`oc.insert.v1:<host>:<user>`).

**Start-up checks.** An unknown profile, setting, block id or feature, a non-boolean feature or
`intents`, a `quick_insert` id the profile does not offer, more than 6 `chips` or a chip that is
empty or over 40 characters, and `chips` with `intents = false` refuse to start, naming the host
and the bad value.

### 2c. Portable live blocks (LIVE-01, docs/27 §2, docs/34 §2, ADR-039, ADR-069, ADR-070)

A live block is written once and shown live in many canvases: its content is **its own host file**
(a small `.ocanvas` with `meta.kind = "live"`), embedded by file id and opened as its own room. You
keep that file like any other, under your ACL; OpenCanvas stores nothing new.

```toml
[host.flags]
live_blocks = true                         # off by default in 0.3.0-alpha

[host.live]
snapshot = "title"                         # "none" | "title" (default) | "content": what of a live
                                           # file the canvases that embed it may keep (§2c below)
link     = "https://app.acme.example/files/{fileId}"   # optional: exports link a live block here
max_open = 8                               # 1-8: live block rooms one editor session may have open
```

You implement two callbacks (§5): **`POST /files`** (create the backing file for "Make live";
without it "Make live" answers 501 and the editor hides it) and **`POST /access`**, which is
**required** for live blocks: every person who meets a live block is checked against it (cached
30 s). Without `/access`, only the files your launch token lists in `live` open, and only
read-only.

- **Who may make and embed.** The token's `perms.live` (default false) lets a person make live
  blocks and insert `liveBlock`/`blockRef` nodes; the room refuses such an insert from anyone else.
- **Derived grants.** When an editor meets a live block it asks
  `POST /v1/live/session {ticket, fileId}`: the canvas must really embed that file, then your
  `/access` answer decides the role (`none`: 403, nothing about the file is shown) and its
  optional `path` is what the block's header shows as where the source lives. The new session
  expires with the parent, has the parent's perms at most (never `live`), and cannot derive
  again. It is an ordinary room session: your role API (§7) and revocations reach it at once.
- **Snapshots.** `snapshot = "title"` keeps only the title in the embedding canvas; `"none"` keeps
  not even that; `"content"` (for hosts whose ACL treats embedding as sharing) also keeps a
  Markdown snapshot (≤ 64 KB), written by the server, never by a client. Exports inline what the
  exporting person can read and show "Live block: <title> (no access)" for the rest.
- **Depth.** A live file cannot contain live blocks or references, and a canvas holds at most 50.
- **Usage.** OpenCanvas keeps no index of where a live block is used: the `live.embedded` and
  `live.removed` events (§7b, webhooks §7c) tell you, so you can keep your own.
- **Deleted files.** Answer `/access` with **410** (or `{"role": "none", "gone": true}`) for a
  live file you deleted or moved: the block then says "This live block was deleted or moved" and
  offers Remove (and, under `snapshot = "content"`, Keep last copy). A plain `none` reads as "no
  access".
- **In the editor (LIVE-03, ADR-069).** The session answer's `live` says what to offer
  (`{enabled, make, insert, snapshot, maxOpen, link}`). "Make live…" is in the block menu; "Live
  block" in the insert menu asks **your** picker (`UI_PickLiveBlock`, below): OpenCanvas keeps no
  list of live files. Pasting a block link (the editor's own "Copy link", or a URL matching
  `[host.live] link`, with `#block=<id>` for one block or `#live` for a live file) asks Live block
  / Reference / Link. A live block shows an always-visible header (Live mark, title, the people in
  it, Open source, options) and is edited in place; references refresh on their own.
- **Who can see this.** `GET /v1/live/audience?ticket&fileId` counts the canvas's other members
  (your members callback, else the token's `members`; at most 200) that your `/access` would not
  let open the live file. One `/access` call per member per 30 s; never names.

**Start-up checks.** A `live_blocks` that is not a boolean, an unknown `[host.live]` key, a bad
`snapshot`, `max_open` outside 1-8, a `link` that is not http(s) or lacks `{fileId}`, and
`live_blocks = true` on a WOPI-only host, a temporary-canvas host or a host without
`callback_base` refuse to start, naming the host.

### 2c-bis. Partial sync (PSYNC-02/03, ADR-076; `[host.flags] partial_sync`)

```toml
[host.flags]
partial_sync = true    # the default from 0.4; false keeps every room whole
```

A room keeps each database, board (diagrams included) and spreadsheet (from 0.4.1) as a
subdocument that the editor loads
when the block comes near the screen, so a large canvas opens on its text and the server and the
browser hold only what people look at (on the 50 MB benchmark canvas the room holds the main
document: 220 MB against 4.4 GB for 20 viewers, and the browser 16 MB against 472 MB). Your files
do not change: every save is the same `.ocanvas` format v1 with the same content and Yjs item ids,
and the API, MCP, exports, `search.json` and history read and write as before. It works on every
storage (SQLite, MySQL/MariaDB, the Redis WAL, Redis only) and under either durability; a part's
edits reach the WAL as they happen.

**Editors before 0.4** do not speak it: a split room closes them with 4426 and they show "reopen
the canvas", which loads the current editor. If you embed an older editor build, or run a client
that edits the Y.Doc directly without `caps=subdoc`, set `partial_sync = false` until it is
updated. Turning it off again is safe: a room folds its parts back into one document when it next
opens. Temporary canvases and live block files are never split.

**Reopening a large canvas (0.4.1).** A split room of 4 MiB or more that closes with everything
saved keeps its split in the database (`OC_KEEP_SPLIT_MIN_BYTES`, bytes; smaller canvases are
purged as before). The next open compares the version your load returns (its `ETag`) with the
version the room saved; when they match, the room opens from what it kept instead of reading
and cutting the file (the 50 MB benchmark canvas: 1.3 s to its first screen instead of 3.3 s).
Any other version, or a host that answers the load with a different version name than the save,
reads the file as before. This costs database space: about the canvas's Yjs size for each large
canvas until it is opened at another version.

### 2c-ter. Formulas, relations and rollups (DB4, ADR-078; `[host.flags] formulas`)

`formulas = true` lets people add formula, relation and rollup fields to databases (off by
default; the session JSON carries `formulas`). Fields that already exist always compute, whatever
the flag. Only expressions and related row ids are stored in the canvas; the server computes the
values for exports (Markdown, HTML, CSV, PDF), `search.json`, the API and MCP (`queryRows` /
`db_query` return them, and filters and sorts see them). Errors are values (`{err: "#DIV/0", msg}`
in JSON, the code in text exports). Relations across canvases go only through a live block already
on the canvas, are one-way, and show "No access" to readers without access to the live file.

### 2d. Offline copies (OFF-01..08, docs/34 §3, ADR-063, ADR-064; `[host.offline]`)

A person can keep a canvas **on their own device** and keep editing without a network; the edits
merge when they are back. The copy lives only in that browser (IndexedDB, encrypted under a device
key per host and person); **OpenCanvas stores no content for it** (ADR-001): the server keeps one
number per host and person (the revocation generation). Off by default at both levels: you turn it
on for the host, you allow it per launch, and the person turns it on per canvas.

```toml
[host.offline]
enabled      = true       # default false; JWT hosts only in v0.3 (WOPI hosts refuse to start)
auto_recent  = 0          # >0: also keep the last N opened canvases without asking (0-50)
grant_days   = 7          # how long a copy opens without reconnecting, 1-30
max_role     = "edit"     # edit | comment | view: the highest role a copy keeps
max_canvases = 50         # per person per host per device (1-500)
max_mb       = 200        # all copies of one person on one device (1-2000)
uploads_mb   = 50         # queued uploads per canvas (and at most 20 files)
unsent_mb    = 5          # unsent changes per canvas before editing pauses (1-50)
```

- **Per launch.** The token's `perms.offline` (default false) says whether this person may keep
  this canvas offline now. Leave it out on shared devices, kiosks, guest and "don't keep me signed
  in" sessions; the optional top-level `offlineReason` (for example `"shared-device"`, ≤ 200
  characters) is shown where "Available offline" would be.
- **The grant.** When both allow it, the session answer carries `offline.grant`: an ES256 JWS the
  server signs (`host`, `sub`, `file`, `role` ≤ `max_role`, `exp` ≤ `grant_days`, `gen`). The
  editor keeps it with the copy and uses it only on the device, to decide whether and in which
  role the copy opens. It is never a credential: reconnecting is always a fresh launch through
  you (`POST /tokens/refresh`, §5), and your current answer decides. The signing key comes from
  `OC_OFFLINE_KEY` (base64 of 32 random bytes) or is derived from `OC_KEK`, so every node agrees.
- **Revoking.** `POST /api/v1/offline/revoke {"userId"}` (host key or `canvas:admin`, §7b) raises
  the person's generation: every device holding their copies for your host deletes them, with
  their unsent changes, at the next session answer. A lower role on reconnect holds the changes
  (download or discard); no access deletes that copy.
- **Signing out.** Your sign-out page must clear the device, below (§4c).

**Start-up checks.** An unknown `[host.offline]` key, a value out of range, a bad `max_role`,
`auto_recent` above `max_canvases`, and `enabled = true` on a WOPI-only host refuse to start,
naming the host.

### 2d-bis. Links and backlinks (LINK-01..05, docs/38 §2, ADR-081; `[host.flags] links`)

People link a canvas, a heading, a database or a row with `[[` in the editor, or by pasting one of
your URLs. Every canvas then shows **Linked from** (the canvases that link to it, with the sentence
around each link) and **unlinked mentions** (canvases that name it without a link, from your
search, §5). Off until you turn it on:

```toml
[host.flags]
links = true          # default false: no index, no panel, [[ inserts an ordinary link

[host.links]
url_patterns = ["https://app.acme.example/canvas/{fileId}#{blockId}",
                "https://app.acme.example/canvas/{fileId}"]   # pasted URLs and links that are canvas links
url_template = "https://app.acme.example/canvas/{fileId}#{blockId}" # what exports and older editors link to
```

- **What OpenCanvas keeps.** A table `link_edges` (migration 0014) of ids only: which file and
  block links to which file, block and row, and whether it is a link, an embed (live block or
  block reference) or a relation. No titles, labels or text. It is written **only after your
  save callback acknowledged a save**, so it describes what you store. A save you refuse
  changes nothing.
- **Who sees what.** Every read asks you, for the reader, about every linking canvas, with
  **`POST /access/batch`** (§5, optional, up to 200 files a call) or else `POST /access` per file
  (8 at a time); both are cached 30 s. A canvas the reader cannot open is left out and not
  counted; a failing answer shows nothing rather than everything. Titles, paths, `updatedAt`,
  `updatedBy` and `space` come from those answers. `POST /access` is required (JWT hosts that
  store their files; not WOPI-only or temporary canvases).
- **Excerpts** are made when the panel opens, from the linking canvas as the reader may read it
  (the open room, else your load callback with that reader's bearer), kept 5 minutes in memory
  and never written.
- **Deleted files.** Answer `/access` with 410 (or `gone: true` in a batch item): a deleted
  linking canvas loses its rows on the next read that sees it, a deleted target shows as
  "Deleted canvas". Call `DELETE /api/v1/links/files/{fileId}` (host key) to drop a deleted
  file's links at once.
- **Turning it on for existing files.** `POST /api/v1/links/index {"fileIds": [...]}` (host key,
  up to 100 a call) loads each file through your load callback, writes its links and drops the
  document. Walk your files once.
- **Graph.** `GET /api/v1/graph` and MCP `canvas_graph` (ADR-082) read the same index through the
  same checks. `space` in your access answers groups canvases (else the first segment of `path`).
- **Storage.** The index needs a database: Redis-only storage (no `DATABASE_URL`) refuses to start
  with `links = true`.

### 2e. Automation (AUTO-01..07, docs/34 §5, ADR-067, ADR-068; `[host.automation]`)

Rules such as "when Status changes to Done, move the row to Archive and notify the owner" are
**stored in the canvas** (the `automations` root, additive to format 1), so you store them with
the file and they travel with copies (a copy's rules are switched off and ownerless). The
OpenCanvas server runs them as the collaborator "Automation" **on behalf of the person who last
saved or switched on the rule**, re-checking that person's role with your `POST /access` at every
run (cached 30 s): below edit, the rule pauses. Without `/access`, the owner must have opened the
canvas in the last 30 days. Automation is off until you add the table:

```toml
[host.automation]
enabled          = true
actions          = ["field.set", "row.move", "todo.set", "todo.add", "comment.add", "notify", "http.post"]
allow_origins    = ["https://ci.acme.example"]  # URL calls may reach these besides your callback origin
max_rules        = 25      # per canvas, at most 100
runs_per_minute  = 60      # per rule
runs_per_day     = 1000    # per canvas
max_changes      = 50      # per run
max_depth        = 3       # rules started by rules
min_interval_min = 15      # schedules
time_zone        = "Europe/Berlin"   # IANA name, UTC, or UTC+05:30; rules may name their own
```

- **Who may create rules:** editors whose launch token has `perms.automate: true` (default
  false). Others see the rules read-only; the run history is shown to editors only. The server
  refuses a client write to `automations` without it, an invalid rule, an action you did not
  allow, a URL on another origin, and an enabled rule not owned by the person saving it.
- **Automation needs a database** (SQLite, MySQL or MariaDB) for its schedule and run log;
  with Redis-only storage the server refuses `[host.automation]` at start-up. Both tables hold
  ids, times, counts and codes, never canvas text; runs are kept 30 days.
- **Date and schedule rules run with nobody in the canvas.** A worker on every node claims due
  rows (one node per slot) and opens the file the way the API does: `GET` and `PUT
  /files/{fileId}` arrive **with no bearer token**, signed (v2) as always. Treat such a signed call
  as your own service acting for the file. A file that does not load is retried every 5 minutes
  for an hour, then the run is logged as failed.
- **`notify`** calls your `POST /mentions` (§5) with `by: "automation:<ruleId>"`,
  `onBehalfOf: <owner id>`, `mentioned`, `excerpt` (the rule's message) and
  `automation: {ruleId, name, runId}`, with no bearer token. OpenCanvas sends no mail.
- **`http.post`** sends `{rule: {id, name}, runId, fileId, by, trigger, fields, at}` (only the
  fields the rule names) to your callback origin or an `allow_origins` origin, signed like
  webhooks (`X-OpenCanvas-Signature` v2 with `[host.webhooks] secret` or your callback secret,
  `X-OpenCanvas-Event: automation.url`, `Idempotency-Key: <runId>`), 10 s timeout, no redirects,
  3 tries (now, after 1 minute, after 10 minutes; a 3xx or 4xx other than 408/425/429 is final).
- Ten failed runs in a row pause a rule and notify its owner once. Events `automation.ran` and
  `automation.failed` go to the events stream and webhooks; edits by a rule carry
  `by: "automation:<ruleId>"`, and the save's `X-OpenCanvas-Authors` lists `automation:<ruleId>`.
- Rules are document data: anyone who can read the file can read every rule, its owner, its URL
  targets and the fields it sends. Never put secrets in a rule.
- API and MCP: `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/files/{fileId}/automations[/{ruleId}]`,
  `POST …/automations/{ruleId}/enable`, `POST …/automations:test`, `GET …/automations/runs`
  (§7b); MCP `canvas_automations`, `canvas_automation_save`, `canvas_automation_enable`,
  `canvas_automation_test`.

### 2f. File types and app mode (FTY-01..08, docs/40 §0.8, ADR-085)

A host may give each file a **type**. A *document* is today's canvas, where any blocks mix. A *spreadsheet*, *whiteboard*
or *database* file holds exactly one root block of that kind and opens in **app mode**: the editor renders that block
full-page with its own chrome, with no document title, page margins, gutter or insert menu.

| `file.type` | Root block | App mode chrome | Exports offered first |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document` (default) | any blocks | the canvas editor | per `export_formats` |
| `spreadsheet` | `core.spreadsheet` | toolbar, formula bar with the cell name, the grid edge to edge, sheet tabs, selection sum/average/count | `xlsx`, `csv`, `pdf` |
| `whiteboard` | `core.whiteboard` (diagram mode is a switch on the board) | tools, board bar (Sketch / Diagram, shapes, frames), zoom, minimap | `png`, `svg`, `pdf`, `drawio` |
| `database` | `core.database` | view tabs (Table, Board, Calendar, Timeline), filter, sort, New row; a row still opens as a page of blocks | `csv`, `md` |

- **Telling us.** Put `file.type` in the launch token (§3). Any other value is refused at launch with `400 TYPE_INVALID`.
  `GET /hosting/capabilities` lists `fileTypes`; a server without it ignores the claim and opens a document, so check it
  before you show typed *New* entries.
- **New files.** When your load callback answers `404` (a new file) for a typed launch, the server creates the root block
  as the file's first edit (an empty sheet `Sheet1`, an empty board, a database with one Table view) and saves it through
  your `PUT /files/{fileId}` like any edit. `start` (ADR-048) is ignored in app mode.
- **The file remembers.** The `.ocanvas` manifest carries `type` (additive to format 1; older readers ignore it). A launch
  without the claim uses the manifest's type, so a downloaded spreadsheet reopens as one in any host. The claim wins when both
  are present.
- **Never lose content.** If a typed launch meets content that is not exactly one root block of that kind (someone added a
  paragraph through the API, or the host typed an old document), the editor opens it as a document with a notice ("This
  spreadsheet has other content, so it opened as a document") and the session answers `app: "document"`,
  `appFallback: "content"`. Nothing is removed or rewritten.
- **Session answer** (docs/15 §2): `app` (`document` | `spreadsheet` | `whiteboard` | `database`). Profiles (§2b) apply to
  documents and to database row pages; app mode has no insert surfaces to filter. `[host.editor.features]` apply as usual
  (comments on cells and shapes, version history, AI, import).
- **Everything else is the same file.** Version history (§5a), search (`search.json` gains `type`), exports, the headless API
  (`GET /api/v1/files/{fileId}` and `/extract` answer `type`), MCP, webhooks, live blocks and offline copies treat a typed
  file exactly like a document. `export` in app mode with no format picks the first of the table's formats that
  `export_formats` allows.
