**Proof keys (§6.4, WOPI-13).** Every call OpenCanvas makes to your WOPI host (CheckFileInfo,
GetFile, PutFile, PUT_RELATIVE, and any later override) carries the Microsoft proof headers:

- `X-WOPI-TimeStamp`: .NET ticks (100 ns since 0001-01-01 UTC) of the call.
- `X-WOPI-Proof`: base64 RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 / SHA-256 signature with the current key.
- `X-WOPI-ProofOld`: the same bytes signed with the old key.

The signed bytes are `be32(len token) ‖ access_token (UTF-8) ‖ be32(len URL) ‖ UPPERCASE(full
request URL, query and access_token included) ‖ be32(8) ‖ be64(timestamp)`. Discovery publishes
both public keys in the spec format, a CryptoAPI `PUBLICKEYBLOB` (base64) plus modulus and
exponent (base64, big-endian):

```xml
<proof-key oldvalue="BgIAAACkAABSU0Ex…" oldmodulus="…" oldexponent="AQAB"
           value="BgIAAACkAABSU0Ex…" modulus="…" exponent="AQAB"/>
```

A host accepts the call when `X-WOPI-Proof` verifies with the current key, or
`X-WOPI-ProofOld` with the current key, or `X-WOPI-Proof` with the old key; refuses a
timestamp older than 20 minutes; and answers `500` otherwise (after re-reading discovery once,
in case the keys rotated). `examples/wopi-host/server.mjs` does exactly this (`checkProof`);
`WOPI_PROOF=off` opts it out for servers without keys. Nextcloud, ownCloud and Seafile verify
these headers the same way they do for Collabora.

**Key configuration and rotation.** `OC_WOPI_PROOF_KEY` is the path of a 2048-bit (or larger)
RSA private key, PEM (PKCS#8 or PKCS#1), or the same PEM sealed with `OC_KEK`
(`opencanvas seal-proof-key < key.pem > key.sealed`). `OC_WOPI_PROOF_KEY_OLD` is the previous
key in the same forms; without it the current key is published and used as the old one.
With `OC_DEV=1` and no key, a pair is generated at start-up (it changes on every restart).
Start-up refuses a hosts file with a WOPI host when there is no key. Rotation: generate a new
key (`openssl genrsa -out new.pem 2048`), set `OC_WOPI_PROOF_KEY_OLD` to the current key and
`OC_WOPI_PROOF_KEY` to the new one, roll every node (they must share the keys); hosts accept
both while their cached discovery catches up. Drop the old key at the next rotation.

**Assets.** WOPI has no asset API, so uploads (`POST /v1/assets?ticket=`) are kept with the room
and answered `201 {"assetId":"a_…","url":"/v1/assets/a_…","mime","size"}`. They are served by
`GET /v1/assets/:id?ticket=` (images inline, anything else as a download, `nosniff`, sandboxed)
and inlined into the saved `.ocanvas` as `assets/<id>` (stored) plus `assets/index.json`
(`{"<id>":{"mime","size"}}`); only assets the document still references are written. On load
they are read back out of your file. Limits: **10 MB per asset, 50 MB of assets per file**
(`413 ASSET_TOO_LARGE`); the whole zip stays under the 100 MB `.ocanvas` read limit. DOCX, PDF
and `.ocanvas` exports include them too.

**Mentions.** The member list is the users who have opened the file (from CheckFileInfo, with
their `detail`) and the saved `people` map: the no-source case of §5 "People". Mention notifications (`POST /mentions`, §5) are not sent in WOPI mode.


# Jitsi Meet

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/jitsi.html
Source file: integrations/jitsi/README.md

`mod_opencanvas.lua` opens an OpenCanvas canvas in a Jitsi Meet call, in the shared-document
slot Etherpad uses. No Docker image or compose changes: one Prosody plugin plus `.env` lines.

- Everyone in the meeting opens the same canvas from **Shared document** and edits it live.
- The canvas is **temporary**: nothing is stored by Jitsi or by your host. It is deleted when
  the meeting ends; people download or export (PDF, Word, Markdown, `.ocanvas`) to keep it.
- It starts blank, or from a template you choose (`template = "meeting"`).
- A reload, a dropped network or an OpenCanvas restart rejoins the same canvas.

The integration was introduced in OpenCanvas 0.1.1. Version 0.1.2 improves how role changes
apply to links minted earlier in the meeting. See the [release notes](../../docs/31-RELEASE-v0.1.2.md).

## How it works

- Jitsi's client opens the `<etherpad>` value of a presence it receives in the shared-document
  iframe, if it resolves to the same origin as `config.etherpad_base`
  (`react/features/etherpad/middleware.ts`).
- The plugin, loaded on the MUC component, rewrites every presence the room delivers so
  `<etherpad>` is `https://canvas.example.com/v1/launch?token=<JWT>&ep=`, minted for that recipient.
  Jitsi appends its Etherpad options with `?` as if the URL had no query; `&ep=` gives them a
  parameter of their own so the token stays intact
  (docs/05 §3). Other `<etherpad>` elements (Jicofo, clients) are removed.
- Hook: it shadows `room:route_stanza()` per room (on `muc-room-created`). In Prosody's
  `plugins/muc/muc.lib.lua` that is the only per-recipient step: `muc-broadcast-presence` and
  `muc-build-occupant-presence` fire once per broadcast, and `pre-presence/full` only fires for
  stanzas from c2s sessions (`core/stanza_router.lua`). See the comment at the top of the file.
- `file.id` = `jitsi-` + SHA-256 of room JID (includes the tenant) and `meetingId`
  (`mod_muc_meeting_id`): a new meeting with the same name gets a fresh canvas.
- Role: `edit` for moderators and owners, `opencanvas_guest_role` for everyone else.
  A role that changes later (Jicofo grants moderator a moment after the join, or a moderator
  promotes someone) is sent to OpenCanvas's role API: the open canvas switches at once, and a
  link minted before the change opens with the new role (docs/05 §7).
- With Jitsi's own JWT sign-in, Jicofo makes every signed-in user a moderator, so signed-in
  people edit and guests (joining without a token, `ENABLE_GUESTS=1`) get
  `opencanvas_guest_role`. With `token_affiliation` and `ENABLE_AUTO_OWNER=0`, the token's
  `moderator` claim decides.
- User: `id`, `name`, `avatar` from the Jitsi JWT context (`session.jitsi_meet_context_user`),
  else the presence nick and an opaque hash of the JID.
- One token per XMPP session and role, re-minted after half its TTL; a reload or rejoin is a new
  session and gets a new `jti`. Presence is resent on every mute, so per-delivery tokens would
  churn the document URL.
- Signing: HS256 with Prosody's `util.hashes`. Jitsi's bundled `luajwtjitsi` is not used: in
  stable-11509-1 its signature segment is not standard base64url, so tokens fail to verify.
- Room destroyed: `DELETE /v1/files/{fileId}/session` with `X-OpenCanvas-Host` /
  `X-OpenCanvas-Key`, async; failures are logged and the idle timeout ends the canvas anyway.
- Tokens and secrets are never logged.

## Install (docker-jitsi-meet)

1. Copy the plugin:
   ```sh
   mkdir -p ${CONFIG}/prosody/prosody-plugins-custom
   cp mod_opencanvas.lua ${CONFIG}/prosody/prosody-plugins-custom/
   ```
2. Generate comma-free hex secrets: `openssl rand -hex 32` (twice).
3. Add to `.env` (values must not contain commas; `XMPP_MUC_CONFIGURATION` is split on them):
   ```sh
   XMPP_MUC_MODULES=opencanvas
   XMPP_MUC_CONFIGURATION=opencanvas_url="https://canvas.example.com",opencanvas_api_url="https://canvas.example.com",opencanvas_host_id="acme-meet",opencanvas_secret="<hex1>",opencanvas_api_key="<hex2>",opencanvas_guest_role="edit",opencanvas_token_ttl=3600
   ETHERPAD_PUBLIC_URL=https://canvas.example.com/
   ```
   If `XMPP_MUC_MODULES` already has values, append `,opencanvas`.
   Optional: `opencanvas_enabled_rooms="^canvas%-"` (a Lua pattern on the room name; default all).
   `opencanvas_api_url` is where Prosody calls OpenCanvas when a meeting ends; set it when
   Prosody reaches OpenCanvas at another address than browsers do (default: `opencanvas_url`).
4. Restart: `docker compose up -d --force-recreate prosody web`
   (`web` picks up `ETHERPAD_PUBLIC_URL`).
5. OpenCanvas `hosts.toml`:
   ```toml
   [[host]]
   id              = "acme-meet"
   name            = "Meeting"
   mode            = "jwt"
   jwt_alg         = "HS256"
   jwt_secret      = "env:ACME_MEET_OC_SECRET"     # <hex1>
   api_key         = "env:ACME_MEET_OC_API_KEY"    # <hex2>
   storage         = "ephemeral"                    # no host storage; ends with the meeting
   # template      = "meeting"                      # optional: a built-in template; unset = blank
   allowed_origins = ["https://meet.acme.example"]

   [host.flags]
   export_formats  = ["md", "html", "docx", "pdf", "ocanvas", "png"]

   [host.editor]
   profile         = "meeting"   # agenda, notes, decisions, tasks: text, headings, checklists,
                                 # lists, callouts, dividers, tables, dates (docs/05 §2b)
   ```
   The `meeting` profile only trims what the / menu offers; a canvas holding other blocks
   (a whiteboard pasted in, a database) still opens and edits as usual. Use `"full"` for every
   block.
   Template ids: `meeting`, `standup`, `retro`, `oneonone`, `brainstorm`, `allhands`, and the
   other built-in templates (an unknown id stops OpenCanvas at startup and lists them all).
   See docs/05 §8a.

## Debian packages (jitsi-meet-prosody)

Put the file in a plugin path (for example `/usr/share/jitsi-meet/prosody-plugins/` or a
directory added to `plugin_paths`) and edit `/etc/prosody/conf.d/meet.example.com.cfg.lua`:

```lua
Component "conference.meet.example.com" "muc"
    modules_enabled = {
        -- ... existing modules ...
        "opencanvas";
    }
    opencanvas_url = "https://canvas.example.com"
    opencanvas_api_url = "https://canvas.example.com"
    opencanvas_host_id = "acme-meet"
    opencanvas_secret = "<hex1>"
    opencanvas_api_key = "<hex2>"
    opencanvas_guest_role = "edit"
    opencanvas_token_ttl = 3600
```

and in `/etc/jitsi/meet/meet.example.com-config.js`: `config.etherpad_base = 'https://canvas.example.com/';`
Then `systemctl restart prosody`.

## Test checklist

- [ ] Prosody log shows `signing launch tokens with util.hashes (HS256)`, no errors.
- [ ] Two browsers join a room; the shared-document button appears; both open the same canvas.
- [ ] Moderator can edit; a guest gets `opencanvas_guest_role`.
- [ ] Reload one browser and open the document again: it opens (fresh `jti`).
- [ ] Leave and rejoin under the same room name after the room closed: a new, empty canvas.
- [ ] Prosody log shows `OpenCanvas session for … ended (2xx)` when the last person leaves.
- [ ] `grep -i token` in the Prosody log shows no JWT.

## Status: verified

Tested end to end on 2026-11-23 against a stock docker-jitsi-meet `stable-11509-1` (web,
prosody, jicofo, jvb) with only the plugin file and the `.env` lines above, and OpenCanvas
0.1.x with `storage = "ephemeral"`, driven by two separate browsers (Playwright):

- Prosody loads the module on the MUC component; `config.js` gets `etherpad_base`.
- Each person gets their own token; both open the same canvas from **Shared document**.
- The canvas opens blank (no template picker, no host name), says "Not saved · temporary".
- Text typed by one person appears for the other, both ways.
- A reload rejoins the same canvas with a fresh `jti`.
- When the meeting ends Prosody calls `DELETE …/session` (200) and OpenCanvas deletes the canvas:
  no rows left in the database.
- Restarting OpenCanvas mid-meeting keeps the canvas (`tests/ephemeral.rs`).

Also covered by tests: token minting and claim shape (`test/mint_test.lua`, Lua 5.4), a
plugin-minted token verified by OpenCanvas's own `jwt::verify`
(`crates/oc-server/tests/jitsi_plugin.rs`, skips without Lua 5.3+; set `OC_LUA`).

Jitsi's own JWT sign-in, tested 2026-11-24 (`ENABLE_AUTH=1`, `AUTH_TYPE=jwt`,
`ENABLE_GUESTS=1`, `opencanvas_guest_role="view"`): the signed-in moderator edits and the canvas
shows their name from the Jitsi token; a guest without a token gets view with the view-only
notice and sees the moderator's text live. Before the role push the moderator opened as view,
because their link was sent before Jicofo made them a moderator (fixed; see Role above).

Not tested yet: Debian-package installs and multi-shard deployments.


# Nextcloud

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/nextcloud.html
Source file: integrations/nextcloud/README.md

`opencanvas/` is a Nextcloud app (app id `opencanvas`, Nextcloud 30–32, PHP 8.1+). It lets
people create `.ocanvas` files in Files and edit them together in OpenCanvas: rich text,
databases and whiteboards in one file. Nextcloud keeps the files, sharing, permissions and
versions. OpenCanvas does the editing and stores no documents.

- Nextcloud is a **WOPI host** for OpenCanvas, the same way it is one for Collabora through
  Nextcloud Office.
- Design and decisions: [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).
- Screens: [UI-SCREENS.md](UI-SCREENS.md); approved prototype in
  `docs/prototypes/nextcloud-approved/`, with screenshots of the built app in its `screenshots/`.

**Status: alpha.**
- The backend and the approved screens S1-S8, S12 and S13 work end to end in a real Nextcloud 31
  with real browsers (see "Verified").
- Nextcloud Talk (TALK-01, v0.4): canvas cards in conversations, the Canvas panel beside the chat
  or call, and a temporary meeting canvas per call (see "Nextcloud Talk").

*Nextcloud is a registered trademark of Nextcloud GmbH. Mattermost is a trademark of Mattermost, Inc. OpenCanvas is an independent open-source project, not affiliated with or endorsed by either company.*

## How it works

1. **Open.** Someone opens an `.ocanvas` file. Nextcloud mints a short-lived access token for
   that person and file, and the page form-POSTs it into an iframe at
   `{opencanvas}/v1/launch?WOPISrc={nextcloud}/index.php/apps/opencanvas/wopi/files/{fileId}`.
2. **Load.** OpenCanvas calls the app's WOPI endpoints:
   - CheckFileInfo returns who the person is and what they may do.
   - GetFile returns the file.
3. **Save.** Saves are PutFile calls. Each save is a normal Nextcloud write, so it shows in
   **Versions** and in Activity under the editor's name.
4. **Conflicts.** If the file changed outside the canvas, OpenCanvas saves a
   "(conflict copy)" next to it (PUT_RELATIVE).
5. **Proof keys.** Every WOPI call carries an RSA proof signed by OpenCanvas. The app checks it
   against OpenCanvas's discovery, so only your OpenCanvas server can read or write files
   through these endpoints. Calls without a valid proof get `500`.
6. **Access checks.** Every call checks access live. When a share is removed or changed, the
   app also calls OpenCanvas's role API, so an open canvas switches to read-only or closes at
   once.
7. **One room per file.** Everyone who opens the same file edits the same live canvas: the room
   id is the WOPISrc.

**Permissions:**

| Nextcloud | In the canvas |
|---|---|
| Owner, or a share with "Can edit" | edit |
| Read-only share | view (read-only, no typing) |
| Share without "Allow download", or a public link with "Hide download" | editing as above, but no export, download or print |
| Share removed | the open canvas closes; opening again is refused |
| Share changed to read-only | the open canvas switches to read-only |

**In Files:**
- Clicking a canvas opens it in Nextcloud's **Viewer**; the row's "…" menu has **Open in full
  page** (`/apps/opencanvas/open/{id}`, with a bar back to the folder, Share and Download).
- The **+ New** menu has, after a separator: **New canvas** (Nextcloud's own name dialog and
  template picker; OpenCanvas opens it on its start screen), **New database canvas** and **New
  whiteboard canvas** (our name dialog, then `POST api/v1/create` with `kind`). The file opens as
  soon as it is created.
- `.ocanvas` files show the indigo canvas icon.
- The Sharing tab shows what each share level means in a canvas. With the admin's comment switch
  on, a view-only share's advanced settings get **Can comment in OpenCanvas**.
- **Public links** to a canvas open it under Nextcloud's public header. Guests on edit links give
  a name first (kept in the browser); view-only guests open at once as "Guest".
- When a canvas can't open (not set up, OpenCanvas down, proof rejected, over 100 MB, no access,
  not found, links turned off) a Nextcloud screen says what happened and what to do; admins get
  the fix.

**In Nextcloud search (SRCH-05, ADR-065).** Canvases appear in the unified search (the
magnifier in the header) under **Canvases**:
- Every save of an `.ocanvas` (OpenCanvas's PutFile, a conflict copy, an upload, a WebDAV PUT,
  a copy) carries `search.json`, the canvas's plain text with block ids. The app reads it into
  its own table `oc_opencanvas_search` (text only; deleted with the file). This is Nextcloud's
  index: OpenCanvas keeps none. Files saved before OpenCanvas 0.3 have no `search.json` and are
  indexed on their next save.
- Results are only files the person can open in Nextcloud, checked at search time, so a removed
  share hides a canvas at once. A result shows the canvas title, the matching text, its heading
  and its folder, and opens the canvas on the full page at the matching block (`#block=<id>`,
  sent to the editor as `Action_ScrollToBlock` once it has loaded).
- `occ opencanvas:search-index [user…]` indexes existing canvases (run once after an upgrade).
- Comments are in `search.json` only when OpenCanvas's `[host.search] comments = true`.

### Nextcloud Talk

With Talk (spreed) enabled, built to `docs/prototypes/v04-approved/nextcloud-talk.html` (TALK-01):

- **Post to a Talk conversation** (sharing sidebar card): pick a conversation, add an optional
  message, post. The message carries the canvas link, which Talk shows as an OpenCanvas card
  (a reference provider, `lib/Reference/CanvasReferenceProvider.php`, resolved per reader).
  **Posting never grants access.** If people in the conversation can't open the file, the dialog
  says how many and offers "Share the file with the conversation" (Can edit / Can view), a normal
  Talk room share.
- **The card**: title, where the file lives, two lines of text, when it was edited, "Open beside
  chat" and "Full screen" ("Open" on a phone). Someone without access sees only the title and who
  shared it, and "Ask … for access", which posts a Talk message mentioning the sharer.
- **The Canvas panel** (a "Canvas" button in Talk's top bar): beside the chat or call at 38 rem,
  as a 25 rem sidebar tab when the window is 64 rem wide or less, full screen (Talk's top bar with
  the call controls stays visible; Esc returns), and full screen with a draggable call tile on a
  phone (under 45 rem). Empty state ("No canvases here yet"), error state (Retry, Copy error; the
  call is not affected) and the no-access card.
- **Meeting canvas per call**: during a call, "New meeting canvas" starts a temporary canvas that
  everyone in the call edits. It lives in the app's data (`appdata_*/opencanvas/meetings`), not in
  anyone's Files. Moderators can turn off "Participants can start a canvas" for the conversation.
  When the call ends, everyone is read only at once and the moderator is asked to save or discard.
  Save writes `<conversation> meeting canvas <date>.ocanvas` into the moderator's Talk folder and,
  by default, shares it with the conversation (Talk posts it). With no answer within 10 minutes,
  or if no moderator was present, it is discarded (background job `ExpireMeetings`, every 5 min,
  plus a check on every look).
- **Guests** (public conversations) see meeting canvases with their Talk name and "(Guest)", read
  only unless the moderator turns on "Guests can edit"; they never save, export or download.
  Shared files keep their own Nextcloud permissions: Talk never raises them.
- **Moderator menu**: Guests can edit, Lock canvas (everyone else read only), Follow me (everyone
  with the panel open on the same canvas scrolls with the moderator; for a shared file only Follow
  me appears), Save to Files, Download.
- Role changes (lock, guests, call end, discard) reach open editors at once through OpenCanvas's
  role API when `opencanvas_api_key` is set; every WOPI call also re-reads the role.
- Meeting canvases use `{wopi_base}/meetings/{id}` as WOPISrc, under the same allow-listed prefix.
- Talk has no public PHP API for participants or call state: the app reads them through Talk's
  classes (`lib/Talk/SpreedGateway.php`, checked with Talk 21 on Nextcloud 31) and the browser
  uses Talk's OCS chat API. A Talk upgrade that changes those classes turns the panel off (no
  button) rather than failing.

## Install

Use an OpenCanvas 0.1.2 server for the features described in this guide. See
[Operations](../../docs/13-OPERATIONS-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md).

**1. OpenCanvas: register Nextcloud as a WOPI host** in `opencanvas.hosts.toml`:

```toml
[[host]]
id              = "nextcloud"
name            = "Nextcloud"
mode            = "wopi"
wopi_allowlist  = ["https://cloud.example.com/index.php/apps/opencanvas/wopi"]
allowed_origins = ["https://cloud.example.com"]
api_key         = "env:NC_OC_API_KEY"      # lets Nextcloud switch open canvases when shares change
[host.flags]
on_conflict     = "copy"
```

Start OpenCanvas with a proof key. It refuses a WOPI host without one:

```sh
openssl genrsa -out proof.pem 2048
OC_WOPI_PROOF_KEY=/path/to/proof.pem NC_OC_API_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 24) opencanvas
```

**2. Nextcloud: install and enable the app.**

```sh
cp -r opencanvas /var/www/nextcloud/custom_apps/   # or apps/
chown -R www-data: /var/www/nextcloud/custom_apps/opencanvas
occ app:enable opencanvas                 # registers .ocanvas (config/mimetypemapping.json)
occ maintenance:mimetype:update-js        # so the browser knows the type too
```

**3. Configure the app.**

```sh
occ config:app:set opencanvas opencanvas_url --value=https://canvas.example.com
occ config:app:set opencanvas opencanvas_api_key --value=<same as NC_OC_API_KEY> --sensitive
# optional
occ config:app:set opencanvas opencanvas_internal_url --value=http://opencanvas:8080
occ config:app:set opencanvas wopi_base --value=https://cloud.example.com/index.php/apps/opencanvas/wopi
occ config:app:set opencanvas opencanvas_host_id --value=nextcloud
```

| Key | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `opencanvas_url` | Where browsers reach OpenCanvas | required |
| `opencanvas_internal_url` | Where Nextcloud reaches OpenCanvas (discovery, role API) | `opencanvas_url` |
| `wopi_base` | The WOPI base OpenCanvas calls. It must be reachable from OpenCanvas and match its `wopi_allowlist`. | `{overwrite.cli.url}/index.php/apps/opencanvas/wopi` |
| `opencanvas_api_key` (sensitive) | The host's `api_key` in OpenCanvas. Without it, share changes take effect only at the next WOPI call or reopen. | empty |
| `opencanvas_host_id` | The host `id` in OpenCanvas | `nextcloud` |
| `allow_public_links` | Guests on public link shares | `true` |
| `allow_comment_role` | Read-only shares with the `opencanvas`/`comment` share attribute get the comment role | `false` |

- The token secret is generated on first use and stored as a sensitive value.
- If Nextcloud runs on a private address (Docker, LAN), also set
  `occ config:system:set allow_local_remote_servers --value=true --type=boolean`. Otherwise
  Nextcloud refuses to fetch discovery from OpenCanvas.

**4. Check the connection.** Open **Administration > OpenCanvas**: enter the address (and the
internal address and API key), save, copy the WOPI base into `wopi_allowlist`, and the
connection check runs its four steps (OpenCanvas answers, opens `.ocanvas`, publishes a proof
key, accepts this Nextcloud) with the fix for any failing one. Or, from a shell:

```sh
curl -u admin -X POST -H 'OCS-APIREQUEST: true' https://cloud.example.com/index.php/apps/opencanvas/settings/check
```

It should answer `{"ok":true,"steps":[…],"discovery":true,"ocanvasAction":true,"proofKey":true,
"accepts":true,"wopiBase":"…"}`. Put the `wopiBase` it shows into OpenCanvas's `wopi_allowlist`.

**5. Front end.** The app's screens are built with Nextcloud's standard tooling
(`@nextcloud/vite-config`, Vue 2.7, `@nextcloud/vue` 8, `@nextcloud/files` 3). Build before
installing from git; `js/` is not committed, as for other app-store apps:

```sh
cd opencanvas && npm ci && npm run build   # writes js/opencanvas-{files,viewer,fullpage,public,admin}.mjs
npm test                                   # JS unit tests (vitest)
```

## Verified

All runs on 2026-11-24.

**Real Nextcloud.** Setup:
- Nextcloud: official image `nextcloud:31-apache` (31.0.14) on SQLite in Docker, with this app
  mounted in `custom_apps`.
- OpenCanvas: built from this branch (`cargo build --release -p oc-server`) with a proof key,
  run on the host.
- Browsers: headless Chromium through Playwright, `tests/browser/nextcloud.e2e.mjs`.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `occ app:enable opencanvas` | enabled. The repair step wrote `ocanvas` → `application/vnd.opencanvas+zip`, and WebDAV reports that type for new files. |
| Admin connection check | `{"discovery":true,"ocanvasAction":true,"proofKey":true}` |
| `api/v1/create` blank / database / whiteboard | `201`, files created in the user's Files |
| Open an `.ocanvas` from Nextcloud (logged-in user, `/apps/opencanvas/open/{id}`) | editor loads. CheckFileInfo and GetFile pass the proof check. |
| Edit as the owner | edits |
| Save | autosave writes the `.ocanvas` into Nextcloud (the edit is in the file). The next save adds a Nextcloud version (versions listed 2 → 3). |
| Read-only user share (permissions 1) | opens view-only (`contenteditable=false`) |
| Second user with an edit share | co-edits live: the text reached the owner and the read-only viewer in about 100 ms |
| Share downgraded to read-only while open | the open editor switches to read-only |
| Share removed while open | the open editor loses access. Opening again is refused (`404`). |
| File changed outside the canvas (WebDAV PUT), then a save (`tests/browser/conflict-copy.sh`) | the save answers `409`, and OpenCanvas writes `<name> (conflict copy).ocanvas` into Nextcloud with the edit (PUT_RELATIVE) |

Commands, with the containers and OpenCanvas running as above:

```sh
PLAYWRIGHT=<e2e/node_modules/playwright> NC=http://localhost:8090 NC_PASS_ALICE=… NC_PASS_BOB=… NC_PASS_CAROL=… \
  node opencanvas/tests/browser/nextcloud.e2e.mjs        # RESULT: PASS (3 runs)
NC_PASS_ALICE=… NC_OC_API_KEY=… opencanvas/tests/browser/conflict-copy.sh   # PASS
```

Before the run, setup creates the users `alice`, `bob` and `carol` (`occ user:add`) and turns
off the first-run wizard (`occ app:disable firstrunwizard`). The test then logs in through
Nextcloud's own login page and makes shares through the files_sharing OCS API.

The downgrade and revoke rows failed before the role sync was added (`ShareDeletedEvent` listener plus the
`post_update_permissions` hook, which call `POST /v1/files/{WOPISrc}/role`): "still editable
10 s after the downgrade" and "… after the revoke". They pass with it. Turning the sync off
again (no `opencanvas_api_key`) brings back both failures.

**Without Nextcloud:**
- `php tests/run-without-phpunit.php`: 22 passed. Covers tokens, permission mapping, proof
  verification, UTF-7 conflict names and starter files. PHPUnit is not installed here; the same
  classes run under `phpunit -c phpunit.xml`.
- `OC_BIN=… tests/e2e/run.sh`: PASS. Runs a real OpenCanvas against a `php -S` harness of the
  app's core classes: PutFile, 409 then conflict copy, starters round-trip, unsigned call
  refused.

**The screens (NC-02), 2026-11-24.** Same setup, the front end built with `npm run build`.
`tests/browser/nextcloud-ui.e2e.mjs` drives them from the Files list in light and dark and saves
screenshots to `docs/prototypes/nextcloud-approved/screenshots/<frame>-<theme>.png`:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Files list (S2b) | `.ocanvas` rows show the canvas icon |
| + New (S1a) | "New canvas", "New database canvas", "New whiteboard canvas" last, after a separator |
| Name dialog (S1c-S1e) | default name selected without the extension; a clash and a "/" are refused in plain words, Create disabled; creating opens the canvas in the Viewer |
| "New canvas" | Nextcloud's own dialog creates the file and it opens in the Viewer |
| Click a canvas (S4a, S4b) | spinner, then OpenCanvas in the Viewer; an edit lands in the Nextcloud file |
| Row "…" (S6b) -> full page (S5a, S5e) | tab "Q1 launch plan - OpenCanvas - Nextcloud", "Files" back to the folder; phone layout moves Share into "…" |
| Full page "Share" (S5c, S8a) | opens the Files sidebar on Sharing, with "What this means in a canvas" |
| Unknown id (S5d) | "This canvas isn't available", tab "Canvas not found - OpenCanvas - Nextcloud" |
| 101 MB file (S13f) | "too large … this one is 101 MB", Download |
| OpenCanvas unreachable (S4g) | "Can't reach OpenCanvas", Try again |
| Not set up (S4h, S4i, S12a) | users: calm message; admins: "Open admin settings"; admin page: "Not connected yet" |
| Admin page (S12h, S12i, S12b) | an address without a scheme is refused before saving; Save, toast, check runs: 4 steps OK |
| Check failures (S12f, S12c) | WOPI base not on the allow-list: step 4 fails with the `wopi_allowlist` line; internal address dead: step 1 fails, the rest skipped |
| End all sessions (S12g) | asks first |
| "Can comment" (S8b) | with the admin switch on, the checkbox is in a view-only share's advanced settings and saves `opencanvas`/`comment` = true |
| Edit link (S7b, S7c) | name prompt, then the guest edits; the name is remembered on reload |
| View-only link (S7d) | no prompt, read only |
| Password link (S7a) | Nextcloud's password page, then the canvas. Before this change the app read an old session key (`public_link_authenticated_token`) and refused every unlocked link; Nextcloud 31 stores `public_link_authenticated_frontend` |
| Links turned off (S7f) | "This canvas can't be opened from a link … Ask alice to share it" |

```sh
npm run build
THEMES=light,dark PLAYWRIGHT=<e2e/node_modules/playwright> NC=http://localhost:8090 \
  NC_PASS_ADMIN=… NC_PASS_ALICE=… NC_PASS_BOB=… OC_PUBLIC=http://localhost:8480 \
  OC_INTERNAL=http://host.docker.internal:8480 node opencanvas/tests/browser/nextcloud-ui.e2e.mjs
```

Unit tests: `php tests/run-without-phpunit.php` 40 passed (adds launch errors, the public-link
password check and the connection-check report); `npm test` 51 passed (names, error screens,
postMessage bridge, admin validation, guest names, file icon).

**Search (SRCH-05), 2026-11-26.** (Since run in a real Nextcloud: see NC-03 below.) No Nextcloud container was available for this change, so
the Nextcloud glue (the migration, `IndexCanvasListener`, `SearchIndexService`,
`CanvasSearchProvider`, the `occ` command) is checked with `php -l` only. The framework-free
part is unit-tested: `php tests/run-without-phpunit.php` 46 passed (adds `SearchTextTest`:
reading `search.json` from a real zip, older and foreign files skipped, every-word matching with
the block, heading trail, accents and case, the title-only result, 5,000-line and 2 MB limits,
snippets); `bridge.test.js` covers `#block=` → `Action_ScrollToBlock`.

Manual test, with the containers and OpenCanvas 0.3 running as under **Verified**:

1. `occ app:enable opencanvas` (or `occ upgrade` from 0.1.0): `oc_opencanvas_search` exists.
2. As alice, create a canvas, type "Quarterly SSO rollout" under a heading "Release 4.2", wait
   for "Saved". In Nextcloud's database, `oc_opencanvas_search` has one row for the file id.
3. Header search "sso rollout": **Canvases** lists it with "Quarterly SSO rollout · Release 4.2";
   clicking opens the full page and the block flashes.
4. As bob (no share): the same search shows nothing. Share it read-only with bob: it shows.
   Remove the share: it is gone at once.
5. Delete the file: its row is gone. `occ opencanvas:search-index alice` on an old canvas after
   one save: "Indexed 1 canvases".

**Full run, scripted (NC-03), 2026-11-26.** `integrations/nextcloud/test/e2e.sh` (from the
repository root) does the whole setup itself: it starts `nextcloud:31-apache` (31.0.14, SQLite)
in Docker, copies this app in and enables it, adds alice and bob, starts an OpenCanvas built from
the checkout with a proof key, runs the connection check, then
`tests/browser/nextcloud-full.e2e.mjs` (Playwright Chromium), and removes the container
(`KEEP=1` leaves it). It runs in CI nightly and on manual dispatch (job `nextcloud-e2e`).

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| App listing (`/ocs/v2.php/cloud/apps/opencanvas`) | carries the LEGAL-01 trademark and not-affiliated line |
| Files > New > "New canvas", Nextcloud's name dialog | the file is created and opens in the Viewer |
| Start from a template, type a heading "Release 4.2" and a line | the owner edits; the save lands in the Nextcloud file |
| Unified search for the line | **Canvases** lists it as "Release plan …" with "<line> · Release 4.2", linked to `/apps/opencanvas/open/{id}#block=…`; `oc_opencanvas_search` has one row |
| bob, no share / read-only share | finds nothing / finds it, opens it view-only |
| Header search in the browser, click the hit | the full page opens at the block, scrolled into view |
| Delete through WebDAV (to the trash bin) | search finds nothing; the index row is gone |

Seen failing first and fixed: the hit's title was "Release plan ….ocanvas" (a canvas made in
Files is titled after its file name); titles now leave out `.ocanvas` (`SearchText::displayTitle`,
unit test). Local run: `integrations/nextcloud/test/e2e.sh` (needs Docker, Node 20+, pnpm,
cargo; `OC_BIN`, `PLAYWRIGHT`, `NC_PORT` 8490 and `OC_PORT` 8680 can be set).

The SRCH-05 manual steps below are covered by this run except `occ opencanvas:search-index`.

## Not yet tested

| What | Why |
|---|---|
| Talk: the 10-minute auto-discard and "no moderator present" in a real server, the error screen (5b), the sidebar tab (2c) and the floating call tile while a call runs on a phone (6b), the Post dialog in the sharing sidebar (1a; the run calls the same endpoints), Follow me scrolling followers' editors (the run checks the shared state) | Unit-tested (PHP `MeetingPolicyTest`, `MeetingServiceTest`; JS `talk.test.js`, `bridge.test.js`; editor `follow.test.ts`); not driven in the scripted run |
| Talk guests see a canvas link as a plain link preview, not the card | Nextcloud resolves references for signed-out readers only through public providers; guests never see shared files anyway (4b) |
| Proof rejected (S13d/e), access removed / deleted / conflict while open (S4e, S4f, S4l), session ending (S4j/k) | The Nextcloud side is unit-tested; these states were not driven in this run |
| Template picker with `.ocanvas` templates (S3) | Stock Nextcloud; without templates it skips the picker (S3c moot), as checked in Nextcloud 31's code |
| Group shares, folder shares, federated shares; MySQL/PostgreSQL Nextcloud; Nextcloud 30, 32, 36 | Not run |
| Members list from share recipients, @mention notifications | Not built: OpenCanvas WOPI mode has neither (gap G1 in DESIGN.md) |

## Limits

- **Viewer header.** Nextcloud's Viewer "…" menu can't take app entries, so "Open in full page" is
  in the Files row menu only; "View only"/"Download off" badges are in OpenCanvas's own bar.
- **File icon.** Nextcloud only resolves file-type icons from `core/img/filetypes`. The app shows
  its icon in the browser (Files, Viewer, public pages) without writing into core; places Nextcloud
  renders on the server (emails, activity) show the generic document icon.
- **Full page Share.** It opens the Files sidebar in Files (not beside the full-page canvas).

- **Mentions.** The @mention list is the people who have opened the canvas, not everyone it is
  shared with, and mentions send no Nextcloud notifications (OpenCanvas WOPI mode; DESIGN.md G1).
- **Sessions.** They last at most 10 h, then the canvas relaunches.
- **Images.** Pictures are stored inside the `.ocanvas`: 10 MB per image, 50 MB per file, files
  up to 100 MB.
- **Comment role.** Read-only shares get view, not comment, unless an admin turns on the comment
  role (DESIGN.md §5).
- **Versions (VH-01c).** Each autosave is a version; Nextcloud's expiry thins them out. The app
  advertises `OpenCanvas_SupportsVersions` and answers `GET {WOPISrc}/versions` and
  `{WOPISrc}/versions/{v}/contents` over `files_versions` (editors only), so the OpenCanvas history
  panel lists, previews, compares and restores them. A named or restore save (`X-COOL-WOPI-IsAutosave:
  false` + `X-OpenCanvas-Commit-Message`) sets the version's Nextcloud **label** and our metadata
  `opencanvas_kind` / `opencanvas_restored_from` (Nextcloud 29+, `IMetadataVersionBackend`; older
  servers keep the name only in the file's manifest). Authors are Nextcloud's own `author` metadata
  (the save runs as the editor). In-file history is off for this host by default (`[host.versions]
  file = false`, docs/05 §2).
- **Do labelled versions survive expiry?** Read from Nextcloud 31 `apps/files_versions/lib/Storage.php`
  (2026-11-24): labelled versions are skipped by the max-age expiry (`expireOlderThanMaxForUser`)
  and by the quota expiry loop in `expire()`, but **not** by its low-space fallback (oldest
  versions deleted until the quota fits, no label check), nor when a version has no database row.
  So named versions are kept in normal operation and can still go when a user runs out of space.
  Not yet confirmed in a running Nextcloud (the real-host pass for VH-01c is pending).
- **Locks.** None. An outside change to an open file produces a conflict copy.


# Element / Matrix

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/matrix.html
Source file: integrations/matrix/README.md

The canvas is a room widget, like Etherpad or Jitsi in Element. Everyone in the room opens the
same canvas from the widget bar and edits it live. A small bridge service is the OpenCanvas
host for Matrix.

- **Identity is checked, not taken from the URL.** The widget asks the Matrix client for an
  OpenID token, and the bridge confirms it with the user's own homeserver.
- **Only room members can open it.** A bot account reads the room's membership and power
  levels. Moderators (power level ≥ `state_default`) edit; everyone else gets
  `MX_MEMBER_ROLE` (default `edit`).
- **Leaving the room ends access.** When someone leaves, is kicked or is banned, the bot closes
  their open canvas right away through the OpenCanvas role API.
- **Names come from Matrix.** People appear under their room display names; the Matrix user id
  is the second line that tells two people with the same name apart.
- **The canvas is temporary.** It is deleted once everyone has left it and the idle grace has
  passed. People download or export it (PDF, Word, Markdown, `.ocanvas`) to keep it.
  Canvases stored in Matrix are planned for phase 2.
- **It is not end-to-end encrypted**, even in encrypted rooms (see Limits).

![Two people co-editing a canvas inside Element](evidence/element-coedit-asha.png)

## How it works

1. A room admin adds a widget state event (`im.vector.modular.widgets`) whose URL points at
   the bridge: `https://canvas-bridge.acme.example/widget?roomId=$matrix_room_id&wid=$matrix_widget_id`.
2. Element shows its own prompts: first "Widget added by …" consent for widgets added by
   someone else, then "Allow this widget to verify your identity".
3. The widget page (`bridge/public/`) answers Element's widget API handshake (it asks for no
   capabilities), requests an OpenID token (`get_openid`), and posts it to the bridge.
4. The bridge finds the user's homeserver by the Matrix server-name rules (`.well-known`, SRV,
   port 8448). It refuses any route that leads to a private, loopback or link-local address.
   It then calls `GET /_matrix/federation/v1/openid/userinfo` and accepts the answer only if
   the user belongs to that server.
5. The bot checks four things: it is still joined itself, the user is joined, the widget is in
   the room and points at this bridge, and the user's power level (which sets the role).
6. The bridge signs a 10-minute, single-use OpenCanvas launch token (HS256, `aud="opencanvas"`,
   `jti`). The canvas id is an opaque hash of room id and widget id, so OpenCanvas never sees
   the room id. The widget posts the token into a nested frame, so it never appears in a URL.
7. OpenCanvas opens the editor at `/app/?h=<host id>`. That page is allowed to be framed by the
   host's `frame_ancestors` (the Matrix client origins) and the bridge origin.

Design and research, with sources: [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md). Screens still waiting for a
prototype: [UI-SCREENS.md](UI-SCREENS.md).

## Install

You need OpenCanvas 0.1.2 or later for per-host `frame_ancestors` and `temporary_wording`, Node 24 for the bridge,
and a Matrix bot account.

1. **Bot account** on your homeserver, for example `@canvasbot:acme.example`. Log in once to
   get its access token and keep the token secret. The bot only reads room state; it never
   sends messages.
2. **OpenCanvas** `hosts.toml`:
   ```toml
   [[host]]
   id              = "acme-matrix"
   name            = "Matrix"
   mode            = "jwt"
   jwt_alg         = "HS256"
   jwt_secret      = "env:ACME_MATRIX_OC_SECRET"     # openssl rand -hex 32
   api_key         = "env:ACME_MATRIX_OC_API_KEY"    # openssl rand -hex 32
   storage         = "ephemeral"
   allowed_origins = ["https://canvas-bridge.acme.example"]
   # Every Matrix client origin your users open the widget from. They apply to this host's
   # editor only, not to the rest of the server.
   frame_ancestors = ["https://element.acme.example", "https://app.element.io"]
   [host.flags]
   temporary_wording = "room"   # room wording in the editor, "Start a new canvas" when it ends
   export_formats  = ["md", "html", "docx", "pdf", "ocanvas", "png"]

   [host.editor]
   profile         = "notebook"  # text, headings, lists, checklists, images, links, callouts
   ```
   A chat room's canvas is a shared notebook (links, notes, pictures people drop in), so the
   sample uses `notebook`. A room that runs meetings can use `"meeting"`; `"full"` offers every
   block. Profiles only trim the / menu: existing content of any type always opens and edits
   (docs/05 §2b).
3. **Bridge**: run it behind TLS, on its own origin.
   ```sh
   cd integrations/matrix/bridge
   PORT=8090 \
   MX_PUBLIC_URL=https://canvas-bridge.acme.example \
   OC_URL=https://canvas.acme.example \
   OC_HOST_ID=acme-matrix \
   OC_JWT_SECRET=<jwt_secret> \
   OC_API_KEY=<api_key> \
   MX_BOT_HOMESERVER_URL=https://matrix.acme.example \
   MX_BOT_ACCESS_TOKEN=<bot token> \
   MX_ALLOWED_SERVERS=acme.example \
   MX_BOT_AUTOJOIN=1 \
   node src/server.mjs
   ```

## Configure

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `PORT` | listen port (default 8090) |
| `MX_PUBLIC_URL` | the bridge's public URL; widget URLs must be `<MX_PUBLIC_URL>/widget?…` |
| `OC_URL` | OpenCanvas as browsers reach it |
| `OC_API_URL` | OpenCanvas as the bridge reaches it (default `OC_URL`) |
| `OC_HOST_ID`, `OC_JWT_SECRET` | the host `id` and `jwt_secret` (at least 32 characters) |
| `OC_API_KEY` | the host `api_key`; turns on closing access when people leave a room |
| `OC_TOKEN_TTL` | launch token lifetime, 60 to 3600 s (default 600) |
| `MX_BOT_HOMESERVER_URL`, `MX_BOT_ACCESS_TOKEN` | the bot's homeserver (Client-Server API base URL) and token |
| `MX_BOT_USER_ID` | optional; read with `whoami` when unset |
| `MX_BOT_AUTOJOIN=1` | join invites from allowed homeservers, leave the others |
| `MX_ALLOWED_SERVERS` | comma-separated homeservers whose users may open canvases; empty means any |
| `MX_PRIVATE_ALLOWED` | server names that may resolve to private addresses (an intranet homeserver) |
| `MX_FEDERATION_OVERRIDES` | JSON `{"server.name": "https://fixed-url"}`; operator-trusted, skips resolution |
| `MX_MEMBER_ROLE` | role for members below `state_default`: `edit` (default), `comment` or `view` |

Logs carry error codes only. Tokens and secrets are never printed.

## Add the canvas to a room

Each widget id is its own canvas. Use any of these three ways:

- **In Element**: `/addwidget https://canvas-bridge.acme.example/widget?roomId=$matrix_room_id&wid=$matrix_widget_id`,
  then `/invite @canvasbot:acme.example`, unless `MX_BOT_AUTOJOIN` is on and the bot was invited already.
- **Script**: this also invites the bot.
  ```sh
  MX_HOMESERVER_URL=https://matrix.acme.example MX_ACCESS_TOKEN=<your token> \
  MX_PUBLIC_URL=https://canvas-bridge.acme.example MX_BOT_USER_ID=@canvasbot:acme.example \
  node scripts/add-widget.mjs '!abc:acme.example' "Planning canvas"
  ```
- **By hand**: in Element, open `/devtools`, choose "Send custom state event", and send:
  ```json
  {
    "type": "im.vector.modular.widgets",
    "state_key": "opencanvas_1a2b3c",
    "content": {
      "type": "m.custom",
      "name": "Planning canvas",
      "url": "https://canvas-bridge.acme.example/widget?roomId=$matrix_room_id&wid=$matrix_widget_id",
      "data": { "title": "Temporary: download to keep a copy" },
      "waitForIframeLoad": true
    }
  }
  ```
  To pin it above the timeline for everyone, also send `io.element.widgets.layout` (empty state key) with
  `{"widgets": {"opencanvas_1a2b3c": {"container": "top", "index": 0, "width": 100, "height": 80}}}`.

**Element `config.json`:** nothing to add. Element has no setting that registers a widget
type or pre-trusts a widget URL.

## Errors (`POST /api/launch`)

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `BAD_REQUEST` | 400 | missing or malformed room id, widget id or token |
| `OPENID_INVALID` | 401 | the homeserver did not vouch for the token, or vouched for someone on another server |
| `SERVER_NOT_ALLOWED` | 403 | homeserver not in `MX_ALLOWED_SERVERS`, or it resolves to a private address |
| `NOT_MEMBER` | 403 | not joined to the room (checked before anything about the room's widgets) |
| `BOT_NOT_IN_ROOM` | 403 | the bot is not joined; invite it |
| `WIDGET_UNKNOWN` | 404 | no such canvas widget in the room |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | over 30 launches per minute from one address |
| `HOMESERVER_UNREACHABLE` | 502 | the user's or the bot's homeserver did not answer |

## Limits

- **Not end-to-end encrypted.** Canvas content goes over TLS to the OpenCanvas server, which
  keeps it while the canvas is open. The widget state event is room state, and Matrix never
  encrypts room state. Element warns about this in encrypted rooms.
- **Temporary only (v1).** A chat room lives much longer than a meeting. Tell people to
  export. Removing the widget does not end the canvas; it ends when idle.
- **Role changes** (power levels) apply at the next launch, at most 10 minutes later. Leaving,
  kicks and bans apply at once.
- **Every Matrix client origin must be listed** in `frame_ancestors`. A user whose client is
  not listed sees a blocked frame.
- **Avatars** are not passed to OpenCanvas: Matrix avatars are `mxc://` URLs behind
  authenticated media.
- Element X and the mobile apps do not show room widgets like this today.
- The widget's own screens (loading, the identity explanation, refused identity, errors) follow
  the approved prototype (MX-02). With `temporary_wording = "room"` the editor says the canvas is
  deleted after everyone has closed it, and its ended screen offers **Start a new canvas**, which
  reloads the widget.

## Status: verified vs not yet tested

**Verified on 2026-11-24, in a real Element Web with Synapse and OpenCanvas.**
`e2e/element-e2e.mjs` passed 17/17 in two consecutive runs. The setup was
`vectorim/element-web:latest` and `matrixdotorg/synapse:latest` in Docker, OpenCanvas 0.1.1
from this branch (`storage = "ephemeral"`, `frame_ancestors` set), and three Playwright
browser contexts:

- Asha Rao (room owner) opens the room in Element. Element sends the OpenID token, the bridge
  verifies it against Synapse's `openid/userinfo`, and the editor loads inside the widget.
- Ravi Menon (member) sees Element's "Widget added by Asha Rao" consent and the "Allow this
  widget to verify your identity" dialog, accepts both, and opens the same canvas.
- Text typed by each appears live for the other. The editors show "Asha Rao" and "Ravi Menon"
  (Matrix display names), not Matrix ids.
- Lena Ortiz (not in the room) adds a forged widget in her own room that names Asha's room and
  widget. The widget is refused with "Only members of this room can open the canvas." and no
  editor frame is created.
- Ravi leaves the room. The bot closes his live canvas connection (role API, 1 connection),
  Element removes the widget, and a fresh launch with his real OpenID token is refused
  (`NOT_MEMBER`). Asha's canvas stays open.
- Control run without `frame_ancestors`: the token is accepted but the editor frame is blocked
  (`frame-ancestors`), so the per-host setting is what makes the widget work.

Screenshots are in `evidence/`. Also verified:

- `cd bridge && npm test`: 21 unit tests (`node --test`). They cover the address guard,
  server-name resolution, OpenID success and failure, the allow-list, membership (including a
  bot that left, and a non-member asking for a forged widget), roles, launch claims, and the
  revoke on leave.
- `bridge/scripts/e2e-synapse.mjs`: the bridge's server side against Synapse and OpenCanvas,
  11/11.

To run the Element check yourself:

```sh
docker run --rm -v $PWD/hs:/data -e SYNAPSE_SERVER_NAME=hs.local -e SYNAPSE_REPORT_STATS=no matrixdotorg/synapse generate
docker run -d --name hs -v $PWD/hs:/data -p 127.0.0.1:8008:8008 matrixdotorg/synapse
# element.json: {"default_server_config": {"m.homeserver": {"base_url": "http://localhost:8008", "server_name": "hs.local"}}}
docker run -d --name element -v $PWD/element.json:/app/config.json:ro -p 127.0.0.1:8081:80 vectorim/element-web
# OpenCanvas on :18080 with the host above (allowed_origins ["http://localhost:8090"],
# frame_ancestors ["http://localhost:8081"]), then:
PLAYWRIGHT=<path to playwright/index.mjs> REG_SECRET=<registration_shared_secret> \
OC_JWT_SECRET=<jwt_secret> OC_API_KEY=<api_key> node e2e/element-e2e.mjs
```

**Not tested yet:**

- Real federation: users on a second homeserver, live `.well-known` and SRV lookups, and TLS
  on port 8448. Only the unit tests (with stubbed DNS) cover these.
- Encrypted rooms, popped-out widgets, and Element Desktop.
- Other Matrix clients and the mobile apps.
- `MX_BOT_AUTOJOIN` against a live server (the runs joined the bot through the API), and
  `scripts/add-widget.mjs` against a live server.
- Power-level changes during a session; they apply at the next launch.


# Mattermost

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/mattermost.html
Source file: integrations/mattermost/README.md

A Mattermost plugin that adds collaborative canvases to channels:

- **Create a canvas** from the channel header or with `/canvas new [title]`. A card is posted in
  the channel, and everyone in the channel can open it and edit it live.
- **Meeting notes** with `/canvas notes [title]`: a canvas that starts with Agenda, Notes,
  Decisions and Action items.
- **Workspace panel:** canvases open in Mattermost's right-hand panel, which can be expanded.
- **Stored in Mattermost.** The plugin is the OpenCanvas *host*. It keeps each `.ocanvas` file
  in Mattermost's file store and the list of canvases in the plugin key-value store. OpenCanvas
  keeps nothing once a canvas is closed.
- **Access follows the channel.** Channel members edit. Someone who leaves the channel loses
  access at once, even with the canvas open. Guests get the role you choose (default: none).

> **Status: alpha.** The server plugin is complete and was tested end to end in Mattermost
> 12.1.0. The webapp follows the screens approved on 2026-11-24 (MM-02): the card, the panel and
> its states, the create dialog and the slash replies; they follow your Mattermost theme. New
> canvases open on the page, not the template picker (the plugin sends `"start": "page"`).
> Design and security details: [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

*Nextcloud is a registered trademark of Nextcloud GmbH. Mattermost is a trademark of Mattermost, Inc. OpenCanvas is an independent open-source project, not affiliated with or endorsed by either company.*

## How it works

1. **Create.** The plugin checks that you can edit in the channel, saves a canvas record and
   posts a `custom_opencanvas` card as you. Mobile apps, notifications and search show the
   card's text: "Canvas: <title> (open it in the Mattermost web or desktop app)".
2. **Open.** Clicking **Open** asks the plugin for a launch token. The plugin checks that you
   are a channel member and signs a short-lived token (HS256, 10 minutes by default, single use)
   with your name, the channel's members and your role. The panel posts the token to OpenCanvas
   in a form, so it never appears in a URL.
3. **Load and save.** OpenCanvas calls the plugin back under
   `/plugins/com.casualoffice.opencanvas/oc`: `GET` to load the file, `PUT` to save it (autosave),
   plus assets, members and conflict copies. Each save is a new file in the channel's file
   storage; the plugin keeps the version and the last 50 saves.
4. **Callback security.** The plugin accepts a callback only with a valid
   `X-OpenCanvas-Signature` v2 (HMAC-SHA256 over time, method, path, query and body, within 5
   minutes). Mattermost removes the `Authorization` header before a plugin sees a request, so
   OpenCanvas also sends the callback token as `X-OpenCanvas-Callback-Token` (OpenCanvas 0.1.2 or later); the plugin checks that it belongs to the same canvas. Mattermost also re-sorts the
   query string, which the plugin allows for.
5. **Access changes.** When someone leaves a channel, the plugin tells OpenCanvas (role API,
   `none`), which closes their open canvas at once. When someone joins, the @mention list is
   refreshed.

| Who | Role in the channel's canvases |
|---|---|
| Channel member | edit |
| Guest account that is a channel member | the **Guest access** setting: none (default), view, comment or edit |
| Anyone else, bots, deactivated accounts | none: no token, the card says "You don't have access" |

In a **public channel**, any team member can join, and Mattermost joins them automatically when
they open the channel. Joining gives edit access, the same as reading and posting. Use a private
channel for canvases that only some people may edit.

## Requirements

- Mattermost 9.11 or later (tested: 12.1.0 Team Edition), web or Desktop app.
- OpenCanvas 0.1.x, reachable from browsers and from the Mattermost server. Version 0.1.2 and later also
  send the callback token header (older versions work with signature-only checks).
- To build: Go 1.24.3 or later, Node 20 or later.

## Build

```sh
integrations/mattermost/build.sh        # tests, Linux binaries (amd64, arm64), webapp, bundle
# -> integrations/mattermost/dist/com.casualoffice.opencanvas-0.1.0.tar.gz
```

Parts: `cd server/canvas && go test ./...`, `cd server && go test ./...`,
`cd webapp && npm ci && npm run check && npm run build && npm test`.

## Install

1. Generate two secrets: `openssl rand -hex 32` (shared secret) and `openssl rand -hex 32`
   (API key).
2. Install the bundle: **System Console → Plugins → Plugin Management → Upload Plugin**
   (needs `PluginSettings.EnableUploads`), or `mmctl plugin add <bundle>.tar.gz`. Then enable
   **OpenCanvas**.
3. Fill in the plugin settings (below).
4. Add Mattermost to OpenCanvas `hosts.toml` (below) and restart OpenCanvas.
5. In a channel: `/canvas new Sprint 42`, then click **Open** on the card.

### Plugin settings

**System Console → Plugins → OpenCanvas:**

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| OpenCanvas URL | `https://canvas.example.com` (what browsers open) |
| OpenCanvas API URL | only if the Mattermost server reaches OpenCanvas at another address |
| Host id | `mattermost` |
| Shared secret | the first secret |
| Callback secret | empty, unless `hosts.toml` sets `callback_secret` |
| API key | the second secret |
| Guest access | No access, View, Comment or Edit |
| Launch token lifetime | 10 (minutes, 1 to 60) |

A wrong value turns the plugin's endpoints off (`503 NOT_CONFIGURED`) and the server log names
the setting, never its value.

### OpenCanvas hosts.toml

```toml
[[host]]
id              = "mattermost"
name            = "Mattermost"
mode            = "jwt"
jwt_alg         = "HS256"
jwt_secret      = "env:MM_OC_SECRET"      # the shared secret
api_key         = "env:MM_OC_API_KEY"     # the API key
callback_base   = "https://chat.acme.example/plugins/com.casualoffice.opencanvas/oc"
allowed_origins = ["https://chat.acme.example"]
[host.flags]
on_conflict     = "copy"
```

`callback_base` is your Mattermost Site URL, with its subpath if it has one, followed by
`/plugins/com.casualoffice.opencanvas/oc`. Mattermost needs no CSP change: it sends no
`frame-src`, so the OpenCanvas frame is allowed.

## Endpoints

| Path under `/plugins/com.casualoffice.opencanvas` | Caller | Authentication |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` and `PUT /oc/files/{id}`, `POST /oc/files/{id}/copies`, `POST /oc/files/{id}/assets`, `GET /oc/files/{id}/assets/{assetId}`, `GET /oc/files/{id}/members`, `POST /oc/access` | OpenCanvas | `X-OpenCanvas-Signature` v2, plus `X-OpenCanvas-Callback-Token` when sent |
| `POST /api/v1/canvases`, `POST /api/v1/canvases/{id}/launch`, `GET /api/v1/channels/{id}/canvases`, `GET /api/v1/canvases/{id}/assets/{assetId}` | Mattermost webapp | Mattermost session |

## Limits

- 100 MB per canvas file, 10 MB per image or attachment.
- Titles: one line, at most 120 characters.
- The launch token lists up to 500 members; larger channels use the members callback, which
  reads up to 5,000 people.
- Mobile apps show the card as text only (Mattermost mobile runs no plugin UI).
- The Desktop app may refuse clipboard writes from the canvas frame unless the OpenCanvas origin
  is trusted in the Desktop app settings.
- Each save keeps a new file in Mattermost's file storage. The plugin remembers the last 50 per
  canvas; older files are not deleted yet.
- Guest accounts need a Mattermost license (not available in Team Edition).

## Test checklist

- [ ] The plugin enables without errors.
- [ ] `/canvas new Test` posts a card; a second member opens it; edits appear for both.
- [ ] `/canvas notes` opens with Agenda, Notes, Decisions and Action items.
- [ ] After closing and reopening, the edits are still there (`.ocanvas` files appear in the
      channel's storage).
- [ ] Removing a member from the channel closes their open canvas.
- [ ] Someone outside a private channel cannot open its canvas.
- [ ] `grep` for the shared secret in the Mattermost and OpenCanvas logs finds nothing.

## Status: verified vs not yet tested

**Verified in a real Mattermost (2026-11-24):** Mattermost Team Edition 12.1.0 (official image,
amd64 emulated on Apple silicon) with PostgreSQL 16, OpenCanvas built from this branch, and two
signed-in browser users (Playwright, Chromium). Compose file: `e2e/docker-compose.yml`.

- The bundle installs with `mmctl plugin add` and enables. Settings were applied with
  `mmctl config patch`.
- Create through the plugin API: `201`, with a `custom_opencanvas` card posted in the channel for
  both a canvas and meeting notes. A non-member trying to create gets `403 NO_ACCESS`.
- Launch: `200`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. The token has `iss mattermost`, `aud opencanvas`,
  role `edit`, a 600 s lifetime, a 32-character `jti`, user `Alice Doe` / `@alice`, the channel
  as context, and the channel members. OpenCanvas accepts it (`303`); replaying the same token is
  refused (`401`). A non-member's launch gets `404 NO_ACCESS`.
- In the browser: the card's **Open** opens the panel with the editor. Text typed by one user
  shows up for the second user live, and the second user sees the first by name. Meeting notes
  open with their sections. Switching from one canvas to another in the panel works.
- Callbacks, recorded by a pass-through between OpenCanvas and Mattermost:
  - `GET` and `PUT /oc/files/{id}` and `GET …/members` reached the plugin with
    `x-opencanvas-signature` and `x-opencanvas-callback-token` and were answered `200`.
  - Autosave versions 1 and 2 were stored as `.ocanvas` files in the channel's file storage.
- Bad callbacks are refused with `401`: wrong key, a timestamp 10 minutes old, no signature, a
  v1-only signature, and a forged callback token.
- Removing a member from the channel while their canvas was open: OpenCanvas logged "role changed
  by host … none" and their editor showed the loss of access within seconds.
- Neither log contains the shared secret.

Bugs that run found, now fixed:

- Mattermost re-sorts the query string, so the members callback failed its signature check
  (`TestSignatureSurvivesQueryReordering`, seen failing first).
- The webapp bundle loaded its own `react` instead of Mattermost's (`npm test` bundle check, seen failing first).
- Switching canvases in the panel did nothing. Fixed in the placeholder panel with one stable
  frame name; checked in the browser run, no unit test.

**Unit tests:** `server/canvas` 15 tests (token claims, signatures against OpenCanvas's own
reference vector, membership roles, load/save with `If-Match` and `Idempotency-Key`, assets
scoped to their canvas, conflict copies, revocation, the callback token header);
`server` 2 tests; OpenCanvas `callback_token_also_sent_in_its_own_header`.

**MM-02 webapp, verified 2026-11-24** in Mattermost 12.1.0 with two signed-in users in the light
theme (`e2e/setup.sh`, then `MAIN_ONLY=1 node e2e/mm-e2e.mjs`, 13/13): the App Bar's Create canvas
opens the dialog (placeholder "Untitled canvas", meeting notes default title, the channel note,
busy Create); the new canvas opens in the panel on its page with no template picker; the second
user sees the card (title, "Canvas · Edited …", Open on the title row, the menu with Download
greyed "Later"), Copy link without clipboard permission shows the link selected, clicking the card
body opens the panel, the card gets its ring, and the first user's text shows live; the canvas
follows the Mattermost theme. Screenshots: `docs/prototypes/mattermost-approved/real-host/`.
Built but not checked in the real host: the dark theme, S2 error states (no access, not set up,
unreachable, closed + Reopen), expanded view, rename, `/canvas notes` opening the panel, the
channel canvases list (S4), the System Console help text (S6) and the Desktop app (S7).

**Not yet tested:**

- **Guest accounts.** Team Edition has no guests ("Your license does not support guest
  accounts"). The guest rules are unit-tested only.
- **A non-member in the browser.** Public channels add the visitor automatically, so this was
  tested through the API (`404`), not with a private channel in the browser.
- Images and attachments in a canvas, conflict copies and very large channels, in a real run.
- The channel header button: it works through the same create API, but it was not clicked.
- Mattermost Desktop, mobile, a subpath Site URL, high availability.
- Upgrading to the current plugin SDK (v0.6.x needs Go 1.26); built with v0.1.15.


# Protocol and build contract

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/protocol.html
Source file: docs/15-BUILD-CONTRACT.md

**Status:** binding for the P1 build, 2026-11-21. If a builder needs to change
anything here, they update this file and say so in their report.

## 1. Repository layout

```
Cargo.toml                 Rust workspace
crates/oc-model            .ocanvas zip read/write, Yjs doc helpers, markdown/html export
crates/oc-server           axum binary `opencanvas`: config, host connector, store, rooms, autosave, routes
migrations/sqlite|mysql    identical logical schema (docs/04 §5)
web/packages/ui            design tokens (tokens.css) + shared TS types (BlockEnv, OcUser, Role)
web/packages/editor        Vite + React app: shell, Tiptap editor, gallery, comments, mobile bar
web/packages/database      React database block (table / board / calendar / gallery, CSV)
web/packages/board         React whiteboard block
examples/sample-host       Node reference host (JWT signing + callbacks + file store)
examples/wopi-host         Node reference WOPI host (CheckFileInfo/GetFile/PutFile/PutRelative)
```

The server serves the built editor (`web/packages/editor/dist`) at `/app/`.
`OC_WEB_DIR` overrides the path.

## 2. Launch flow

1. Host page form-POSTs `token=<JWT>` to `POST /v1/launch`.
2. Server verifies the JWT (docs/05 §3, HS256 via the host's `jwt_secret`), creates
   a session row, and answers `303 See Other` → `/app/#t=<ticket>`.
   (The ticket goes in the fragment so it never appears in server logs or Referer headers.)
   `GET /v1/launch?token=` does the same, for hosts that use a plain iframe `src`.
3. The SPA reads `#t`, calls `GET /v1/sessions/<ticket>` → `200`:
   ```json
   { "ticket":"01J…", "room":"r_7k…", "role":"edit",
     "user": {"id":"u_123","name":"Asha Rao","color":"#7a45f0","avatar":null},
     "file": {"id":"doc_8812","name":"Sprint 42 notes"},
     "host": {"id":"acme","name":"Acme"},
     "perms": {"export":true,"download":true,"comment":true,"print":true,"history":true,"restore":true,"commitMessage":true},
     "history": "full", "historySource": "host", "historyHostName": "Acme",
     "isNew": true,
     "ai": {"enabled":true,"modes":["edit","comment","answer"],"mcp":false},
     "import": {"formats":["md","html","csv"]},
     "blocks": [],
     "editor": {"profile":"full","allowProfileSwitch":false,"blocks":["core.text","…"],"quickInsert":[],
                "features":{"comments":true,"versionHistory":true,"ai":true,"diagramming":true,"templates":true,"import":true}},
     "wsUrl": "ws://localhost:8080/v1/collab" }
   ```
   *(EDP-01)* `editor`: the host's profile (docs/05 §2b), `blocks` the ids insertion surfaces may
   offer (`core.*` and SDK types; `core.text` always), `quickInsert`, and `features` after the
   aliases (`ai` and `import` are the host-level switches, server settings included; `ai`,
   `import` and `perms` above stay what this person may actually use). The editor filters every
   insertion surface through one function (`editor/profile.ts`); an absent `editor` (older
   server) means everything. Content of any type always loads and stays editable.
   *(BSDK-01)* `blocks`: the SDK block packages `[host.blocks]` enables, each
   `{type, version, v, title, icon, description, content, attrs, data, export, migrations, entry,
   integrity}` (docs/05 §2a; `v` is the data version the package writes, its SemVer major).
   *(VH-01a)*: `history` `full` | `link` | `none`, `historySource` `host` | `file` (the list shown
   first), `historyHostName`, and in link mode `historyUrl` + `historyPostMessage` (docs/05 §5a).
   `perms.history`, `perms.restore`, `perms.commitMessage` are effective (the role included).
   `ai` (AI-02): `enabled` when `[host.ai] enabled = true` and the role is not `view`; `modes` are
   the run modes the server accepts for the role (`edit`: `edit`, `comment`, `answer`; `comment`:
   `answer`, `comment`; `view`: none); `mcp` mirrors `[host.ai] mcp`. The editor shows the
   assistant from this; `?ai=1` only turns it on when `ai` is absent (demo, dev).
   `isNew` is true when the host returned 404 / an empty file. The SPA then shows
   the template gallery. *(0.4.1, PSYNC-BUG-2)* The answer waits at most 250 ms for the room to
   open; for a canvas that takes longer to read (a large file) `isNew` is `null`, and the room
   sends control `{"t":"room","isNew":bool}` on the socket right after its sync step 1 (every
   join sends it), before the first sync completes. A host error that takes longer than the wait
   closes the socket (1011) instead of failing the session.
   *(docs/21 revision 2)*: `user` is `{id, name, color, avatar, detail?}`, never an e-mail. A `GET`
   lifts a role-API revoke for that viewer (a fresh token means access). `401 {"error":{"code":"TICKET_INVALID"}}` when unknown or expired.
   (Implementation: `isNew` = the room's doc has no `content` and empty `meta`/`databases`/`boards`,
   so a second user joining after a template was picked gets `false`.)
   Launch failures answer `401 {"error":{"code":"TOKEN_INVALID"|"TOKEN_REUSED",…}}`; `jti` is
   single-use per host (table `launch_jti`). The algorithm is pinned by the host entry
   (`jwt_alg` = `HS256` with `jwt_secret`, or `RS256`/`EdDSA` with `jwt_public_key` PEM or
   `jwt_jwks_url`; JWKS is cached 10 min, the token's `kid` must match a key whose type fits
   `jwt_alg`, an unknown `kid` refetches at most every 30 s), `aud` must be
   `opencanvas`, `iss` the host id, `exp` at most 10 h ahead, `nbf` honoured, 30 s leeway.
   **WOPI launch** (docs/05 §6, added 2026-11-21): `POST /v1/launch?WOPISrc=<urlencoded>` with form
   `access_token` (+ `access_token_ttl`, ms since the epoch) for a host with `mode = "wopi" | "both"`
   whose `wopi_allowlist` admits the URL (else `403 WOPISRC_NOT_ALLOWED`); CheckFileInfo decides
   role, user and perms (`401 TOKEN_INVALID` when it answers 4xx). Same `303`. The ticket lives
   until `access_token_ttl` (10 h when absent). `GET /hosting/discovery` (XML) and
   `GET /hosting/capabilities` (JSON). A JWT for a `mode = "wopi"` host is refused.
   **Open at a block** (UX-02): a `block` form field (or `?block=` query) on either launch adds
   `&block=<id>` to the fragment (`/app/#t=<ticket>&block=<id>`) when it matches
   `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}`; the editor scrolls to that block and flashes it.
4. Tickets live for the launch token's `exp`. The WS must connect within 60 s of the
   first `GET /v1/sessions`, though reconnects with the same ticket are allowed until `exp`.

## 3. Collaboration WebSocket

`GET /v1/collab/<room>?ticket=<ticket>[&caps=ext,live,subdoc]`, upgraded to a WebSocket. This is compatible
with the stock `y-websocket` `WebsocketProvider(wsUrl, room, doc, { params: { ticket } })`.

*(BSDK-02)* `caps` lists client capabilities, comma-separated. `ext`: the client keeps `extBlock`
nodes (§4.2); the 0.2 editor always sends it. Editors before 0.2 bind the document with
y-prosemirror against a schema without `extBlock`, and y-prosemirror deletes nodes its schema
lacks. So an update from a connection **without** `caps=ext` that lowers the number of `extBlock`s
is refused (auth frame `this editor is out of date; reopen the canvas`) and the socket is closed
with **4426** `"editor out of date: reopen the canvas"` (0.1.x clients treat 4400-4499 as final
and show their ended screen; reopening loads the current editor). Nothing else changes for such
connections. Headless CRDT clients that delete SDK blocks must send `caps=ext`.

*(LIVE-02, ADR-071)* `live`: the client keeps `liveBlock` and `blockRef` nodes (§4.4); editors from
0.3 send `caps=ext,live`. The same rule: an update from a connection without `caps=live` that
lowers the number of those nodes is refused and closed with **4426**, so a 0.2 editor sharing the
room loses nothing. Every update is also held to the live block rules: adding a reference needs
`[host.flags] live_blocks` and the grant's `perms.live`; the document may not newly break the depth
rule, the 50-reference limit or `[host.live] snapshot` (auth frame naming the rule). A live block
room's ticket comes from `POST /v1/live/session` (§6); at most `[host.live] max_open` (≤ 8) of them
are connected per parent session, the next upgrade answers `429 LIVE_LIMIT`. In a live room the
server stamps each awareness state of a derived session with `from: {fileId, title}` (the embedding
canvas; a client's own `from` is dropped) and sends it only to viewers whose session comes from that
same canvas; everyone else gets the state without `from`.

Binary frames, y-protocols encoding (lib0 varuint message type first):

| type | meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | sync: 0 = step1, 1 = step2, 2 = update |
| 1 | awareness update |
| 2 | auth: the server sends `[2, 0 (permission denied), varString reason]` when a write is rejected |
| 3 | query awareness (client → server; the server answers with all awareness states) |
| 100 | OpenCanvas control: varString JSON, both directions |
| 101 | subdocument (PSYNC-02, §3.2): varUint8Array of (varString guid, one y-protocols message) |

(Changed 2026-11-21 by the server build: auth is type **2** and query-awareness is 3, as in
y-protocols / y-websocket and yrs. The earlier draft said 3 for auth.)

Server → client control JSON:
`{"t":"saving"}`, `{"t":"saved","at":<epoch ms>,"version":"18"}`,
`{"t":"save_error","retryInMs":10000,"message":"…"}`,
`{"t":"conflict","policy":"copy","fileId":"doc_9001","url":"…"}` (room stays read-only; joiners
get it as the save state),
`{"t":"conflict","policy":"reload"}` (followed by `closed` and close code 1012: the client must
drop its local Y.Doc and reconnect, the room now holds the host's version),
`{"t":"role","role":"view"}` (also sent mid-session when the host changes the role),
`{"t":"closed","reason":"…"}` (`access revoked` → close 1008; `closed by the host` → close 1000),
`{"t":"ping"}` (heartbeat every `OC_HEARTBEAT_MS`, default 10 s, on every connection; clients
treat 15 s without any frame as a lost connection, docs/06 §5; added 2026-11-21, UX-02),
`{"t":"restored","by","byName","from","name","at","restoreId"}` (VH-01b: someone restored a version; the
edit itself arrives as an ordinary update, docs/30 §5),
`{"t":"reconnect"}` (always followed by close **1012**: the client keeps its Y.Doc and
reconnects; sent on graceful drain and, in cluster mode, when the room moved to another node).
(Changed 2026-11-21 by the server hardening: `conflict` carries `policy`.)
On connect the server sends sync step1 and the current awareness states. When the client's
step1 arrives the server answers with step2, then `{"t":"role",…}` and the current save state
(`saved` with the last known host version, or `saving`). Client → server control messages are
accepted and ignored for now.

Server rules:
- `view` role: sync step2 and update messages are dropped, and an auth frame is sent once.
- `comment` role: an update is accepted only if it touches nothing but the `comments` root
  (applied to a scratch copy of the doc first; updates that create other roots or cannot fully
  integrate are refused). The auth frame is sent once per connection.
- Awareness: the server rewrites the `user` field from the grant before fan-out
  (`{"id","name","color","avatar","detail"?}`), so nobody can spoof another person's name or colour.
  *(docs/21 revision 2)* Every recipient gets the same states: real names for everyone with access.
  Entries over 2 KB, or for a client id owned by another connection, are dropped.
- An update that would push the encoded doc over `OC_MAX_DOC_MB` (20) is refused with an auth
  frame `document size limit reached`; while a conflict is being handled every write is refused.
- Frames over `OC_MAX_FRAME_KB` (1024) close the socket with code 1009. More than 60 non-awareness
  frames/s (burst 120) closes it with **4429** `"rate limit"` (not 1008, which only means access
  revoked / session expired). Awareness frames (type 1) have their own bucket of 120/s (burst 240);
  excess awareness frames are dropped silently, never fatal. Clients should still batch (y-websocket
  awareness throttling, 50 ms update windows).
  (Changed 2026-11-21: was 1008 with awareness counted against the same bucket; fast typing tripped it.) When the ticket expires the server sends
  `{"t":"closed","reason":"session expired"}` and closes with 1008; on shutdown (SIGTERM drain)
  it commits dirty rooms, then sends `{"t":"reconnect"}` and closes with 1012.
  (Changed 2026-11-21 by CLU-01: was `{"t":"closed","reason":"server shutting down"}`.)
- Cluster mode (ADR-006): the socket may land on any node. A node that does not own the room
  relays it to the owner over an internal WebSocket; the protocol above is unchanged, roles
  are enforced by the owner. If the owner dies the client gets `reconnect` + 1012 (or a
  dropped socket) and reconnects with the same ticket.
- Room ids are `r_` + 26 lowercase base32 chars of sha256(`<hostId>:<fileId>`).

### 3.1 AI control messages (AI-02, ADR-034; docs/24 §10)

Client → server (type 100 JSON); answers go only to the sending connection:

| Message | Who | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `{"t":"ai-run","runId","prompt","selection"?,"selectionBlockIds"?,"mode"?,"confirm"?}` | `edit`: modes `edit` (default), `comment`, `answer`; `comment`: `answer` (default) and `comment` only; `view`: refused | Starts a run on the room owner node. `runId` is chosen by the client, `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}`, unique per room. `selectionBlockIds` (optional; one per selection line, or one for the whole selection) only places injection flags. `confirm` (boolean; default `true` in mode `edit`, ignored otherwise): the run stops after `ai-plan` and calls no tool (so writes nothing) until `ai-approve` |
| `{"t":"ai-approve","runId"}` | the user who started the run | Lets a run waiting on its plan act ("Nothing changes until you run it"). Ignored for any other run, user or state. Without it the wait ends after 10 minutes: outcome `cancelled`, `reason: "plan_timeout"`; the run's time limit starts on approval |
| `{"t":"ai-cancel","runId"}` | the user who started the run | Aborts the model call or the wait for approval; the current tool call finishes; outcome `cancelled` |
| `{"t":"ai-undo","runId"}` | the user who started the run | Reverts every change made with origin `ai:<runId>` (once; in memory, lost if the room moves) |
| `{"t":"automation-undo","runId","ruleId"}` | an editor | *(AUTO-06, frame 3a)* Reverts every change of that automation run (transaction origin `automation:<ruleId>#<runId>`, the newest 50 runs, in memory); the undo starts no rule. The server sends `{"t":"automation-ran","runId","ruleId","text"}` to the connections of the person whose change started a run that changed the canvas |

Server → client:

| Message | When |
|---|---|
| `{"t":"ai-plan","runId","plan":[{"n","text","kind"}],"awaitingApproval","flags"}` | After the plan call (modes `comment` and `edit`). `plan` is the steps in order, `n` from 1, `kind` one of `create`, `update`, `suggest`, `read` (a server-side classification of the step text; the panel marks `suggest` steps). `awaitingApproval: true` when the run waits for `ai-approve`. `flags` (always present, often empty): prompt-injection flags on the selection, see below |
| `{"t":"ai-step","runId","step","tool","ok","error"?,"flags"?}` | After each tool call; `error` is a code (`not_allowed`, `forbidden`, `bad_input`, `not_found`, `stale`, `confirmation_required`, `internal`). `flags` when a read tool returned instruction-like content |
| `{"t":"ai-done","runId","outcome","summary"?,"reason"?,"steps","writes","undoable","usage":{"input","output"},"flags"?}` | `outcome`: `done`, `cancelled` (`reason: "plan_timeout"` when approval never came), `limit` (`reason`: `steps`, `time`, `tokens`, `writes`, `quota`), `error`, `refused` (with `reason`), `undone` |

**Prompt-injection flags** (docs/24 §9.1 T1). The server scans the content a run reads (the
selection before the plan, then every read tool's result) with a deterministic heuristic for
text addressed to the assistant: "ignore previous/your instructions", "disregard the above",
"you are now", "send/email/post/forward this … to …", a line starting with a speaker label
(`assistant:`, `AI,`, `Claude:`, `system:`), and system-prompt markers (`system prompt`,
`<|im_start|>`, `[INST]`, `<<SYS>>`, a stray `</canvas_data>`). Each hit is
`{"blockId": string|null, "kind": "instruction_in_content", "excerpt"}` (the matched line, at
most 120 characters; `blockId` null for a whole-page read or an unplaced selection line), at
most 20 per message. `ai-done.flags` is every flag of the run. Detection **never blocks the run
and never changes what the model gets**: the content is still sent as data inside
`<canvas_data>` and tool results, and the system prompt still says it is never an instruction.
The panel shows one note on the plan or answer card when flags exist. The excerpt goes only to
