import { OpenCanvas } from "@opencanvas/client"; const secret = new TextEncoder().encode(process.env.ACME_OC_SECRET!); async function mintUserToken(userId: string, scope: string, files: string[]): Promise<string> { return new SignJWT({ scope, role: "edit", files }) .setProtectedHeader({ alg: "HS256" }) .setIssuer("acme") .setAudience("https://canvas.example.com/api/v1") .setSubject(userId) .setIssuedAt() .setExpirationTime("10m") .sign(secret); } // The token callback runs before every request, so a long job never sends an expired token. const oc = new OpenCanvas({ baseUrl: "https://canvas.example.com", auth: { token: () => mintUserToken("u_42", "canvas:read canvas:comment", ["doc_1"]) }, }); const { threads } = (await oc.listComments({ fileId: "doc_1" })) as { threads: unknown[] }; // jsonwebtoken = "9", serde_json = "1" use jsonwebtoken::{encode, EncodingKey, Header}; use opencanvas_client::{Auth, Client}; use serde_json::json; fn mint_user_token(secret: &[u8], user_id: &str, scope: &str, files: &[&str]) -> String { let now = std::time::SystemTime::now() .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH) .unwrap() .as_secs(); let claims = json!({ "iss": "acme", "aud": "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1", "sub": user_id, "scope": scope, "role": "edit", "files": files, "iat": now, "exp": now + 600, }); encode(&Header::default(), &claims, &EncodingKey::from_secret(secret)).expect("signed") } let secret = std::env::var("ACME_OC_SECRET").expect("ACME_OC_SECRET"); let token = mint_user_token(secret.as_bytes(), "u_42", "canvas:read canvas:comment", &["doc_1"]); let oc = Client::builder("https://canvas.example.com") .auth(Auth::Token(token)) .build(); let threads = oc.list_comments("doc_1", None).await?; # pip install pyjwt requests import os import time import jwt import requests def mint_user_token(user_id: str, scope: str, files: list[str]) -> str: now = int(time.time()) claims = { "iss": "acme", "aud": "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1", "sub": user_id, "scope": scope, "role": "edit", "files": files, "iat": now, "exp": now + 600, } return jwt.encode(claims, os.environ["ACME_OC_SECRET"], algorithm="HS256") token = mint_user_token("u_42", "canvas:read canvas:comment", ["doc_1"]) r = requests.get( "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/comments", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}, timeout=30, ) r.raise_for_status()

## Scopes

A token's scope is a ceiling: the operation's x-opencanvas-scope in the OpenAPI document must be within it, or the answer is 403 SCOPE_REQUIRED . Each scope includes the ones above it. Scope Allows Least role Operations canvas:read Read canvases, blocks, databases, boards, comments and members; export; stream events; a sync ticket with the view role. view readFile , listBlocks , getBlock , findBlocks , listDatabases , getDatabase , queryRows , readBoard , listComments , listMembers , exportFile , renderFile , listReferences , streamEvents , createSyncToken , convert , extract , search , listAutomations , listAutomationRuns , listBacklinks , getGraph canvas:comment Everything canvas:read allows, and start or reply to comment threads. comment addComment canvas:write Everything canvas:comment allows, and change blocks, databases and boards, and import. canvas:write:direct counts as canvas:write . edit batchBlocks , createDatabase , upsertRows , addField , createBoard , addShapes , makeLive , importFile , testAutomation , saveAutomation , deleteAutomation , enableAutomation canvas:admin Save now, change a user's role, close the session, drop cached members. Counts for tokens only when the host sets [host.api] token_admin = true ; otherwise these are the host key's. host key, or a token with canvas:admin commitFile , setRole , closeSession , invalidateMembers , offlineRevoke

## Roles

The effective permission is min(scope, role) . A canvas:write token does not let a view user write, and a canvas:read token does not let an editor write. Where the role comes from. If you implement the optional POST /access callback, OpenCanvas asks it for the user's role on each file a call touches (cached 30 seconds, dropped by the role API) and ignores the token's role claim; none refuses every operation. Without it, the role claim counts, but only for the files listed in files ( 403 FILES_REQUIRED otherwise, unless [host.api] all_files = true ). Revocation. After POST /api/v1/files/{fileId}/role with "role": "none" , the user's next call is refused, and their event streams close with code 4003 . The host key acts with the edit role on every file, plus the admin operations.

## Expiry

Tokens live at most 15 minutes: an exp further ahead than that is refused ( 401 TOKEN_INVALID ). An expired token answers 401 TOKEN_EXPIRED ; an event stream opened with a token closes with code 4001 when it expires. Mint a fresh token per job or per request: the clients take a token callback that runs before every request.

## Errors

Status Code When 401 UNAUTHENTICATED No credentials, an unknown host, or a wrong host key. 401 TOKEN_INVALID Signature, issuer, audience, a lifetime over 15 minutes, not yet valid, or no public base URL for the host. 401 TOKEN_EXPIRED The token's exp has passed. 403 SCOPE_REQUIRED The operation needs a scope the token lacks (admin operations: canvas:admin and token_admin ). 403 ROLE_FORBIDDEN The user's role on the file is too low, the file is not in files , or access was revoked. 403 FILES_REQUIRED No POST /access callback, and the token lists no files . 401 answers carry WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="opencanvas" (with error="invalid_token" for token problems). The MCP endpoint uses the same check with its own audience; see AI and MCP . Last changed 2026-11-28 .


# Errors

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/errors.html

## Errors

Every error answer is RFC 9457 problem details, application/problem+json, with a machine code you can branch on. The code is stable; the human detail is not.

## The shape

{ "type": "urn:opencanvas:problem:stale-block", "title": "Precondition Failed", "status": 412, "detail": "a block changed since it was read; re-read it and retry", "code": "STALE_BLOCK", "fresh": { "stale": [ { "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk", "rev": "5641be1fd2cb", "markdown": "Ship on Friday.\n" } ] } } Member Meaning type urn:opencanvas:problem:<code in lower case, hyphens> . A stable name, not a URL to fetch. title The HTTP reason phrase of status . status The HTTP status, repeated in the body. detail What went wrong, in words, for logs and people. It can change between releases; do not parse it. code The machine code: branch on this. The same codes the 0.1 routes use. fresh Only with STALE_BLOCK : the current state to retry against. Unknown members may be added later; ignore them. Even answers the router gives before an operation runs (an unknown path, a wrong method) are problem details, so a client parses one error format.

## Handling them

Status What to do 400 Fix the request; detail says what is wrong. Do not retry it unchanged. 401 Fix the credentials: the host key, or mint a new token. 403 The scope or the user's role does not allow it. Do not retry. 404 Unknown file part or operation, or the API is off ( API_OFF ). 409 CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED : send again with "confirm": true . IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS : retry after Retry-After . CONFLICT : your save callback reported a conflict. 410 CURSOR_EXPIRED : start the walk again without a cursor. 412 STALE_BLOCK : re-read (or use fresh ), apply your change again, send it with the new revision. 413 The body or the resulting document is too large. 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED : a new request needs a new key. 429 Wait Retry-After seconds, then retry. 5xx 503 and 502 are transient: retry after Retry-After with backoff. 501 : the server is not set up for it (PDF). The TypeScript and Rust clients turn these into typed errors and retry 429 , 503 and 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS for you; see SDKs .

## Every code

## Any operation on a file

Authentication, the API switch, rate limits and availability: every /api/v1 operation on a file can answer these. Code Status Meaning TOKEN_EXPIRED 401 The bearer token's exp has passed. Mint a new one; tokens live at most 15 minutes. TOKEN_INVALID 401 A bearer token failed a check: signature, issuer, audience, a lifetime over 15 minutes, or not yet valid ( nbf ). Also answered when the host has no public base URL, so user tokens are off for it. UNAUTHENTICATED 401 No credentials, an unknown host, or a wrong host key. The answer carries WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="opencanvas" . FILES_REQUIRED 403 The host does not implement POST /access , so a token's role claim counts only for the files in its files claim, and this token has none. Add files , implement /access , or set [host.api] all_files = true . ROLE_FORBIDDEN 403 The user's role on the file is below what the operation needs (the effective permission is min(scope, role) ), the token does not list the file in files , or the host revoked the user. SCOPE_REQUIRED 403 The token's scope does not cover the operation. Admin operations need canvas:admin , which counts only when the host sets [host.api] token_admin = true . API_OFF 404 The host has turned the API off ( [host.flags] api_v1 = false in its entry of the hosts file). RATE_LIMITED 429 A token bucket is empty: the caller's, or the file's write bucket. Wait for Retry-After seconds. The RateLimit header says which bucket and when it refills. INTERNAL 500 An unexpected server error, or the host's POST /access callback failed. The server logs the cause; retrying may help. BUSY 503 The server cannot take the request right now: rooms are recovering after a restart, or no database connection is free. The answer carries Retry-After (1-5 s); send the same request again after it. Never a 500 for overload (RLB-01b). UNAVAILABLE 503 A dependency is briefly unavailable: the idempotency store, the node that runs the file's live room, or the ticket store. Retry after Retry-After .

## Operation-specific

Each operation's section in the reference lists the ones it can answer. Code Status Meaning BAD_INPUT 400 The request is not what the operation takes: the body is not a JSON object, a field is missing or has the wrong type, an op, mode, format or event type is unknown, or fileId is longer than 1,024 bytes. detail says which. readFile , findBlocks , batchBlocks , createDatabase , queryRows , upsertRows , addField , createBoard , addShapes , addComment , makeLive , setRole , streamEvents , search , offlineRevoke , testAutomation , saveAutomation , deleteAutomation , enableAutomation , listBacklinks , deleteFileLinks , indexLinks , getGraph CURSOR_INVALID 400 The cursor is not one this server signed for this file and query: changed, truncated, from another host, or sent with a different filter , sort or fields . Pass next_cursor back unchanged. listBlocks , queryRows IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID 400 The Idempotency-Key header is empty, longer than 255 bytes, or has characters outside visible ASCII. batchBlocks , createDatabase , upsertRows , addField , createBoard , addShapes , addComment , makeLive , importFile , commitFile , setRole , invalidateMembers , testAutomation , saveAutomation , deleteAutomation , enableAutomation IMPORT_INVALID 400 The file could not be read: not UTF-8, a malformed CSV, or a diagram that is unreadable, too deep or declares entities. importFile , legacyImport INPUT_INVALID 400 Convert: the body is not a readable .ocanvas file. convert , legacyConvert ROLE_INVALID 400 role is not view , comment , edit or none . setRole , legacySetRole RULE_INVALID 400 The rule does not parse, names an action the host does not allow, or schedules more often than the minimum. saveAutomation RULE_LIMIT 400 The canvas has max_rules rules; delete one to add another. saveAutomation URL_NOT_ALLOWED 400 A URL call to an origin that is neither the host's callback origin nor in [host.automation] allow_origins (ADR-068). saveAutomation USER_TOKEN_REQUIRED 400 Search runs as a person, so the host's permissions apply;
