## Router fallbacks

Answers the router gives before an operation runs. Code Status Meaning UNAUTHORIZED 401 A fallback for a 401 that did not carry its own code. FORBIDDEN 403 A fallback for a 403 that did not carry its own code. METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED 405 The path exists but not with this method; Allow lists the methods it takes. UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE 415 A fallback for a request the router could not read. ERROR other Any other error status without its own code.

## 0.1 routes only

The deprecated /v1/... routes answer {"error": {"code", "message"}} with these and the codes above. Code Status Meaning PATCH_INVALID 400 0.1 patch : an op is malformed. API_KEY_INVALID 401 0.1 routes: the host id or key is missing or wrong.

## The 0.1 routes

The deprecated /v1/files/{fileId}/... routes keep their old error shape, {"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}} , with the same codes. Only /api/v1 answers problem details. Last changed 2026-11-28 .


# Pagination

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/pagination.html

## Pagination

Two operations answer pages: listBlocks (top-level blocks, up to 100 per page) and queryRows (database rows, up to 200). Cursors are opaque and signed, and a block walk stays correct while people edit the canvas.

## How it works

Ask for the first page with an optional limit . Each page answers has_more and next_cursor ; when more follow, it also carries a Link header with the next page's URL. Pass next_cursor back as cursor , unchanged, until has_more is false . GET /api/v1/files/doc_1/blocks?limit=2 HTTP/1.1 200 OK ETag: "c465d27bcd7e" Link: </api/v1/files/doc_1/blocks?cursor=eyJmIjoiZG9jXzEi...&limit=2>; rel="next" {"blocks": [...], "rev": "c465d27bcd7e", "has_more": true, "next_cursor": "eyJmIjoiZG9jXzEi..."} Operation Items limit Default GET /api/v1/files/{fileId}/blocks blocks 1-100 100 GET /api/v1/files/{fileId}/databases/{dbId}/rows rows 1-200 50

## Walk every page

Every block of a canvas curl TypeScript Rust Python url="https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/blocks?limit=100" while [ -n "$url" ]; do page=$(curl -s "$url" -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY") echo "$page" | jq -c '.blocks[]' cursor=$(echo "$page" | jq -r '.next_cursor // empty') url=${cursor:+"https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/blocks?limit=100&cursor=$cursor"} done // paginate() follows next_cursor and yields each item. for await (const block of oc.paginate("listBlocks", { fileId: "doc_1", query: { limit: 100 } })) { console.log(block); } use futures::StreamExt; use opencanvas_client::{CallOptions, Params}; let mut blocks = Box::pin(oc.paginate("listBlocks", Params::file("doc_1").query("limit", 100), CallOptions::default())); while let Some(block) = blocks.next().await { println!("{}", block?); } def every_block(api, file_id): params = {"limit": 100} while True: r = api.get(f"{BASE}/files/{file_id}/blocks", params=params, timeout=30) r.raise_for_status() page = r.json() yield from page["blocks"] if not page["has_more"]: return params["cursor"] = page["next_cursor"]

## Cursors

Opaque and signed. Do not build or change them; a changed cursor answers 400 CURSOR_INVALID . Bound to the request. A block cursor belongs to its file; a row cursor to its file, database, filter , sort and fields . Sending it with other values is CURSOR_INVALID . Valid for an hour. After that, 410 CURSOR_EXPIRED : start again without one. Stable under edits. A block cursor is a position after the last block you got (a Yjs relative position), not an index. A block inserted or deleted before it does not shift the next page, and if that last block is deleted, the next page starts at its successor. Every block that exists for the whole walk is returned exactly once.

## Errors

Status Code When 400 CURSOR_INVALID Not a cursor this server signed for this file and query. 410 CURSOR_EXPIRED Older than an hour. 400 BAD_INPUT filter or sort is not a JSON array. Last changed 2026-11-28 .


# Idempotency

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/idempotency.html

## Idempotency

Every POST under /api/v1/files takes an Idempotency-Key header. Send the same key on every retry of one request, and the change is applied once, even across nodes of a cluster.

## How it works

Pick a key per logical request (a UUID, or an id from your own job) and send it on the first try and on every retry: POST /api/v1/files/doc_1/comments Idempotency-Key: remind-2026-11-25-doc_1 Content-Type: application/json {"text": "Is Friday still right?", "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk"} Case Answer First request with the key Runs, and its answer is stored for 24 hours. The same request again (method, path and body) The stored answer, with Idempotency-Replayed: true . Nothing runs again. The same key with another request 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED . The same key while the first is still running, on any node 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS with Retry-After: 1 . Retry to get the first one's answer. The first request failed (any error) Not stored: a retry with the key runs again. A malformed key 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID .

## The key

1 to 255 visible ASCII characters. Yours per caller: the host key with its X-OpenCanvas-Author , or a token's sub . Two users can use the same key without seeing each other's answers. Kept 24 hours. After that, the same key is a new request.

## Which operations

Every POST under /api/v1/files/{fileId}/... takes a key, except POST .../sync-token : its answer is a credential, never stored, so the same key gets a fresh ticket. POST /api/v1/convert changes nothing and takes no key. Reads and DELETE .../session (closing a session twice is harmless) take none.

## What is stored

The request's hash and the write's answer: ids, counts and revisions. Never document content. Keys live in the database ( api_idempotency , SQLite, MySQL or MariaDB) or, with Redis-only storage, in Redis ( oc:idem:... ).

## In the clients

The TypeScript and Rust clients send a random key on every write and reuse it for each retry of that call. Pass your own key when a retry may come from another process (a job queue that re-runs a job after a crash): Your own key curl TypeScript Rust Python curl -s -X POST "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/comments" \ -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Idempotency-Key: remind-2026-11-25-doc_1" \ -d '{"text": "Is Friday still right?", "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk"}' const res = await oc.call( "addComment", { fileId: "doc_1", body: { text: "Is Friday still right?", blockId: "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk" } }, { idempotencyKey: "remind-2026-11-25-doc_1" }, ); console.log(res.replayed); // true when the server answered from the stored result use opencanvas_client::{CallOptions, Params}; use serde_json::json; let res = oc .call( "addComment", &Params::file("doc_1").json(json!({"text": "Is Friday still right?", "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk"})), &CallOptions::key("remind-2026-11-25-doc_1"), ) .await?; println!("replayed: {}", res.replayed); r = api.post( f"{BASE}/files/doc_1/comments", json={"text": "Is Friday still right?", "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk"}, headers={"Idempotency-Key": "remind-2026-11-25-doc_1"}, timeout=30, ) replayed = r.headers.get("Idempotency-Replayed") == "true" Last changed 2026-11-28 .


# Rate limits

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/rate-limits.html

## Rate limits

Token buckets, announced on every answer. One bucket per caller, shared with MCP, and one per file for writes. With Redis the buckets are shared by every node of a cluster.

## The buckets

Bucket Applies to Default Setting ( [host.api] ) subject Every request of one caller: the host key, or a token's sub 10 requests a second, burst 30 rate_per_sec , burst file-writes POST and DELETE on one file, from everyone 5 a second, burst 10 file_writes_per_sec , file_burst MCP calls take from the same subject bucket as the API. [host.ai] mcp_rate_per_min still sets the rate when [host.api] does not.

## The headers

Every answer says where you stand (draft IETF RateLimit header fields): RateLimit-Policy: "subject";q=30;w=3, "file-writes";q=10;w=2 RateLimit: "subject";r=29;t=1 Header Meaning RateLimit-Policy The buckets that apply: q is the burst, w the seconds an empty bucket takes to refill. file-writes appears on writes only. RateLimit The bucket closest to empty: r requests remaining, t seconds until it is full again.

## When a bucket is empty

The answer is 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After (seconds). Wait that long, then retry; keep the same Idempotency-Key for a write. HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests Content-Type: application/problem+json Retry-After: 1 RateLimit: "subject";r=0;t=3 {"type": "urn:opencanvas:problem:rate-limited", "title": "Too Many Requests", "status": 429, "detail": "too many requests (subject limit); retry later", "code": "RATE_LIMITED"} The clients retry 429 and 503 after Retry-After (else 500 ms doubling, at most 30 seconds), 3 times by default. In your own code: Retry after 429 curl TypeScript Rust Python for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do status=$(curl -s -o page.json -w '%{http_code}' -D headers.txt \ "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1" \ -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY") [ "$status" != 429 ] && break sleep "$(awk 'tolower($1) == "retry-after:" { print $2 + 0 }' headers.txt)" done // Retries are built in: maxRetries (default 3) per client or per call. const oc = new OpenCanvas({ baseUrl: "https://canvas.example.com", auth, maxRetries: 5 }); const doc = await oc.readFile({ fileId: "doc_1" }, { maxRetries: 0 }); // or none for this call // Retries are built in: max_retries (default 3) per client or per call. let oc = Client::builder("https://canvas.example.com").auth(auth).max_retries(5).build(); import time def get_with_retry(api, url, **kw): for _ in range(4): r = api.get(url, timeout=30, **kw) if r.status_code not in (429, 503): return r time.sleep(float(r.headers.get("Retry-After", "1"))) return r

## Other limits

At most 100 event streams per file on one server ( 429 TOO_MANY_STREAMS ). At most 200 rows per rows:upsert and per page of queryRows ; at most 100 blocks per page of listBlocks . Import files up to 5 MiB; CSV up to 10,000 rows and 200 columns ( 413 IMPORT_TOO_LARGE ). A batch that deletes more than 5 blocks needs "confirm": true . Last changed 2026-11-28 .


# Events

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/events.html

## Events

GET /api/v1/files/{fileId}/events streams what happens to one file: edits, comments, mentions, people joining and leaving, saves, restores. Events carry ids, user ids, versions and counts, never document text.

## Open a stream

The same URL serves Server-Sent Events and, when the request is a WebSocket upgrade, a WebSocket with one JSON text message per event. It needs canvas:read and access to the file, checked like every read. ?types= keeps only the types you list. Stream saves and comments curl TypeScript Rust Python curl -s -N "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/events?types=saved,commented" \ -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" \ -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY" \ -H "Accept: text/event-stream" // Reconnects with Last-Event-ID when the stream drops, and resumes where it stopped. const stream = oc.events({ fileId: "doc_1", types: ["saved", "commented"] }); for await (const event of stream) { console.log(event.id, event.type, event.data); } // stream.lastEventId: keep it to resume after a restart (lastEventId option). use opencanvas_client::EventsOptions; let mut opts = EventsOptions::new("doc_1"); opts.types = vec!["saved".into(), "commented".into()]; let mut stream = oc.events(opts); while let Some(event) = stream.next().await { let event = event?; println!("{} {} {:?}", event.id, event.type_, event.data); } import json import os import requests r = requests.get( "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/events", params={"types": "saved,commented"}, headers={ "X-OpenCanvas-Host": "acme", "X-OpenCanvas-Key": os.environ["OC_API_KEY"], "Accept": "text/event-stream", }, stream=True, timeout=(10, 60), ) r.raise_for_status() for line in r.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True): if line.startswith("data:"): event = json.loads(line[5:]) print(event["id"], event["type"], event["data"]) On the wire, each SSE event has an id , an event name (the type) and one data line; a comment line keeps the connection alive every 15 seconds: id: ev_01m87jv4t3ggvh8n6d6nh38xc0 event: commented data: {"at":1795550974787,"data":{"added":2,"blockId":"b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk","by":["svc:acme"],"threadId":"t_01m87jv4sqj5z6jz5q2n5zdtdw"},"fileId":"doc_1","id":"ev_01m87jv4t3ggvh8n6d6nh38xc0","type":"commented"} :

## The event

Every event, on a stream, a WebSocket or a webhook , is the same JSON: Member Meaning id ev_<ulid> : sorts by time. Pass the last one back to resume; webhooks send it as Idempotency-Key . type One of the types below. fileId Your file id. at Unix milliseconds. data The type's payload. type data When edited {blockIds, removedBlockIds, databaseIds?, boardIds?, by, truncated?, untracked?} Changes, debounced: once edits pause for [host.api] events_coalesce_ms (default 250) and at least every 2 seconds during a long burst. blockIds are the deepest blocks with a blockId that changed (at most 500; truncated: true beyond). untracked: true when something changed outside any identified block: re-read. by lists who sent the changes. commented {threadId, blockId?, added, by} New comment messages in a thread. mentioned {mentioned, by, blockId?, threadId?} New @mentions, as for the mentions callback, without the excerpt. member.joined {userId, role} A person's first connection to the live room opened. member.left {userId} Their last connection closed. saved {version} Your application accepted a save. restored {restoreId, from, by} A version was restored. session.closed {reason: "host" | "idle"} The live room ended: DELETE .../session , or everyone left. resync {reason} Streams only: the resume point is gone; re-read the file.

## Resume

Send the last id you handled as Last-Event-ID (or ?since= ; the header wins). The server keeps the last 512 events of each file in memory and answers the ones after your id. When your id is gone (evicted, the server restarted, or another node that was not listening), you get one resync event, whose id is the newest the server has: re-read the file, then carry on from there. In a cluster, the node that runs the file's live room publishes each event to the others, so a stream on any node gets them.

## Close codes

Code SSE Meaning What to do 4008 a final event: close with {"code": 4008, "reason": "..."} The stream fell 256 events behind. Reconnect with your last id. 4001 the same The user token expired. Mint a new token and reconnect. 4003 the same The host revoked the user ( role: none ). Nothing is sent after the revoke. Stop.

## Limits and proxies

At most 100 streams per file on one server: 429 TOO_MANY_STREAMS . Share one stream between your workers. Behind nginx the answer sets X-Accel-Buffering: no ; keep proxy read timeouts above 15 seconds (the keep-alive interval). Events are a notification, not a log: when you need the content, read it with the API.

## Sync the document itself

A Yjs-native program (yrs, Yjs, y-crdt bindings) can hold the CRDT document instead of calling the API per change: POST /api/v1/files/{fileId}/sync-token answers a ticket for the room WebSocket. {"ticket": "01M87JV4T23GYQ773ZF1WN91VA", "room": "r_2whbv4nncveupmqu35cywoidfe", "role": "edit", "url": "/v1/collab/r_2whbv4nncveupmqu35cywoidfe?ticket=01M87JV4T23GYQ773ZF1WN91VA", "expiresAt": 1795551874, "connectWithinSecs": 60} Connect a y-websocket client to url within 60 seconds. role is the effective one, min(scope, role) : a canvas:read token gets view , and the room refuses its writes as it would a viewer's. The session ends at expiresAt (at most 15 minutes, never after the token's exp ); ask for a new ticket to continue. The answer is a credential: Cache-Control: no-store , and it is never stored for idempotent replays. See createSyncToken . Last changed 2026-11-28 .


# Webhooks

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/webhooks.html

## Webhooks

OpenCanvas POSTs a file's change events to one URL of yours, so you can react without holding a stream open: index a saved file, notify on a comment. Deliveries are signed, retried, and survive restarts.

## Turn them on

Webhooks are off unless the host's entry has a [host.webhooks] table: [host.webhooks] url = "https://host.example.com/opencanvas/hooks" # must be on your callback_base origin events = ["saved", "commented", "mentioned"] # or ["*"]; the event types below # secret = "env:OC_WEBHOOK_SECRET" # default: callback_secret, else jwt_secret # max_attempts = 12 # 1-20 Setting Meaning url Where to POST. It must be on the same origin (scheme, host and port) as your callback_base ; anything else stops the server at start-up and is refused again before every delivery. To receive on another domain, relay from your callback origin. events The event types to send, or ["*"] for all. secret The signing secret. Default: the host's callback secret, else its jwt_secret . max_attempts Attempts before an event is dropped, 1 to 20 (default 12, about a day). Webhooks need a database (SQLite, MySQL or MariaDB): with Redis-only storage the server refuses to start with [host.webhooks] .

## The request

One POST per event. The body is the event, the same JSON as on the events stream : ids, user ids, versions and counts, never document text. POST /opencanvas/hooks HTTP/1.1 Content-Type: application/json X-OpenCanvas-Event: commented X-OpenCanvas-Event-Id: ev_01m87jv4t3ggvh8n6d6nh38xc0 Idempotency-Key: ev_01m87jv4t3ggvh8n6d6nh38xc0 X-OpenCanvas-Delivery-Attempt: 1 X-OpenCanvas-Signature: t=1795550974,v1=4c430dee70e32585ea42f8f640c4f9197fd3f8d781cbaca4294566f61d08f656,v2=d85e216af3489979b6aaadd7c54574683679cfa8e0dee639e3d229db0e650f57 {"at":1795550974787,"data":{"added":1,"blockId":"b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk","by":["u_42"],"threadId":"t_01m87jv4sqj5z6jz5q2n5zdtdw"},"fileId":"doc_1","id":"ev_01m87jv4t3ggvh8n6d6nh38xc0","type":"commented"} Header Meaning X-OpenCanvas-Event The event type. X-OpenCanvas-Event-Id The event id ( ev_<ulid> ). Idempotency-Key The event id again: deduplicate on it. X-OpenCanvas-Delivery-Attempt 1 for the first attempt, then 2, 3, ... X-OpenCanvas-Signature t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>,v2=<hex> . Verify v2 . No bearer token is sent; the signature is the credential.

## Payloads

type Example data edited {"blockIds": ["b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk"], "removedBlockIds": [], "databaseIds": ["db_01m87jv4sc2twxjhzzxzh7mene"], "by": ["u_42"]} commented {"threadId": "t_01m87jv4sqj5z6jz5q2n5zdtdw", "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk", "added": 1, "by": ["u_42"]} mentioned {"mentioned": ["u_7"], "by": "u_42", "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk"} member.joined {"userId": "u_42", "role": "edit"} member.left {"userId": "u_42"} saved {"version": "18"} restored {"restoreId": "01m87k0a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h9j0k", "from": "17", "by": "u_42"} session.closed {"reason": "host"} or {"reason": "idle"} resync is never sent to webhooks; it only exists on streams.

## Verify the signature

v2 is HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.POST.<path?query>.<body>" with your secret, in lower-case hex: Read the raw body bytes before any JSON parsing; a re-serialised body does not match. Use the path and query as your server received them (behind a proxy that rewrites paths, the path OpenCanvas sent to). Compare in constant time, and reject a t more than 5 minutes from your clock. t is the time of the attempt, so each retry has a new signature. v1 (timestamp and body only) is kept for old callback verifiers; do not use it for webhooks. Verify a delivery openssl TypeScript Rust Python # A sketch of the check: compare the hex in constant time in real code. secret='whsec_test_example' signature='t=1795550974,v1=4c430dee70e32585ea42f8f640c4f9197fd3f8d781cbaca4294566f61d08f656,v2=d85e216af3489979b6aaadd7c54574683679cfa8e0dee639e3d229db0e650f57' path_query='/opencanvas/hooks' body='{"at":1795550974787,"data":{"added":1,"blockId":"b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk","by":["u_42"],"threadId":"t_01m87jv4sqj5z6jz5q2n5zdtdw"},"fileId":"doc_1","id":"ev_01m87jv4t3ggvh8n6d6nh38xc0","type":"commented"}' t=$(printf '%s' "$signature" | tr ',' '\n' | sed -n 's/^t=//p') v2=$(printf '%s' "$signature" | tr ',' '\n' | sed -n 's/^v2=//p') expected=$(printf '%s.POST.%s.%s' "$t" "$path_query" "$body" \ | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$secret" -hex | sed 's/^.*= //') [ "$expected" = "$v2" ] && echo "signature ok" || echo "signature WRONG" # Then reject it if t is more than 300 seconds from now: # [ $(( $(date +%s) - t )) -le 300 ] && [ $(( t - $(date +%s) )) -le 300 ] import { verifyWebhook } from "@opencanvas/client"; // In your receiver: the raw body (before JSON parsing) and the path and query as received. const ok = await verifyWebhook({ secret: process.env.OC_WEBHOOK_SECRET!, // "whsec_test_example" for the test vector signature: req.headers["x-opencanvas-signature"] as string, body: rawBody, // string or Uint8Array, exactly as received pathQuery: req.originalUrl, // "/opencanvas/hooks" // nowSecs: 1795550974, // pin the clock to check the test vector }); if (!ok) return res.status(401).end(); res.status(204).end(); // answer fast, then do the work const event = JSON.parse(rawBody); use opencanvas_client::{verify_webhook, WebhookRequest}; let ok = verify_webhook( secret.as_bytes(), // b"whsec_test_example" for the test vector WebhookRequest { signature: &signature_header, // X-OpenCanvas-Signature method: "POST", path_query: &path_and_query, // "/opencanvas/hooks" body: &raw_body, // the bytes as received }, now_secs, // 1795550974 for the test vector ); if !ok { return StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED; } import hashlib import hmac import time def verify_webhook(secret: bytes, signature: str, path_query: str, body: bytes, now=None, tolerance=300) -> bool: parts = {} for item in signature.split(","): k, _, v = item.strip().partition("=") parts.setdefault(k, v) try: t = int(parts["t"]) v2 = parts["v2"] except (KeyError, ValueError): return False if abs((time.time() if now is None else now) - t) > tolerance: return False mac = hmac.new(secret, f"{t}.POST.{path_query}.".encode() + body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest() return hmac.compare_digest(mac, v2) # The test vector: assert verify_webhook( b"whsec_test_example", "t=1795550974,v1=4c430dee70e32585ea42f8f640c4f9197fd3f8d781cbaca4294566f61d08f656,v2=d85e216af3489979b6aaadd7c54574683679cfa8e0dee639e3d229db0e650f57", "/opencanvas/hooks", "{\"at\":1795550974787,\"data\":{\"added\":1,\"blockId\":\"b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk\",\"by\":[\"u_42\"],\"threadId\":\"t_01m87jv4sqj5z6jz5q2n5zdtdw\"},\"fileId\":\"doc_1\",\"id\":\"ev_01m87jv4t3ggvh8n6d6nh38xc0\",\"type\":\"commented\"}".encode(), now=1795550974, )

## Test vector

Your verifier must accept this delivery (with the clock at t ) and refuse it when any byte of the body, the path or the signature changes: Input Value Secret whsec_test_example Time (Unix seconds, also t ) 1795550974 Path and query /opencanvas/hooks Body (exact bytes) {"at":1795550974787,"data":{"added":1,"blockId":"b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk","by":["u_42"],"threadId":"t_01m87jv4sqj5z6jz5q2n5zdtdw"},"fileId":"doc_1","id":"ev_01m87jv4t3ggvh8n6d6nh38xc0","type":"commented"} X-OpenCanvas-Signature t=1795550974,v1=4c430dee70e32585ea42f8f640c4f9197fd3f8d781cbaca4294566f61d08f656,v2=d85e216af3489979b6aaadd7c54574683679cfa8e0dee639e3d229db0e650f57

## Answer and retries

Answer any 2xx quickly (10-second timeout) and do the work afterwards. Your answer What OpenCanvas does 2xx Delivered. Network error, timeout, 408 , 425 , 429 , 5xx Retried after 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 5 min, 15 min, 30 min, 1 h, 2 h, 4 h, 8 h, then every 12 h, until max_attempts ; then dropped. A longer Retry-After (seconds, up to 12 h) wins. Any other 3xx or 4xx Dropped at once. Redirects are never followed. At least once. An event can arrive twice: deduplicate on Idempotency-Key . Order is not guaranteed across retries: order a file's events by at and the id (a ULID). Durable. Events are written to a database outbox ( webhook_outbox ) by the server that runs the file's live room before they are sent, so they survive restarts, and exactly one server of a cluster sends each. An event can be lost only if that server dies between the change and the outbox write.

## Metrics

oc_webhook_deliveries_total{host,result} ( ok , retry , rejected , gave_up , refused ) and oc_webhook_delivery_seconds{host} (one attempt's time), on the operations dashboard's "Webhooks" row. Last changed 2026-11-28 .


# SDKs

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/sdks.html

## SDKs

Two clients wrap the API with the same behaviour: typed operations generated from the OpenAPI document, an Idempotency-Key on every write, retries after Retry-After, cursor paging, resumable events, typed errors and the webhook signature check. Both are Apache-2.0 and versioned with the server.

## Install

Both clients live in the OpenCanvas repository and are not yet published to npm or crates.io. Client Where Runs on TypeScript @opencanvas/client [ web/packages/client ](../../../web/packages/client) Node 20+, browsers, Deno, edge runtimes. No runtime dependency beyond fetch . Rust opencanvas-client (library opencanvas_client ) [ crates/oc-client ](../../../crates/oc-client) Tokio, reqwest and serde . Add the client Shell TypeScript Rust Python # TypeScript: build the package from a checkout, then depend on the folder. git clone https://github.com/CasualOffice/opencanvas cd opencanvas/web && pnpm install && pnpm --filter @opencanvas/client build cd /path/to/your/app && npm install /path/to/opencanvas/web/packages/client # Rust: a git dependency. cargo add opencanvas-client --git https://github.com/CasualOffice/opencanvas // package.json, after building web/packages/client in a checkout: // "dependencies": { "@opencanvas/client": "file:../opencanvas/web/packages/client" } import { OpenCanvas } from "@opencanvas/client"; // Cargo.toml: // [dependencies] // opencanvas-client = { git = "https://github.com/CasualOffice/opencanvas" } // tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"] } use opencanvas_client::{Auth, Client}; # No Python client yet: the samples on these pages use requests. # pip install requests import requests

## Create a client

Host key or user token curl TypeScript Rust Python # curl: send the headers yourself (see Authentication). curl -s "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1" \ -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY" import { OpenCanvas } from "@opencanvas/client"; const oc = new OpenCanvas({ baseUrl: "https://canvas.example.com", auth: { hostId: "acme", key: process.env.OC_API_KEY!, author: "u_42" }, // or a user token, minted before every request so it never expires mid-job: // auth: { token: () => mintUserToken("u_42", "canvas:read canvas:write", ["doc_1"]) }, maxRetries: 3, }); use opencanvas_client::{Auth, Client}; let oc = Client::builder("https://canvas.example.com") .auth(Auth::host_key("acme", std::env::var("OC_API_KEY").expect("OC_API_KEY"))) // or .auth(Auth::Token(token)), or Auth::TokenFn(...) to mint one per request .max_retries(3) .build(); import os import requests api = requests.Session() api.headers.update({"X-OpenCanvas-Host": "acme", "X-OpenCanvas-Key": os.environ["OC_API_KEY"]})

## What both do

Feature Behaviour Typed operations One method per operation, with the types of its parameters, body and answer, generated from openapi.json (TypeScript scripts/gen.mjs , Rust tests/models.rs ; CI fails when they drift). The generic call(operationId, params, options) answers status, headers, etag , replayed and rateLimit too. Credentials The host key (with optional author and callback token) or a user token; a token callback runs before every request. Idempotency Every write carries an Idempotency-Key : a random one per call, the same on each retry of that call. Pass your own to survive a process restart, or none. Retries 429 , 503 and 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS , after Retry-After (else 500 ms doubling, at most 30 s), 3 times by default. Network errors are retried for reads and keyed writes only. The wait is injectable, so tests never sleep. Errors Problem details as typed errors, by code first, then status: stale block (412, with fresh ), rate limited ( retryAfterSecs ), key reused, key in progress, cursor expired, bad request, unauthorized, forbidden, not found, conflict, gone, precondition failed, too large, unprocessable, unavailable, server. Paging paginate follows next_cursor through listBlocks and queryRows , item by item. Events The SSE stream of a file. A dropped stream (or close code 4008) reconnects with Last-Event-ID and gets what it missed, or a resync event; 4001 and 4003 end it with an error. Webhooks verifyWebhook / verify_webhook : the v2 check, in constant time, with a 5-minute window.

## Typed errors

Handle a stale write curl TypeScript Rust Python # 412 with "code": "STALE_BLOCK": re-read, apply your change again, send it with the new rev. curl -s -o answer.json -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST \ "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/blocks:batch" \ -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H 'If-Match: "c465d27bcd7e"' \ -d '{"ops": [{"op": "append", "markdown": "Shipped."}]}' jq -r .code answer.json import { RateLimitedError, StaleBlockError } from "@opencanvas/client"; try { await oc.batchBlocks( { fileId: "doc_1", body: { ops: [{ op: "append", markdown: "Shipped." }] } }, { ifMatch: doc.rev }, ); } catch (e) { if (e instanceof StaleBlockError) console.log("changed meanwhile", e.fresh); else if (e instanceof RateLimitedError) console.log("retry in", e.retryAfterSecs, "s"); else throw e; } use opencanvas_client::ProblemKind; match oc.batch_blocks("doc_1", &req, &CallOptions::if_match(rev)).await { Ok(result) => println!("{:?}", result.block_ids), Err(e) if e.kind() == Some(ProblemKind::StaleBlock) => { println!("changed meanwhile: {:?}", e.api().and_then(|a| a.fresh())); } Err(e) => return Err(e), } r = api.post(f"{BASE}/files/doc_1/blocks:batch", json={"ops": [{"op": "append", "markdown": "Shipped."}]}, headers={"If-Match": f'"{rev}"'}, timeout=30) if r.status_code == 412 and r.json().get("code") == "STALE_BLOCK": print("changed meanwhile", r.json()["fresh"]) else: r.raise_for_status()

## Paging, events and webhooks

See pagination , events and webhooks : each page has the client samples beside curl and Python.

## The conformance suite

crates/oc-server/api/conformance.json is one list of scenarios that both clients run against a real server: a read, a block batch with If-Match , idempotent replay, paging, a rate limit, an events resume and a webhook signature, plus offline webhook signature vectors. The server pins its clock, so no scenario sleeps. A third-party client can run the same scenarios; the format is in the integration guide .

## Block SDK

To add your own block types to the editor rather than call the API, use @opencanvas/block-sdk . It is a different package: blocks run sandboxed inside the canvas, not on your server. See the Block SDK guide . Last changed 2026-11-28 .


# API changelog

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/changelog.html

## API changelog

The API-relevant entries of CHANGELOG.md , newest first. The OpenAPI document is version 1.0.0 ; within /api/v1 changes are additive, and a breaking change gets a new path major.

## 0.4.1 (2026-11-28)

Added Links between canvases (LINK-01..03, ADR-081; off until a host sets [host.flags] links ): a canvasLink node links a canvas, a block or a row; the server keeps a link index of ids only ( link_edges , migration 0014, SQLite, MySQL and MariaDB), written only after the host acknowledged a save. GET /api/v1/files/{fileId}/backlinks and the MCP tool canvas_backlinks list the canvases that link to one, with the sentence around each link, checked with the host's new optional POST /access/batch (else POST /access per file): canvases the reader cannot open are left out and not counted. Backfill with POST /api/v1/links/index , drop a deleted file's links with DELETE /api/v1/links/files/{id} . Exports write canvas links as links to [host.links] url_template . Both API clients have the new operations. Redis-only storage refuses links = true . Added The link graph (GRAPH-01, ADR-082): GET /api/v1/graph and the MCP tool canvas_graph answer the canvases around one canvas (depth 1-3) or the most-connected canvases, with every canvas checked with the host before it is shown or expanded, so a canvas the reader cannot open never connects two others. 30 s cache per person, 10 a minute (2 full). Added Links in the editor (LINK-01/04/05, to the approved prototype; with [host.flags] links ): type [[ to link a canvas from the host's search and your recent canvases, # to link one of its headings, databases or rows, or paste one of the host's URLs. Links show the canvas's current title, and "No access", a struck-through deleted canvas or a missing block when that is so. Resting on a link (or Space on a selected one) previews it. Every canvas ends with "Linked from": the canvases that link here, grouped, with the sentence around each link, filters by kind and block, and only canvases you can open; headings with backlinks get a "Linked from" chip that opens the side panel on that heading. "Unlinked mentions" lists canvases that name this one without a link, with Link (as you, in that canvas) and Undo. All of it loads on its own after the canvas (initial JS +0.6 KB for the node). Fixed Partial sync: the one-client-id-per-document rule now refuses only items at clocks another document was given. An editor that loaded a database during server work had its sync reply refused (PSYNC-BUG-4).

## 0.4.0 (2026-11-28)

Added Backup and restore (RLB-03, docs/13): a runbook for SQLite, MySQL/MariaDB and Redis, scripts/restore-drill.sh , and a restore epoch. Start once with OC_RESTORED=1 after a restore. Devices revoked after the backup stay revoked (every offline copy is dropped once), and schedule slots due before the restore are skipped instead of running twice. Migration 0013 adds the restore_epoch table. Added Partial sync in the room (PSYNC-02, ADR-076), behind [host.flags] partial_sync ( off by default ; leave it off until the 0.4 editor ships): databases and boards become subdocuments on the room socket (message type 101, docs/15 §3.2), loaded when a connection asks, the role checked per request, evicted when unheld; the API, MCP, history, templates, AI tools, automation and saves work on a whole view flattened with the original item ids, so saves stay .ocanvas format v1. Editors without caps=subdoc are closed with 4426 on a split room. Room memory on the 50 MB fixture with 20 viewers (caps=subdoc, first page, no edits; release build, Apple M4, local; one process per figure, test-process RSS): split room opened from its WAL 220 MB (a high-water mark: opening walks every part once, one at a time, to index its ids) against 4,401 MB for the same room whole (2,382 MB in a second run), 5-9%, under the 30% bar (tests/partial_sync.rs room_memory_on_the_fixture). Fixed After a restart with a slow host, rooms reopen and save at full speed (RLB-01c): a room no longer holds one of the OC_ROOM_LOADS slots while the host answers its file request. Fixed Overload never answers 500: while rooms recover after a restart (more than OC_ROOM_LOAD_QUEUE , default 32, waiting to load) or when no database connection is free, launches, session lookups and WebSocket upgrades answer 503 with a Retry-After of 1-5 s. The browser launch shows "Reconnecting…" and posts again; the editor waits out Retry-After for up to 60 s instead of showing an error (RLB-01b). Fixed A launch that failed after its token was recorded (database timeout, server killed mid-launch) spent the token, so every retry was refused as a replay. The token is now spent last (SEC-59). Fixed Partial sync (off by default): one client id writing both the main document and a block's document made the whole view drop the block's content (SEC-54); block edits now count against the document size limit (SEC-55). Fixed After a restart on MySQL/MariaDB, launches failed with 500 for about 20 s while every room reopened at once (connection pool exhausted). Rooms now load at most 8 at a time ( OC_ROOM_LOADS ), and the pool is 32 connections ( OC_DB_MAX_CONNECTIONS ; RLB-01b). Fixed Load generator: a client refused by a full room retried every 0.5 s and counted as a drop; it now backs off and is counted as refused. Fixed Automation in a cluster (AUTO-CL): rule operations (API, editor, MCP) sent to a node that does not hold the canvas answered 503; they now run on the owner. A scheduled rule whose canvas was open on another node could be put off for five minutes at a time; the node holding the canvas now runs it. A run cut off by a node that stopped is logged as failed ( INTERRUPTED ) after an hour instead of staying "running". Added Benchmark program, first part (BENCH-01, BENCH-04, ADR-079): scripts/bench/run <scenario> with scenario files in bench/scenarios/ that state their load mix (X10K, R1K, STORM, SOAK, and the docs/22 scenarios run unchanged), oc-bench scenario (idle, presence-only and typing peers, latency per bucket, kill -9 and restart mid-run with reconnect timing, source addresses), JSON results with hardware, load average and mix in bench/results/ , seeded fixtures ( oc-bench fixture s|m|l|50mb ), bench/budgets.toml , the initial-JS and --forbid gate in scripts/prepush.sh and CI, and a nightly benchmark workflow. Added OFF-08 tests: a three-client simulated day offline in vitest (text, database cells, board objects, block deletes and moves, comments; the real replay frames, cut connections, the pending log and the merge summary; seeds 1, 7, 42 and OC_FUZZ_SEED , a long run behind OC_FUZZ_LONG=1 ), and Playwright zf-offline-2 (expiry by the browser clock, queued upload end to end, the 5 MB pause).

## 0.3.0 (2026-11-26)

Added Automation, server side (AUTO-01..05, AUTO-07, ADR-067, ADR-068; off unless [host.automation] ): rules stored in the canvas ( automations root) run by the server as "Automation" on behalf of their owner, re-checked with the host's /access at every run. Triggers: row added, field changed, checklist item checked, comment or mention added, a date reached and schedules (every 15 minutes or more, in the canvas time zone, even with the canvas closed). Actions: set a field, move a row, check or add checklist items, comment, notify through the host's POST /mentions , and call a URL signed like webhooks on allowed origins only. Loop guard (never itself, 3 deep), limits, auto-pause after 10 failures, a metadata-only run log (30 days), automation.ran / automation.failed events, perms.automate , migration 0010, the API ( /api/v1/files/{id}/automations… ) and MCP tools. Added Offline copies, server side (OFF-01, OFF-07, ADR-063/064): [host.offline] (off by default; checked at start-up; JWT hosts only), the launch token's perms.offline and offlineReason , an ES256 offline grant in the session answer that the editor keeps with its copy and uses only on the device, a revocation generation per host and person (migration 0011; Redis oc:offgen: ) raised by POST /api/v1/offline/revoke , and the GET /v1/offline/clear sign-out page. The server stores one number per host and person, never content. Added Offline-first editing in the editor (OFF-02..07, ADR-063/064/073, the approved prototype): a person keeps a canvas on their device ("Available offline on this device"), encrypted in IndexedDB under a per-person device key; it opens and edits without a network (a service worker caches the editor code, never content) and locks when its 7-day grant runs out. The save pill shows where changes are (on this device, or this tab only). Reconnecting is a fresh launch through the host; unsent changes go in frames under the frame and rate limits, long sessions get a "Before <name>'s offline changes" version first and collaborators a toast. A merge summary appears only for edits inside a deleted block (restore as a new block) and both-sides cell changes (use mine). View only on reconnect holds the changes (download or discard); no access deletes the copy. Images added offline wait as oc-pending: and upload first. Hosts clear the device at sign-out with OpenCanvas.clearOffline() or the /v1/offline/clear iframe and list copies with OpenCanvas.offlineFiles() . Added Live blocks in the editor (LIVE-03, LIVE-07, approved prototype , ADR-073): an always-visible header (Live mark, title, the people in it, Open source, options), editing in place with presence, a one-time hint on the first edit, view only, and every failure state (connecting, not up to date, no access with or without the title, deleted or moved, access removed, limits). The header says where the source lives ("from Leadership weekly › Q1") when the host's /access answers the new optional path (≤ 200 characters, shown as text), else the host's name. Inside a live block, "/" offers the same categorised insert menu, filtered by the host profile, without live blocks (depth rule) and without what acts on the embedding canvas (assistant, import, uploads, SDK blocks). "Make live…" in the block menu, "Live block" in the insert menu through the host's own picker ( UI_PickLiveBlock → Action_InsertLiveBlock ), and paste a block link as a live block, a reference or a link. References refresh on their own and flash once. "Convert to a copy" and "Who can see this" ( GET /v1/live/audience ). A host answers /access with 410 for a deleted live file. Phones get a compact header and an options sheet. The live block code loads only when a canvas shows one. Added <open-canvas view="block"> (LIVE-06): one live block with compact chrome for chats and side panels; its height follows the content ( UI_Resize , oc:resize ). The SDK gains insertLiveBlock() , livePicker() , liveBlockUsage() and the oc:pick-live-block , oc:live-block-open and oc:live-block-usage events. Added Search across canvases, server side (SRCH-02/03/05, ADR-065): every saved .ocanvas carries search.json , a plain-text projection with block ids and heading trails for the host to index (comments only with [host.search] comments = true ; never in-file history; at most 2 MB). POST /api/v1/extract answers it statelessly for a .ocanvas or Markdown body. Hosts may implement GET /search ( [host.search] callback = true ); GET /api/v1/search and the MCP tool canvas_search proxy it for user tokens only, 10 a minute per user, dropping files the host's /access refuses. OpenCanvas keeps no index and caches no result. The sample host indexes search.json and serves the callback and a search page. Added Portable live blocks, server side (v0.3, behind [host.flags] live_blocks , off by default): the host contract (LIVE-01, docs/05 §2c, ADR-070): [host.live] checked at start-up, the POST /files callback, /access required (with optional name and callbackToken ), the token's perms.live and live claims, derived sessions for embedded live files ( POST /v1/live/session ) and "Make live" ( POST /v1/live/make ). Added Live block projections, snapshots, exports and render (LIVE-04/05/06, ADR-072): GET /v1/live/projection with ETags, POST /v1/live/refresh under the snapshot policy, exports that inline only what the exporting person can read, and API operations makeLive , listReferences and renderFile ( GET /api/v1/files/{id}/render ) in the OpenAPI document, both clients and the conformance suite.

## 0.2.1 (2026-11-26)

Fixed A newly inserted SDK block takes focus when its frame is ready only while it is still selected.

## 0.2.0 (2026-11-25)

Added Headless API is the supported contract. /api/v1 with OpenAPI 3.1, RFC 9457 errors, scoped user tokens shared with MCP, Idempotency-Key , signed cursors, rate limits, the events stream and the sync token. Most of it shipped in 0.1.2 behind [host.flags] api_v1 . Added Webhooks for the events-stream events (WH-01): [host.webhooks] , signed deliveries ( X-OpenCanvas-Signature v2, Idempotency-Key = event id) from a durable outbox (migration 0009_webhook_outbox ), retries with backoff, each sent once per cluster, same origin as callback_base only. Added Clients: TypeScript @opencanvas/client and Rust opencanvas-client , generated from the OpenAPI document, with retries, idempotency keys, paging, events resume and webhook verification. They share a conformance suite (HAPI-06, HAPI-07). Added MCP canvas tools are adapters over the API operations, with one scope check, limiter and idempotency store, and a parity contract test (HAPI-08). New operation: POST /api/v1/files/{id}/boards . Added Block SDK (data side): - block.json manifests installed by the operator ( OC_BLOCKS_DIR , sha384 integrity, OC_BLOCKS_ORIGIN ) and enabled per host with [host.blocks] ; - JSON Schema validation of attrs and data on every write path; - one generic extBlock node and an ext root; - declarative export templates and fallbacks; - data versions with declarative migrations (BSDK-01, -02, -05). Added API reference on the website ( /api/ ): guides for authentication, errors, pagination, idempotency, rate limits, events, webhooks and the SDKs, and one page per resource generated from the OpenAPI document, with samples in curl, TypeScript, Rust and Python. Added tools/check-openapi.py : every API operation is documented with examples and its error codes. Changed An editor older than 0.2 that would delete an SDK block is closed with 4426 ("editor out of date: reopen the canvas"). Changed A webhook sweep claims at most 40 deliveries, and the next sweep starts at once (SEC-48). Security SEC-46: room updates over the WebSocket are checked against installed SDK block schemas, as API and MCP writes are. A broken block could otherwise make the file unopenable. Security SEC-51: a restore's undo cannot be reached with a crafted restoreId by a user whose id is a suffix of the restorer's.

## 0.1.2 (2026-11-24)

Added Version history with named versions, preview and comparison, restore and temporary undo where supported by the host. Added Headless API under /api/v1 with OpenAPI 3.1, scoped tokens, and idempotency keys on file writes. Added API events stream (SSE and WebSocket) with resume, and a headless sync token. Fixed A Jitsi role change takes precedence over launch tokens issued before the change.

## 0.1.1 (2026-11-23)

Added Jitsi Meet ( integrations/jitsi/ , JIT-02): mod_opencanvas.lua gives every meeting a shared canvas in Jitsi's Shared document slot, like Etherpad. One Prosody plugin plus .env lines, no Docker image or compose changes. Per-person launch tokens, a fresh token on reload, the meeting end closes the canvas. Tested end to end against a stock docker-jitsi-meet (stable-11509-1) with two browsers; guide in integrations/jitsi/README.md . Added Temporary canvases ( storage = "ephemeral" , ADR-043, JIT-01) for hosts with no file storage: no load or save callbacks; everything is deleted when the room closes (idle grace or DELETE /v1/files/{id}/session ). A server restart or deploy keeps the canvas for the reconnect. Fixed Plugin: tokens signed with Jitsi's luajwtjitsi did not verify (non-standard signature encoding); the plugin now signs with Prosody's own HMAC. Jitsi appends its Etherpad options with ? , which broke the token; the launch URL now ends in &ep= .

## 0.1.0 (2026-11-23)

Added Block schema validation (MOD-01) in oc-model on .ocanvas read, REST patch, import and MCP writes, with JSON-pointer paths; unknown nodes are warnings, kept and counted in oc_schema_warnings_total . Security MCP audience (SEC-33): the MCP token audience comes from [host.ai] mcp_audience or OC_PUBLIC_URL , never from the request's Host header. Without either, MCP is off ( 404 ) and the server logs one start-up warning. Security MCP file scope (SEC-34): when the host has no /access callback, an MCP token must name its files in a files claim; a token without one is refused ( FILES_REQUIRED ). The broad behaviour (one token's role on every file) needs [host.ai] mcp_all_files = true .

## 0.1.0-alpha.1 (2026-11-23)

Added Host integration: HS256, RS256, EdDSA and JWKS launch tokens; signed callbacks; the live role API; host members and revocation; the <open-canvas> embed SDK and postMessage API; access expiry warning and quiet renewal (ADR-036). Added WOPI client mode: discovery, CheckFileInfo, GetFile, PutFile, PUT_RELATIVE conflict copies, assets and mentions, and a reference WOPI host. Added AI assistant and MCP endpoint (experimental, disabled by default): server-side model providers (Claude Platform, OpenAI-compatible servers), plan → approve → act → review → undo runs, suggestions, limits, quotas and audit; MCP at POST /mcp/{hostId} with host-issued tokens (ADR-031 to ADR-035). Fixed Saves kept using a revoked editor's token after a role change (docs/23 PERM-05). Security Callback and outbox tokens sealed at rest with AES-256-GCM under OC_KEK ; the server refuses to start without OC_KEK outside development. Last changed 2026-11-28 .


# API reference: Canvas

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/reference/canvas.html

Read a whole canvas as JSON blocks, Markdown or a heading outline.

## Read a canvas as JSON blocks, Markdown or an outline

GET /api/v1/files/{fileId} (operationId readFile, scope canvas:read)

The canvas as JSON blocks (default), Markdown or a heading outline. Every block carries its `blockId` and a `rev` hash; the document `rev` comes back as `ETag`. Pass a block's `rev` as `ifMatch`, or the document's as `If-Match`, when you change it.

If nobody has the file open, OpenCanvas loads it from your load callback first.

Parameters:
- fileId (path, string, required): The host's file id
- format (query, string): json (default), markdown or outline

Response 200 (application/json), example:
{
  "blocks": [
    {
      "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtz1wkrv27pzmqk64r",
      "node": {
        "attrs": {
          "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtz1wkrv27pzmqk64r",
          "level": 2
        },
        "content": [
          {
            "text": "Launch plan",
            "type": "text"
          }
        ],
        "type": "heading"
      },
      "rev": "689ac3d33e18"
    },
    {
      "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk",
      "node": {
        "attrs": {
          "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk"
        },
        "content": [
          {
            "text": "Ship on Friday.",
            "type": "text"
          }
        ],
        "type": "paragraph"
      },
      "rev": "5641be1fd2cb"
    },
    {
      "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtngbs1n2p5aypa4mz",
      "node": {
        "attrs": {
          "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtngbs1n2p5aypa4mz"
        },
        "content": [
          {
            "attrs": {
              "checked": false
            },
            "content": [
              {
                "content": [
                  {
                    "text": "Write the release notes",
                    "type": "text"
                  }
                ],
                "type": "paragraph"
              }
            ],
            "type": "taskItem"
          }
        ],
        "type": "taskList"
      },
      "rev": "92c98e698f58"
    }
  ],
  "rev": "fc3a67f52c7b",
  "title": null,
  "truncated": false
}

Errors: API_OFF (404), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), TOKEN_INVALID (401), TOKEN_EXPIRED (401), SCOPE_REQUIRED (403), ROLE_FORBIDDEN (403), FILES_REQUIRED (403), RATE_LIMITED (429), UNAVAILABLE (503), INTERNAL (500), BAD_INPUT (400), HOST_UNAVAILABLE (502)

Example:
curl -s "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1?format=json" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY"


# API reference: Blocks

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/reference/blocks.html

List, read and find blocks, and change them in one atomic batch.

## List top-level blocks

GET /api/v1/files/{fileId}/blocks (operationId listBlocks, scope canvas:read)

Top-level blocks in document order, a page at a time. Each page answers `has_more` and `next_cursor` (and a `Link` header when more follow); pass the cursor back unchanged. Cursors are signed Yjs positions: paging survives concurrent edits, and every block that exists for the whole walk comes back exactly once.

Parameters:
- fileId (path, string, required): The host's file id
- limit (query, integer): 1-100, default 100
- cursor (query, string): Opaque, signed cursor from next_cursor (bound to this file and query, valid 1 h)

Response 200 (application/json), example:
{
  "blocks": [
    {
      "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtz1wkrv27pzmqk64r",
      "node": {
        "attrs": {
          "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtz1wkrv27pzmqk64r",
          "level": 2
        },
        "content": [
          {
            "text": "Launch plan",
            "type": "text"
          }
        ],
        "type": "heading"
      },
      "rev": "689ac3d33e18"
    },
    {
      "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk",
      "node": {
        "attrs": {
          "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk"
        },
        "content": [
          {
            "text": "Ship on Friday.",
            "type": "text"
          }
        ],
        "type": "paragraph"
      },
      "rev": "5641be1fd2cb"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "eyJmIjoiZG9jXzEiLCJpIjoiQU1XcW5aRHpfZThKRDBFIiwiayI6ImJsb2NrcyIsInEiOiJlM2IwYzQ0Mjk4ZmMxYzE0OWFmYmY0YzgiLCJ4IjoxODAwMDAzNjAwfQ.pdHAPcfzMM5tjJk54UBrTS9TIqKP3xtJR9yZRY1bPv4",
  "rev": "fc3a67f52c7b"
}

Errors: API_OFF (404), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), TOKEN_INVALID (401), TOKEN_EXPIRED (401), SCOPE_REQUIRED (403), ROLE_FORBIDDEN (403), FILES_REQUIRED (403), RATE_LIMITED (429), UNAVAILABLE (503), INTERNAL (500), CURSOR_INVALID (400), CURSOR_EXPIRED (410)

Example:
curl -s "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/blocks?limit=2" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY"

## Read one block (also nested ones)

GET /api/v1/files/{fileId}/blocks/{blockId} (operationId getBlock, scope canvas:read)

One block by its `blockId`, top-level or nested (a paragraph in a column, a task in a list). The block's `rev` comes back as `ETag`.

Parameters:
- fileId (path, string, required): The host's file id
- blockId (path, string, required): The block's blockId attribute

Response 200 (application/json), example:
{
  "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk",
  "node": {
    "attrs": {
      "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk"
    },
    "content": [
      {
        "text": "Ship on Friday.",
        "type": "text"
      }
    ],
    "type": "paragraph"
  },
  "rev": "5641be1fd2cb"
}

Errors: API_OFF (404), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), TOKEN_INVALID (401), TOKEN_EXPIRED (401), SCOPE_REQUIRED (403), ROLE_FORBIDDEN (403), FILES_REQUIRED (403), RATE_LIMITED (429), UNAVAILABLE (503), INTERNAL (500), BLOCK_NOT_FOUND (404)

Example:
curl -s "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/blocks/b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY"

## Find blocks whose text contains q (case-insensitive)

GET /api/v1/files/{fileId}/blocks:find (operationId findBlocks, scope canvas:read)

Blocks whose text contains `q`, case-insensitively, in document order, with an excerpt and the block's position (`path`, indexes from the top). `types` keeps only those block types (`paragraph`, `heading`, `taskList`, ...).

Parameters:
- fileId (path, string, required): The host's file id
- q (query, string): Text to find
- types (query, string): Comma-separated block types
- limit (query, integer): 1-100

Response 200 (application/json), example:
{
  "matches": [
    {
      "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk",
      "excerpt": "Ship on Friday.",
      "path": "1",
      "rev": "5641be1fd2cb",
      "type": "paragraph"
    }
  ]
}

Errors: API_OFF (404), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), TOKEN_INVALID (401), TOKEN_EXPIRED (401), SCOPE_REQUIRED (403), ROLE_FORBIDDEN (403), FILES_REQUIRED (403), RATE_LIMITED (429), UNAVAILABLE (503), INTERNAL (500), BAD_INPUT (400)

Example:
curl -s "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/blocks:find?q=friday" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY"

## Change blocks in one atomic transaction

POST /api/v1/files/{fileId}/blocks:batch (operationId batchBlocks, scope canvas:write)

Change blocks in one Yjs transaction: all ops apply, or none. Ops: `append` and `insertAfter` (with `markdown` or Tiptap `blocks`), `replace`, `delete`, and `editText` (`textEdits: [{find, replace}]`). An op with `ifMatch` whose block changed since you read it answers `412 STALE_BLOCK` with the fresh block, and the `If-Match` header does the same for the whole document. Deleting more than 5 blocks needs `"confirm": true`.

New content lands directly. Changes to existing blocks land directly too, unless the call sends `"mode": "suggest"` or the host sets `[host.api] default_mode = "suggest"`: then they become a suggestion (`suggestionId`) for a person to accept. The answer's `rev` is the new document revision (also the `ETag`).

Parameters:
- fileId (path, string, required): The host's file id
- If-Match (header, string): The document rev (ETag) the batch expects; a mismatch answers 412 STALE_BLOCK.
- Idempotency-Key (header, string): 1-255 visible ASCII characters, scoped to the caller. A repeat of the same request within 24 h answers the stored result (Idempotency-Replayed: true); another request with the same key is 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a duplicate while the first runs is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS. Failed requests are not stored.

Request body (application/json), example:
{
  "ops": [
    {
      "op": "append",
      "markdown": "## Decisions\n\nShip on Friday."
    },
    {
      "op": "editText",
      "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk",
      "ifMatch": "5641be1fd2cb",
      "textEdits": [
        {
          "find": "Friday",
          "replace": "Monday"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Response 200 (application/json), example:
{
  "applied": 2,
  "blockIds": [
    "b_01m87jv4s4hw2f9n0k3q6t8y1v",
    "b_01m87jv4s4p7d2m5c8x0z3r6tb",
    "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk"
  ],
  "mode": "direct",
  "rev": "27ae51518968",
  "stale": []
}

Errors: API_OFF (404), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), TOKEN_INVALID (401), TOKEN_EXPIRED (401), SCOPE_REQUIRED (403), ROLE_FORBIDDEN (403), FILES_REQUIRED (403), RATE_LIMITED (429), UNAVAILABLE (503), INTERNAL (500), IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID (400), IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED (422), IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS (409), BODY_TOO_LARGE (413), BAD_INPUT (400), BLOCK_NOT_FOUND (404), STALE_BLOCK (412), CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED (409), HOST_UNAVAILABLE (502)

Example:
curl -s -X POST "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/blocks:batch" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY" \
  -H 'If-Match: "fc3a67f52c7b"' \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "ops": [
      {
        "op": "append",
        "markdown": "## Decisions\n\nShip on Friday."
      },
      {
        "op": "editText",
        "blockId": "b_01m87jv4rtkdxymn93jwtx35sk",
        "ifMatch": "5641be1fd2cb",
        "textEdits": [
          {
            "find": "Friday",
            "replace": "Monday"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'

## Make blocks live

POST /api/v1/files/{fileId}/live (operationId makeLive, scope canvas:write)

"Make live" (LIVE-01, docs/27 §2.2): OpenCanvas asks your `POST {callback_base}/files` to create the live file (with the `X-OpenCanvas-Callback-Token` you send), writes the blocks into it as one edit with `meta.kind = "live"`, saves it through the normal commit path, and replaces them in this canvas with one `liveBlock` node, one edit. Needs `[host.flags] live_blocks`. The blocks must be top-level; SDK blocks and blocks that hold live blocks cannot move. Databases and boards the blocks show move with them.

Parameters:
- fileId (path, string, required): The host's file id
- Idempotency-Key (header, string): 1-255 visible ASCII characters, scoped to the caller. A repeat of the same request within 24 h answers the stored result (Idempotency-Replayed: true); another request with the same key is 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a duplicate while the first runs is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS. Failed requests are not stored.

Request body (application/json), example:
{
  "blockIds": [
    "b_01j9k2m3n4"
  ],
  "name": "Q1 OKRs"
}

Response 201 (application/json), example:
{
  "liveFileId": "f_8812",
  "blockId": "b_01j9k2m3n5",
  "kind": "blocks"
}

Errors: API_OFF (404), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), TOKEN_INVALID (401), TOKEN_EXPIRED (401), SCOPE_REQUIRED (403), ROLE_FORBIDDEN (403), FILES_REQUIRED (403), RATE_LIMITED (429), UNAVAILABLE (503), INTERNAL (500), BAD_INPUT (400), BLOCK_NOT_FOUND (404), LIVE_OFF (404), LIVE_DEPTH (403), LIVE_CREATE_UNSUPPORTED (501), HOST_UNAVAILABLE (502), IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID (400), IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED (422), IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS (409)

Example:
curl -s -X POST "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/live" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"blockIds": ["b_01j9k2m3n4"], "name": "Q1 OKRs"}'

## List the live blocks and block references

GET /api/v1/files/{fileId}/references (operationId listReferences, scope canvas:read)

The `liveBlock` and `blockRef` nodes in this canvas (LIVE-01, docs/27 §2.4) with the caller's access to each source, from your `POST /access` answers (cached 30 s). "Where is this live block used" is yours to answer: OpenCanvas keeps no usage index, and tells you with the `live.embedded` and `live.removed` events instead.

Parameters:
- fileId (path, string, required): The host's file id

Response 200 (application/json), example:
{
  "items": [
    {
      "blockId": "b_01j9k2m3n5",
      "type": "liveBlock",
      "fileId": "f_8812",
      "kind": "blocks",
      "access": "edit"
    }
  ]
}

Errors: API_OFF (404), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), TOKEN_INVALID (401), TOKEN_EXPIRED (401), SCOPE_REQUIRED (403), ROLE_FORBIDDEN (403), FILES_REQUIRED (403), RATE_LIMITED (429), UNAVAILABLE (503), INTERNAL (500)

Example:
curl -s "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/references" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY"


# API reference: Databases

URL: https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/reference/databases.html

Describe databases, query rows with filters and sorts, create databases and fields, and create or update rows.

## List databases with fields, row counts and views

GET /api/v1/files/{fileId}/databases (operationId listDatabases, scope canvas:read)

Every database block in the canvas: its fields (id, name, type, options), row count and views.

Parameters:
- fileId (path, string, required): The host's file id

Response 200 (application/json), example:
{
  "databases": [
    {
      "dbId": "db_01m87jv4sc2twxjhzzxzh7mene",
      "fields": [
        {
          "description": null,
          "id": "f_01m87jv4scpzrpdkt85ph5kftr",
          "name": "Task",
          "options": [],
          "type": "title"
        },
        {
          "description": null,
          "id": "f_01m87jv4schbq8mwrxbq9m31wr",
          "name": "Status",
          "options": [
            {
              "c": "gray",
              "v": "Todo"
            },
            {
              "c": "gray",
              "v": "Doing"
            },
            {
              "c": "gray",
              "v": "Done"
            }
          ],
          "type": "select"
        },
        {
          "description": null,
          "id": "f_01m87jv4scmq5tffb8z3jfphjv",
          "name": "Due",
          "options": [],
          "type": "date"
        }
      ],
      "name": "Tasks",
      "rowCount": 1,
      "views": []
    }
  ]
}

Errors: API_OFF (404), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), TOKEN_INVALID (401), TOKEN_EXPIRED (401), SCOPE_REQUIRED (403), ROLE_FORBIDDEN (403), FILES_REQUIRED (403), RATE_LIMITED (429), UNAVAILABLE (503), INTERNAL (500)

Example:
curl -s "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/databases" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY"

## Create a database block

POST /api/v1/files/{fileId}/databases (operationId createDatabase, scope canvas:write)

Add a database block, after `afterBlockId` or at the end, with its fields and optional first rows. Field types: `title`, `text`, `status`, `select`, `tags`, `person`, `date`, `number`, `checkbox`, `url`, `progress`; `options` lists the choices of `select`, `status` and `tags`. Rows are `{values: {<field name or id>: value}}`.

Parameters:
- fileId (path, string, required): The host's file id
- Idempotency-Key (header, string): 1-255 visible ASCII characters, scoped to the caller. A repeat of the same request within 24 h answers the stored result (Idempotency-Replayed: true); another request with the same key is 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a duplicate while the first runs is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS. Failed requests are not stored.

Request body (application/json), example:
{
  "name": "Tasks",
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "Task",
      "type": "title"
    },
    {
      "name": "Status",
      "type": "select",
      "options": [
        "Todo",
        "Doing",
        "Done"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "Due",
      "type": "date"
    }
  ],
  "rows": [
    {
      "values": {
        "Task": "Write the release notes",
        "Status": "Doing",
        "Due": "2026-11-27"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Response 200 (application/json), example:
{
  "blockId": "b_01m87jv4sc1ya7yxpfn918vty9",
  "dbId": "db_01m87jv4sc2twxjhzzxzh7mene",
  "fieldIds": [
    "f_01m87jv4scpzrpdkt85ph5kftr",
    "f_01m87jv4schbq8mwrxbq9m31wr",
    "f_01m87jv4scmq5tffb8z3jfphjv"
  ],
  "rowIds": [
    "r_01m87jv4scp2q5qt8k4r4mchy8"
  ]
}

Errors: API_OFF (404), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), TOKEN_INVALID (401), TOKEN_EXPIRED (401), SCOPE_REQUIRED (403), ROLE_FORBIDDEN (403), FILES_REQUIRED (403), RATE_LIMITED (429), UNAVAILABLE (503), INTERNAL (500), IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID (400), IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED (422), IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS (409), BODY_TOO_LARGE (413), BAD_INPUT (400), BLOCK_NOT_FOUND (404), HOST_UNAVAILABLE (502)

Example:
curl -s -X POST "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/databases" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Tasks",
    "fields": [
      {
        "name": "Task",
        "type": "title"
      },
      {
        "name": "Status",
        "type": "select",
        "options": [
          "Todo",
          "Doing",
          "Done"
        ]
      },
      {
        "name": "Due",
        "type": "date"
      }
    ],
    "rows": [
      {
        "values": {
          "Task": "Write the release notes",
          "Status": "Doing",
          "Due": "2026-11-27"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'

## Describe one database

GET /api/v1/files/{fileId}/databases/{dbId} (operationId getDatabase, scope canvas:read)

One database: its fields, row count and views. Use the field ids (or names) in `queryRows` and `rows:upsert`.

Parameters:
- fileId (path, string, required): The host's file id
- dbId (path, string, required): Database id

Response 200 (application/json), example:
{
  "dbId": "db_01m87jv4sc2twxjhzzxzh7mene",
  "fields": [
    {
      "description": null,
      "id": "f_01m87jv4scpzrpdkt85ph5kftr",
      "name": "Task",
      "options": [],
      "type": "title"
    },
    {
      "description": null,
      "id": "f_01m87jv4schbq8mwrxbq9m31wr",
      "name": "Status",
      "options": [
        {
          "c": "gray",
          "v": "Todo"
        },
        {
          "c": "gray",
          "v": "Doing"
        },
        {
          "c": "gray",
          "v": "Done"
        }
      ],
      "type": "select"
    },
    {
      "description": null,
      "id": "f_01m87jv4scmq5tffb8z3jfphjv",
      "name": "Due",
      "options": [],
      "type": "date"
    }
  ],
  "name": "Tasks",
  "rowCount": 1,
  "views": []
}

Errors: API_OFF (404), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), TOKEN_INVALID (401), TOKEN_EXPIRED (401), SCOPE_REQUIRED (403), ROLE_FORBIDDEN (403), FILES_REQUIRED (403), RATE_LIMITED (429), UNAVAILABLE (503), INTERNAL (500), NOT_FOUND (404), DB_NOT_FOUND (404)

Example:
curl -s "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/databases/db_01m87jv4sc2twxjhzzxzh7mene" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY"

## Query rows

GET /api/v1/files/{fileId}/databases/{dbId}/rows (operationId queryRows, scope canvas:read)

Rows of a database, filtered, sorted and paged. `filter` is a JSON array of `{f, op, v}` (`op`: `eq`, `ne`, `contains`, `gt`, `lt`, `ge`, `le`, `empty`, `notEmpty`), `sort` a JSON array of `{f, dir}` (`asc`, `desc`), `fields` the fields to return; fields by id or name. Values come back keyed by field id. Pages of at most 200 rows, with a cursor bound to this database, filter, sort and fields.

Parameters:
- fileId (path, string, required): The host's file id
- dbId (path, string, required): Database id
- filter (query, string): JSON array [{f, op, v}]
- sort (query, string): JSON array [{f, dir}]
- fields (query, string): Comma-separated field ids or names
- limit (query, integer): 1-200
- cursor (query, string): Opaque, signed cursor from next_cursor (bound to this database, filter, sort and fields, valid 1 h)

Response 200 (application/json), example:
{
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "eyJmIjoiZG9jXzEiLCJpIjp7ImFmdGVyIjoicl8wMW04N2p2NHNjcDJxNXF0OGs0cjRtY2h5OCIsIm8iOiIxIn0sImsiOiJyb3dzIiwicSI6IjI4MGMzOGFjNTM4NTYyN2FmMWFhZGE5ZiIsIngiOjE4MDAwMDM2MDB9.ZAFcDhTGnqZklHMuAINEeogPeSpmm29T1AbRmxg-rRU",
  "rows": [
    {
      "rowId": "r_01m87jv4scp2q5qt8k4r4mchy8",
      "values": {
        "f_01m87jv4schbq8mwrxbq9m31wr": "Doing",
        "f_01m87jv4scmq5tffb8z3jfphjv": "2026-11-27",
        "f_01m87jv4scpzrpdkt85ph5kftr": "Write the release notes"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Errors: API_OFF (404), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), TOKEN_INVALID (401), TOKEN_EXPIRED (401), SCOPE_REQUIRED (403), ROLE_FORBIDDEN (403), FILES_REQUIRED (403), RATE_LIMITED (429), UNAVAILABLE (503), INTERNAL (500), BAD_INPUT (400), NOT_FOUND (404), CURSOR_INVALID (400), CURSOR_EXPIRED (410)

Example:
curl -s -G "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/databases/db_01m87jv4sc2twxjhzzxzh7mene/rows" \
  --data-urlencode 'filter=[{"f": "Status", "op": "ne", "v": "Done"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'sort=[{"f": "Due", "dir": "asc"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'limit=1' \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY"

## Create or update rows (at most 200)

POST /api/v1/files/{fileId}/databases/{dbId}/rows:upsert (operationId upsertRows, scope canvas:write)

Create or update up to 200 rows in one transaction. `values` maps field names or ids to values; a row with an existing `rowId` is updated, any other row is created.

Parameters:
- fileId (path, string, required): The host's file id
- dbId (path, string, required): Database id
- Idempotency-Key (header, string): 1-255 visible ASCII characters, scoped to the caller. A repeat of the same request within 24 h answers the stored result (Idempotency-Replayed: true); another request with the same key is 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a duplicate while the first runs is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS. Failed requests are not stored.

Request body (application/json), example:
{
  "rows": [
    {
      "values": {
        "Task": "Tag the release",
        "Status": "Todo",
        "Due": "2026-11-28"
      }
    },
    {
      "rowId": "r_01m87jv4scp2q5qt8k4r4mchy8",
      "values": {
        "Status": "Done"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Response 200 (application/json), example:
{
  "created": 1,
  "rowIds": [
    "r_01m87jv4sg668wqdmpx9n1frsj",
    "r_01m87jv4scp2q5qt8k4r4mchy8"
  ],
  "updated": 1
}

Errors: API_OFF (404), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), TOKEN_INVALID (401), TOKEN_EXPIRED (401), SCOPE_REQUIRED (403), ROLE_FORBIDDEN (403), FILES_REQUIRED (403), RATE_LIMITED (429), UNAVAILABLE (503), INTERNAL (500), IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID (400), IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED (422), IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS (409), BODY_TOO_LARGE (413), BAD_INPUT (400), NOT_FOUND (404), HOST_UNAVAILABLE (502)

Example:
curl -s -X POST "https://canvas.example.com/api/v1/files/doc_1/databases/db_01m87jv4sc2twxjhzzxzh7mene/rows:upsert" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Host: acme" \
  -H "X-OpenCanvas-Key: $OC_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "rows": [
      {
        "values": {
          "Task": "Tag the release",
          "Status": "Todo",
          "Due": "2026-11-28"
        }
      },
      {
        "rowId": "r_01m87jv4scp2q5qt8k4r4mchy8",
        "values": {
          "Status": "Done"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'

## Add a field

POST /api/v1/files/{fileId}/databases/{dbId}/fields (operationId addField, scope canvas:write)

Add a field to a database. `type` as in `createDatabase`; `options` for `select`, `status` and `tags`.

Parameters:
- fileId (path, string, required): The host's file id
- dbId (path, string, required): Database id
- Idempotency-Key (header, string): 1-255 visible ASCII characters, scoped to the caller. A repeat of the same request within 24 h answers the stored result (Idempotency-Replayed: true); another request with the same key is 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; a duplicate while the first runs is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS. Failed requests are not stored.

Request body (application/json), example:
{
  "name": "Owner",
  "type": "person"
}

Response 200 (application/json), example:
{
  "fieldId": "f_01m87jv4shsxrhbw3cyfhpgz91"
}

Errors: API_OFF (404), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), TOKEN_INVALID (401), TOKEN_EXPIRED (401), SCOPE_REQUIRED (403), ROLE_FORBIDDEN (403), FILES_REQUIRED (403), RATE_LIMITED (429), UNAVAILABLE (503), INTERNAL (500), IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID (400), IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED (422), IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS (409), BODY_TOO_LARGE (413), BAD_INPUT (400), NOT_FOUND (404), HOST_UNAVAILABLE (502)

Example:
